title.raw: 卷八十六 列傳第五十六 張軌 Volume 86 Biographies 56: Zhang Gui

sentences.zh: 張軌

translations.literal: Zhang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: The subject of this biography is Zhang Gui.

sentences.zh: 張軌，字士彥，安定烏氏人，漢常山景王耳十七代孫也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, courtesy name Shiyan, was a native of Wushi in Anding commandery, the seventeenth-generation descendant of Liu Er, the Prince Jing of Changshan of the Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, whose courtesy name was Shiyan, came from Wushi in Anding; he traced his line to Liu Er, the Han Prince Jing of Changshan, seventeen generations back.

sentences.zh: 家世孝廉，以儒學顯。

translations.literal: For generations his family had produced men recommended as xiaolian, and they were eminent in Confucian scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had long supplied xiaolian candidates and was known for Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 父溫，為太官令。

translations.literal: His father, Zhang Wen, served as Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Wen held the post of Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 軌少明敏好學，有器望，姿儀典則，與同郡皇甫謐善，隱于宜陽女幾山。

translations.literal: In youth Gui was quick, perceptive, and fond of learning; he had presence and high repute, and his bearing was dignified and correct. He was on good terms with Huangfu Mi of the same commandery and lived in seclusion on Mount Nüji in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was bright, eager to learn, and carried an air of capacity; his deportment was exemplary. He befriended Huangfu Mi of Anding and withdrew to Mount Nüji in Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，受叔父錫官五品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taishi era he received from his uncle Xi an office of the fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi reign he was given fifth-rank office through his uncle Zhang Xi.

sentences.zh: 中書監張華與軌論經義及政事損益，甚器之，謂安定中正為蔽善抑才，乃美為之談，以為二品之精。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhang Hua discussed with him the meaning of the Classics and the gains and losses of government affairs, thought very highly of him, and said that the commandery impartial judge of Anding was concealing the worthy and suppressing talent; he therefore spoke well of him, deeming him the finest among those rated in the second grade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua, the Palace Library director, debated classical doctrine and policy with him and came to esteem him deeply, blaming Anding’s impartial judge for hiding talent and praising Zhang Gui as the outstanding man of the second-grade roster.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍楊珧辟為掾，除太子舍人，累遷散騎常侍、征西軍司。

translations.literal: General of the Guards Yang Yao summoned him as a clerk; he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Heir Apparent’s Household, then rose in stages to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Army Supervisor on the Western Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao, General of the Guards, took him on as a clerk; he was made a gentleman attendant at the heir’s household and eventually promoted through posts to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and western-expedition army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 軌以時方多難，陰圖據河西，筮之，遇《泰》之《觀》，乃投策喜曰：「霸者兆也。

translations.literal: Because the times were full of troubles, he secretly planned to occupy the region west of the Yellow River. He cast the milfoil and obtained Hexagram Tai changing to Guan; he threw down the stalks and said in joy, ‘This is an omen for a hegemon.’
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the realm in turmoil, he quietly set his sights on the Hexi region. When he divined with the Changes and drew Tai turning into Guan, he cast the stalks aside and exclaimed that the lines foretold a hegemon’s rise.

sentences.zh: 」於是求為涼州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought appointment as governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore petitioned to be posted as Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 公卿亦舉軌才堪禦遠。

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers also recommended Gui as a man whose talents fitted him to guard a distant frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Court grandees likewise urged that he was the man to hold the far west.

sentences.zh: 永甯初，出為護羌校尉、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongning era he went out as Colonel Who Protects the Qiang and Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first years of Yongning he left the capital as Colonel Who Protects the Qiang and as inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 于時鮮卑反叛，寇盜從橫，軌到官，即討破之，斬首萬餘級，遂威著西州，化行河右。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianbei rebelled, and bandits ran rampant in every direction. As soon as he reached his post he attacked and defeated them, beheading more than ten thousand, so that his awe spread through the western provinces and his transforming influence reached the right bank of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei had risen in revolt and raiders swarmed the region; on taking office he struck them down at once, taking over ten thousand heads, until his name carried weight across the west and his rule extended east of the river.

sentences.zh: 以宋配、陰充、氾瑗、陰澹為股肱謀主，征九郡胄子五百人，立學校，始置崇文祭酒，位視別駕，春秋行鄉射之禮。

translations.literal: He took Song Pei, Yin Chong, Fan Yuan, and Yin Dan as his chief arms and strategists, conscripted five hundred sons of gentry from the nine commanderies, established schools, and for the first time appointed a Libationer for Exalting Culture, with rank equal to a chief clerk; in spring and autumn he held the village archery ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Song Pei, Yin Chong, Fan Yuan, and Yin Dan became his principal advisers; he drafted five hundred young nobles from nine commanderies, set up schools, created the post of Libationer for Exalting Culture on a par with chief clerk, and observed the archery rites in spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 秘書監繆世征、少府摯虞夜觀星象，相與言曰：「天下方亂，避難之國唯涼土耳。

translations.literal: The Palace Library Supervisor Miao Shizheng and the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Zhi Yu watched the stars by night and said to each other, ‘The realm is about to fall into chaos; the only land to flee to is Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Palace librarian Miao Shizheng and chamberlain Zhi Yu, studying the stars at night, agreed that with chaos coming, Liangzhou alone would offer refuge.

sentences.zh: 張涼州德量不恆，殆其人乎！

translations.literal: Inspector Zhang’s virtue and capacity are not ordinary—perhaps he is the man!’
translations.idiomatic: They said Inspector Zhang’s moral stature was anything but common and wondered whether he might be the leader fate had chosen.

sentences.zh: 」及河間、成都二王之難，遣兵三千，東赴京師。

translations.literal: When the troubles of the Princes of Hejian and Chengdu broke out, he sent three thousand troops east to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When civil war erupted between the princes of Hejian and Chengdu, he dispatched three thousand soldiers toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 初，漢末金城人陽成遠殺太守以叛，郡人馮忠赴屍號哭，嘔血而死。

translations.literal: In the beginning, at the end of the Han, a man of Jincheng commandery named Yang Cheng Yuan killed the grand administrator and rebelled; a man of the commandery, Feng Zhong, went to the corpse and wailed until he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in late Han, Yang Cheng Yuan of Jincheng had murdered the grand administrator and risen in revolt; Feng Zhong of the same commandery threw himself on the body and wept until he coughed blood and died.

sentences.zh: 張掖人吳詠為護羌校尉馬賢所辟，後為太尉龐參掾，參、賢相誣，罪應死，各引詠為證，詠計理無兩直，遂自刎而死。

translations.literal: Wu Yong of Zhangye was summoned by Colonel Who Protects the Qiang Ma Xian and later served as a clerk to Grand Commandant Pang Can; when Can and Xian falsely accused each other, the offense carried death, and each cited Wu Yong as witness. Yong reckoned that the truth could not satisfy both sides, so he cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yong of Zhangye had served Ma Xian and later Pang Can; when the two commanders slandered each other and faced capital charges, each tried to drag Wu Yong into court. Believing no testimony could vindicate both, Wu Yong slit his own throat.

sentences.zh: 參、賢慚悔，自相和釋。

translations.literal: Can and Xian were ashamed and regretful and reconciled with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Can and Ma Xian, stricken with remorse, made peace between themselves.

sentences.zh: 軌皆祭其墓而旌其子孫。

translations.literal: Gui sacrificed at all their tombs and honored their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui offered sacrifices at their graves and ennobled their posterity.

sentences.zh: 永興中，鮮卑若羅拔能皆為寇，軌遣司馬宋配擊之，斬拔能，俘十餘萬口，威名大震。

translations.literal: In the Yongxing era the Xianbei Raluo and Baneng both raided as bandits; Gui sent his Major Song Pei against them. Song Pei beheaded Baneng and captured more than a hundred thousand persons, and Gui’s renown shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxing, when Xianbei leaders Raluo and Baneng pillaged the frontier, he sent Major Song Pei, who slew Baneng and took over a hundred thousand captives, so that his fame resounded far and wide.

sentences.zh: 惠帝遣加安西將軍，封安樂鄉侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: The Emperor Hui sent orders promoting him to General Who Guards the West and enfeoffing him as Marquis of Anle Township with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui added him as General Who Guards the West, enfeoffed him as marquis of Anle township with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 於是大城姑臧。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly enlarged the city of Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: He then undertook a major expansion of Guzang.

sentences.zh: 其城本匈奴所築也，南北七里，東西三里，地有龍形，故名臥龍城。

translations.literal: The city had originally been built by the Xiongnu: seven li from north to south and three li from east to west; the terrain resembled a dragon, so it was called the Recumbent Dragon City.
translations.idiomatic: The walls had been raised by the Xiongnu—seven li north–south, three li east–west—with ground shaped like a crouching dragon, hence the name “Recumbent Dragon.”

sentences.zh: 初，漢末博士敦煌侯瑾謂其門人曰：「後城西泉水當竭，有雙闕起其上，與東門相望。

translations.literal: In the beginning, at the end of the Han, the erudite Hou Jin of Dunhuang said to his disciples, ‘Later the spring west of the city will dry up, and a pair of gate-towers will rise upon it, facing the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the Han scholar Hou Jin of Dunhuang told his students that the western spring would one day fail and twin towers would stand there, aligned with the east gate.

sentences.zh: 中有霸者出焉。

translations.literal: In their midst a hegemon will arise.’
translations.idiomatic: From that place, he said, a hegemon would spring.

sentences.zh: 」至魏嘉平中，郡官果起學館，築雙闕於泉上，與東門正相望矣。

translations.literal: By the Jiaping era of Wei the commandery office indeed built a schoolhouse and raised paired gate-towers on the spring, exactly facing the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei’s Jiaping years officials did build a school and twin towers over the spring, mirroring the east gate as foretold.

sentences.zh: 至是，張氏遂霸河西。

translations.literal: At this point the Zhang clan thereupon dominated the Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: With that omen fulfilled, the Zhang house began its ascendancy west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，會東羌校尉韓稚殺秦州刺史張輔，軌少府司馬楊胤言於軌曰：「今稚逆命，擅殺張輔，明公杖鉞一方，宜懲不恪，此亦《春秋》之義。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongjia era, when Colonel of the Eastern Qiang Han Zhi killed Inspector of Qinzhou Zhang Fu, Yang Yin, Gui’s chief clerk for the lesser treasury, said to Gui, ‘Now Zhi has defied orders and on his own authority killed Zhang Fu. You, sir, hold the axe of command in this quarter and ought to punish such disrespect; this too is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongjia, after Han Zhi of the eastern Qiang slew Qinzhou inspector Zhang Fu, Yang Yin urged Zhang Gui that, as regional commander, he should chastise the killer—exactly the principle the Spring and Autumn teaches.

sentences.zh: 諸侯相滅亡，桓公不能救，則恆公恥之。

translations.literal: When feudal states destroyed one another, if Duke Huan could not save them, Duke Huan was shamed by it.’
translations.idiomatic: When states annihilated one another, Duke Huan of Qi was disgraced if he failed to rescue them—Yang Yin invoked that precedent.

sentences.zh: 」軌從焉，遣中督護氾瑗率眾二萬討之。

translations.literal: Gui followed this advice and sent Central Army Supervisor Fan Yuan with twenty thousand men to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui agreed and sent Central Army Supervisor Fan Yuan at the head of twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 先遺稚書曰：「今天綱紛撓，牧守宜戮力勤王。

translations.literal: He first sent Zhi a letter saying, ‘Now the celestial net is tangled; shepherds and guards ought to join their strength in serving the king.
translations.idiomatic: First he wrote to Han Zhi: “The imperial order is in chaos; every governor should rally to the throne.

sentences.zh: 適得雍州檄，雲卿稱兵內侮，吾董任一方，義在伐叛，武旅三萬，駱驛繼發，伐木之感，心豈可言！

translations.literal: I have just received a dispatch from Yongzhou saying that you have turned your weapons inward against your superiors. I am charged with responsibility for this region; my duty is to crush rebels. Thirty thousand troops are already on the march in continuous columns—the feeling of “felling trees” in the Odes—how can words express it!
translations.idiomatic: I hold a brief from Yongzhou that you have raised arms against lawful authority. I am bound to punish rebellion; thirty thousand soldiers are marching in relays—my heart burns like the poem’s woodcutters, beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 古之行師，全國為上，卿若單馬軍門者，當與卿共平世難也。

translations.literal: In ancient campaigns the best policy was to preserve the enemy state intact. If you come alone on horseback to my camp gate, I shall join you in settling the troubles of the age.’
translations.idiomatic: The ancients prized winning without ruin; if you ride alone to my gate, we can still set the age to rights together.”

sentences.zh: 」稚得書而降。

translations.literal: When Zhi received the letter he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhi capitulated after reading the letter.

sentences.zh: 遣主簿令狐亞聘南陽王模，模甚悅，遺軌以帝所賜劍，謂軌曰：「自隴以西，征伐斷割悉以相委，如此劍矣。

translations.literal: He sent his chief clerk Linghu Ya on a mission to Prince of Nanyang Sima Mo; Mo was greatly pleased, gave Gui the sword the emperor had bestowed, and said to Gui, ‘West of Long, all expeditions and decisions are wholly entrusted to you, as with this sword.’
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched chief clerk Linghu Ya to Prince Sima Mo of Nanyang, who was delighted and presented him with the imperial sword, telling him that west of Long all military authority rested in his hands.

sentences.zh: 」俄而王彌寇洛陽，軌遣北宮純、張纂、馬魴、陰浚等率州軍擊破之，又敗劉聰於河東，京師歌之曰：「涼州大馬，橫行天下。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Mi raided Luoyang; Gui sent Bei Gong Chun, Zhang Zuan, Ma Fang, Yin Jun, and others leading the provincial army to defeat him, and they also defeated Liu Cong east of the Yellow River. The capital sang a song: ‘A great horse from Liangzhou gallops across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi struck Luoyang, Zhang Gui sent Bei Gong Chun, Zhang Zuan, Ma Fang, and Yin Jun with provincial troops to rout him and again defeated Liu Cong in Hedong. The capital took up a rhyme: “The mighty steeds of Liangzhou ride the whole world under heaven.

sentences.zh: 涼州鴟苕，寇賊消；

translations.literal: The shrike-reed of Liangzhou—bandits melt away;
translations.idiomatic: The Liangzhou shrike-reed—raiders vanish in fear;

sentences.zh: 鴟苕翩翩，怖殺人。

translations.literal: The shrike-reed flutters—enough to frighten a man to death.’
translations.idiomatic: The shrike-reed wheels overhead—enough to scare a man to death.”

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其忠，進封西平郡公，不受。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his loyalty, advanced his fief to Duke of Xiping commandery, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored his loyalty by promoting his title to duke of Xiping, an honor he declined.

sentences.zh: 張掖臨松山石有「金馬」字，磨滅粗可識，而「張」字分明，又有文曰：「初祚天下，西方安萬年。

translations.literal: On a stone at Linpine Mountain in Zhangye there were the characters “golden horse,” worn so that they could barely be made out, while the character “Zhang” was clear; there was also an inscription reading, ‘At the first blessing, all under heaven; the west secure for ten thousand years.’
translations.idiomatic: A Zhangye cliff face showed the words “golden horse,” faintly legible, with “Zhang” sharp and clear, and a prophecy that the west would know peace for ages under a new mandate.

sentences.zh: 」姑臧又有玄石，白點成二十八宿。

translations.literal: In Guzang there was also a black stone on which white dots formed the twenty-eight lunar lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Guzang likewise held a dark stone speckled white in the pattern of the twenty-eight mansions.

sentences.zh: 于時天下既亂，所在使命莫有至者，軌遣使貢獻，歲時不替。

translations.literal: By then the realm was already in chaos, and nowhere did imperial messengers arrive; yet Gui sent tribute missions without fail at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: While couriers ceased everywhere else, Zhang Gui never missed the seasonal tribute to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，屢降璽書慰勞。

translations.literal: The court applauded this and repeatedly sent edicts of imperial comfort.
translations.idiomatic: The throne responded with repeated sealed letters of praise and consolation.

sentences.zh: 軌後患風，口不能言，使子茂攝州事。

translations.literal: Later Gui suffered a stroke and could not speak; he had his son Mao take charge of provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui later suffered a paralytic stroke and lost speech, leaving his son Zhang Mao to administer the province.

sentences.zh: 酒泉太守張鎮潛引秦州刺史賈龕以代軌，密使詣京師，請尚書侍郎曹祛為西平太守，圖為輔車之勢。

translations.literal: The grand administrator of Jiuquan, Zhang Zhen, secretly brought in Inspector of Qinzhou Jia Kan to replace Gui, secretly sent someone to the capital to request Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Cao Qu as grand administrator of Xiping, and plotted a paired-wheels alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuquan’s grand administrator Zhang Zhen secretly invited Qinzhou inspector Jia Kan to supplant Zhang Gui, sent agents to Chang’an to have Cao Qu named grand administrator of Xiping, and tried to build a mutual-support pact.

sentences.zh: 軌別駕麹晁欲專威福，又遣使詣長安，告南陽王模，稱軌廢疾，以請賈龕，而龕將受之。

translations.literal: Gui’s chief clerk Qu Chao wished to monopolize authority and profit; he also sent a messenger to Chang’an to inform Prince of Nanyang Sima Mo, claiming that Gui was incapacitated by illness in order to request Jia Kan—and Kan was about to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Qu Chao, hungry for power, wrote to Prince Sima Mo claiming Zhang Gui was bedridden so Jia Kan could take over, and Kan nearly agreed.

sentences.zh: 其兄讓龕曰：「張涼州一時名士，威著西州，汝何德以代之！

translations.literal: Kan’s elder brother remonstrated with Kan, saying, ‘Inspector Zhang is a leading gentleman of the age whose awe fills the western provinces—by what virtue could you replace him!’
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kan’s elder brother warned him: “Zhang Gui is a famous man whose prestige rules the west—what merit could let you step into his shoes?”

sentences.zh: 」龕乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kan desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Kan dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 更以侍中爰瑜為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Instead they appointed Palace Attendant Yuan Yu as Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court then named palace attendant Yuan Yu inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 治中楊澹馳詣長安，割耳盤上，訴軌之被誣，模乃表停之。

translations.literal: The headquarters aide Yang Dan galloped to Chang’an, cut off his ear and placed it on a platter, and complained that Gui had been slandered; Mo thereupon memorialized to halt the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters aide Yang Dan raced to Chang’an, sliced his ear onto a platter to protest the slander, and Sima Mo stayed the replacement.

sentences.zh: 晉昌張越，涼州大族，讖言張氏霸涼，自以才力應之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue of Jinchang, a great clan of Liangzhou, believed a prophecy that the Zhang house would rule Liangzhou and thought his own talents matched it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue of Jinchang, a powerful Liangzhou lineage, read a prophecy that the Zhangs would dominate the west and believed he was the man.

sentences.zh: 從隴西內史遷梁州刺史。

translations.literal: He moved from interior administrator of Longxi to inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He transferred from Longxi interior administrator to Liangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 越志在涼州，遂託病歸河西，陰圖代軌，乃遣兄鎮及曹祛、麹佩移檄廢軌，以軍司杜耽攝州事，使耽表越為刺史。

translations.literal: Yue’s ambition lay in Liangzhou; he therefore feigned illness and returned to the west of the river, secretly plotting to supplant Gui. He sent his elder brother Zhen together with Cao Qu and Qu Pei to circulate a proclamation deposing Gui, had Army Supervisor Du Dan act in provincial affairs, and had Dan memorialize recommending Yue as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His sights were fixed on Liangzhou, so he pretended illness, slipped back to Hexi, and conspired to oust Zhang Gui, circulating a manifesto through his brother Zhang Zhen, Cao Qu, and Qu Pei, installing army supervisor Du Dan and urging the court to name himself inspector.

sentences.zh: 軌令曰：「吾在州八年，不能綏靖區域，又值中州兵亂，秦隴倒懸，加以寢患委篤，實思斂跡避賢。

translations.literal: Gui issued an order saying, ‘I have been in this province eight years yet have been unable to pacify the region; moreover the central plain is torn by soldiers, Qin and Long hang upside down, and my illness grows grave—I truly wish to retire and yield the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui issued a notice: “Eight years in office and I have still not quieted the frontier; the heartland is at war and Longyou reels, while my sickness worsens—I would gladly step aside for someone abler.

sentences.zh: 但負荷任重，未便輒遂。

translations.literal: But the burden on my shoulders is heavy, and I cannot lightly walk away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the charge is too heavy to cast off on a whim.

sentences.zh: 不圖諸人橫興此變，是不明吾心也。

translations.literal: I did not expect you gentlemen suddenly to raise this trouble—you do not understand my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I never thought you would stir such a revolt; you misread my intentions.

sentences.zh: 吾視去貴州如脫屣耳！

translations.literal: I regard leaving your noble province as lightly as kicking off a sandal!’
translations.idiomatic: To me, leaving your fine province would be as easy as kicking off a slipper!”

sentences.zh: 」欲遣主簿尉髦奉表詣闕，便速脂轄，將歸老宜陽。

translations.literal: He wished to send his chief clerk Wei Mao to present a memorial at the palace gates, then quickly grease the axle hubs and retire to old age in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to send chief clerk Wei Mao to the capital with a memorial, then pack his carriage and retire to Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 長史王融、參軍孟暢蹋折鎮檄，排闔諫曰：「晉室多故，人神塗炭，實賴明公撫寧西夏。

translations.literal: The chief clerk Wang Rong and adjutant Meng Chang tore up Zhen’s proclamation, burst through the doors, and remonstrated, saying, ‘The house of Jin faces many crises; gods and men are smeared with ashes; we truly depend on you, sir, to soothe the western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Wang Rong and adjutant Meng Chang shredded Zhang Zhen’s edict, forced their way in, and pleaded: “The Jin court is in crisis; only you can steady the western regions.

sentences.zh: 張鎮兄弟敢肆凶逆，宜聲其罪而戮之，不可成其志也。

translations.literal: The brothers Zhang Zhen dare to commit such violence; you should proclaim their crimes and execute them—you must not let them succeed.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhen’s faction must be denounced and cut down; you cannot let their plot stand.”

sentences.zh: 」軌嘿然。

translations.literal: Gui was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui said nothing.

sentences.zh: 融等出而戒嚴。

translations.literal: After Rong and the others left, they ordered the troops on alert.
translations.idiomatic: When they withdrew, they put the army on full alert.

sentences.zh: 武威太守張琠遣子坦馳詣京，表曰：「魏尚安邊而獲戾，充國盡忠而被譴，皆前史之所譏，今曰之明鑒也。

translations.literal: The grand administrator of Wuwei, Zhang Tian, sent his son Tan posthaste to the capital with a memorial saying, ‘Wei Shang secured the border yet incurred blame; Zhao Chongguo gave his utmost loyalty yet suffered impeachment—both were mocked by earlier histories and are clear mirrors for today.
translations.idiomatic: Wuwei’s grand administrator Zhang Tian rushed his son Tan to court with a petition comparing Zhang Gui to Wei Shang and Zhao Chongguo, loyal border generals unjustly accused.

sentences.zh: 順陽之思劉陶，守闕者千人。

translations.literal: In Shunyang a thousand men thronged the palace gates thinking of Liu Tao.
translations.idiomatic: At Shunyang a thousand people besieged the gates for Liu Tao’s sake.

sentences.zh: 刺史之蒞臣州，若慈母之于赤子，百姓之愛臣軌，若旱苗之得膏雨。

translations.literal: When the inspector came to my province it was like a loving mother toward an infant; the people’s love for your servant Gui is like drought-stricken seedlings meeting timely rain.
translations.idiomatic: Your inspector has been a mother to us; the people cherish Zhang Gui as parched shoots welcome rain.

sentences.zh: 伏聞信惑流言，當有遷代，民情嗷嗷，如失父母。

translations.literal: We have heard that credulous rumors speak of a change of office; the folk wail as if they had lost father and mother.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors of his replacement have left the populace wailing like orphans.

sentences.zh: 今戎夷猾夏，不宜騷動一方。

translations.literal: Now the barbarians are raiding the Xia lands; you ought not to stir up trouble in this region.’
translations.idiomatic: With barbarians ravaging the heartland, the west must not be thrown into turmoil.”

sentences.zh: 」尋以子寔為中督護，率兵討鎮。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he appointed his son Shi as central army supervisor and led troops against Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He then named his son Zhang Shi central army supervisor and marched against Zhang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 遣鎮外甥太府主簿令狐亞前喻鎮曰：「舅何不審安危，明成敗？

translations.literal: He sent Zhen’s nephew, chief clerk of the grand treasury Linghu Ya, ahead to lecture Zhen, saying, ‘Uncle, have you not weighed safety against danger and understood success and failure?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Zhen’s nephew Linghu Ya ahead to ask: “Have you weighed the odds, uncle?

sentences.zh: 主公西河著德，兵馬如雲，此猶烈火已焚，待江漢之水，溺於洪流，望越人之助，其何及哉！

translations.literal: Our lord’s virtue is renowned west of the Yellow River, and his soldiers are like clouds—this is like a fire already blazing while you wait for the waters of the Yangzi and Han, or drowning in a flood while you look for help from the Yue—how could that arrive in time!
translations.idiomatic: His lordship’s fame fills the west and his host is like a cloud—waiting for the Yangzi when the blaze has started is futile.

sentences.zh: 今數萬之軍已臨近境，今唯全老親，存門戶，輸誠歸官，必保萬全之福。

translations.literal: Now several tens of thousands of troops are already at your border; your only course is to preserve your aged kin, save your household, and surrender in good faith to the authorities, and you are sure to win the blessing of perfect safety.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands stand at your gates; save your family by submitting and you will keep fortune whole.

sentences.zh: 」鎮流涕曰：「人誤我也！

translations.literal: Zhen wept and said, ‘Men have misled me!’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhen wept, “I was led astray!”

sentences.zh: 」乃委罪功曹魯連而斬之，詣寔歸罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he shifted blame to his merit clerk Lu Lian, beheaded him, and went to Shi to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He blamed merit clerk Lu Lian, executed him, and went to Zhang Shi to surrender.

sentences.zh: 南討曹祛，走之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi marched south against Cao Qu and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi took the army south, struck Cao Qu, and sent him fleeing.

sentences.zh: 張坦至自京師，帝優詔勞軌，依模所表，命誅曹祛。

translations.literal: When Tan arrived from the capital, the emperor issued a gracious edict comforting Gui, following Mo’s memorial, and ordered Cao Qu executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tan’s arrival from Luoyang brought an imperial rescript praising Zhang Gui and, on Sima Mo’s recommendation, commanding Cao Qu’s death.

sentences.zh: 軌大悅，赦州內殊死已下。

translations.literal: Gui was greatly pleased and granted amnesty within the province for all crimes short of capital ones.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui rejoiced and declared an amnesty short of capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 命寔率尹員、宋配步騎三萬討祛，別遣從事田迥、王豐率騎八百自姑臧西南出石驢，據長寧。

translations.literal: He ordered Shi to lead Yin Yuan, Song Pei, and thirty thousand foot and horse against Qu, and separately sent aides Tian Jiong and Wang Feng with eight hundred cavalry southwest from Guzang out through Stone Mule to hold Changning.
translations.idiomatic: He told Zhang Shi to take Yin Yuan, Song Pei, and thirty thousand men against Cao Qu while aides Tian Jiong and Wang Feng led eight hundred horse southwest from Guzang via Stone Mule to seize Changning.

sentences.zh: 怯遣麹晁距戰于黃阪。

translations.literal: Cao Qu sent Qu Chao to oppose them at Yellow Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Qu dispatched Qu Chao to hold them at Yellow Slope.

sentences.zh: 寔詭道出浩亹，戰於破羌。

translations.literal: Shi took a concealed route through Haomen and fought at Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi slipped through Haomen and fought at Poyang.

sentences.zh: 軌斬祛及牙門田囂。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui put Cao Qu and gate guard Tian Ao to death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui executed Cao Qu and gate captain Tian Ao.

sentences.zh: 遣治中張閬送義兵五千及郡國秀孝貢計、器甲方物歸於京師。

translations.literal: He sent headquarters aide Zhang Lang to escort five thousand righteous troops together with commandery and kingdom “filial and incorrupt” candidates, tribute accounts, armor, weapons, and local products to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched headquarters aide Zhang Lang with five thousand volunteer troops, provincial examination graduates, tribute tallies, arms, and native goods to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 令有司可推詳立州已來清貞德素，嘉遁遺榮：「高才碩學，著述經史；

translations.literal: He ordered the relevant offices to investigate thoroughly, since the province was founded, for chaste integrity and plain virtue, for reclusion with honor renounced, for ‘men of high talent and broad learning who have authored Classics and histories;
translations.idiomatic: He told officials to compile, from the founding of the province, lists of the incorrupt, the reclusive, and scholars who had written on the Classics and history;

sentences.zh: 臨危殉義，殺身為君；

translations.literal: for those who faced peril and died for righteousness, giving their lives for the ruler;
translations.idiomatic: those who died for loyalty in crisis;

sentences.zh: 忠諫而嬰禍，專對而釋患；

translations.literal: for loyal remonstrators who met disaster, and envoys who by eloquence dispelled peril;
translations.idiomatic: those who remonstrated at the cost of their lives and diplomats who talked their way out of danger;

sentences.zh: 權智雄勇，為時除難；

translations.literal: for men of bold stratagem and heroic courage who removed difficulties for the age;
translations.idiomatic: strategists and champions who removed threats to the state;

sentences.zh: 謅佞誤主，傷陷忠賢；

translations.literal: for sycophants who misled their lords and injured the loyal and worthy;
translations.idiomatic: and flatterers who led rulers astray and ruined good men;

sentences.zh: 具狀以聞。

translations.literal: submit full particulars in memorials.’
translations.idiomatic: each case to be reported in detail.”

sentences.zh: 州中父老莫不相慶。

translations.literal: Not one of the elders of the province failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: The province’s elders rejoiced together.

sentences.zh: 光祿傅祗、太常摯虞遺軌書，告京師饑匱，軌即遣參軍杜勳獻馬五百匹、毯布三萬匹。

translations.literal: Superintendent of the Household Fu Zhi and Chamberlain for Ceremonies Zhi Yu sent Gui letters telling him that the capital was starving; Gui immediately sent adjutant Du Xun to present five hundred horses and thirty thousand bolts of felt and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi and Zhi Yu wrote that Luoyang was starving; Zhang Gui at once sent adjutant Du Xun with five hundred horses and thirty thousand bolts of felt and cloth.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者進拜鎮西將軍、都督隴右諸軍事，封霸城侯，進車騎將軍、開府辟如、儀同三司。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched envoys promoting him to General Who Garrisons the West and Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs on the right of Long, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Baling, then advancing him to chariot-and-horse general with a separate establishment equal to the Three Excellencies and ceremonies matching the Three Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys promoted him to General Who Garrisons the West, commander of all Longyou armies, marquis of Baling, then chariot-and-horse general with independent staff and honors matching the three dukes.

sentences.zh: 策未至，而王彌遂逼洛陽，軌遣將軍張斐、北宮純、郭敷等率精騎五千來衛京都。

translations.literal: Before the patent arrived, Wang Mi pressed Luoyang; Gui sent generals Zhang Fei, Bei Gong Chun, and Guo Fu with five thousand picked cavalry to defend the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before the patent reached him, Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, so he sent Zhang Fei, Bei Gong Chun, and Guo Fu with five thousand elite horse to the capital’s relief.

sentences.zh: 及京都陷，斐等皆沒於賊。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Fei and the others all perished among the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, those generals died in the enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 中州避難來者日月相繼，分武威置武興郡以居之。

translations.literal: Refugees from the central provinces arrived day after day; he divided off part of Wuwei to form Wuxing commandery to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives from the east streamed in daily, so he carved Wuxing commandery out of Wuwei to house them.

sentences.zh: 太府主簿馬魴言於軌曰：「四海傾覆，乘輿未反，明公以全州之力徑造平陽，必當萬里風披，有征無戰。

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the grand treasury Ma Fang said to Gui, ‘The four seas are overturned and the imperial carriage has not returned; if you, sir, with the strength of a whole province marched straight on Pingyang, you would scatter the enemy for ten thousand li without a battle.
translations.idiomatic: Grand-treasury chief clerk Ma Fang urged him to take the entire province straight to Pingyang and sweep the rebels away.

sentences.zh: 未審何憚不為此舉？

translations.literal: I do not understand what you fear that keeps you from doing this.’
translations.idiomatic: He asked why Zhang Gui hesitated to strike.

sentences.zh: 」軌曰：「是孤心也。

translations.literal: Gui said, ‘That is this solitary one’s own heart.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui answered, “That has been my own mind as well.”

sentences.zh: 」又聞秦王入關，乃馳檄關中曰：「主上遘危，遷幸非所，普天分崩，率土喪氣。

translations.literal: When he also heard that the Prince of Qin had entered the passes, he hurriedly sent a proclamation into Guanzhong saying, ‘The sovereign has met peril and been moved to a place that is not fitting; all under heaven is split apart, and every inch of soil has lost its breath.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Prince of Qin had entered the passes, he fired a manifesto into Guanzhong: “The Son of Heaven is in jeopardy, driven to an unworthy refuge; the realm is shattered and morale is broken.

sentences.zh: 秦王天挺聖德，神武應期。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin is heaven-endowed with sagely virtue, divine in arms and fitted to the hour.’
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin bears heaven’s sagely virtue, a warlike spirit born for the moment.”

sentences.zh: 世祖之孫，王今為長。

translations.literal: He is a grandson of Emperor Shizu; you, Prince, are now the senior among us.
translations.idiomatic: You are of Shizu’s line, and among the princes you now stand first.

sentences.zh: 凡我晉人，食土之類，龜筮克從，幽明同款。

translations.literal: All of us people of Jin who live on this soil—tortoise-shell and milfoil approve, and the spirits of light and dark are of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: Every Jin subject dwelling on this earth finds tortoise and milfoil in accord, and both realms of the unseen give their assent.

sentences.zh: 宜簡令奪奉登皇位。

translations.literal: It is fitting to select the worthy and raise him to the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: The time has come to choose a worthy man and set him on the throne.

sentences.zh: 今遣前鋒督護宋配步騎二萬，徑至長安，翼衛乘輿，折沖左右。

translations.literal: Now I send Forward Army Supervisor Song Pei with twenty thousand foot and horse straight to Chang’an to shield the imperial carriage and strike down foes on either side.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatches Song Pei, forward supervisor, with twenty thousand troops to Chang’an to guard the emperor and clear the flanks.

sentences.zh: 西中郎寔中軍三萬，武威太守張琠胡騎二萬，駱驛繼發，仲秋中旬會于臨晉。

translations.literal: He sends Forward Army Supervisor Song Pei with twenty thousand foot and horse straight to Chang’an; General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the West Zhang Shi with thirty thousand central-army troops; Grand Administrator Zhang Tian of Wuwei with twenty thousand Hu cavalry—these are to follow in continuous columns and assemble at Linjin in the middle ten days of mid-autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Song Pei takes twenty thousand straight to Chang’an; Zhang Shi, as western household general, leads thirty thousand from the central army; Zhang Tian of Wuwei brings twenty thousand Hu horse—all marching in relays to rendezvous at Linjin by mid-autumn.

sentences.zh: 俄而秦王為皇太子，遣使拜軌為驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，固辭。

translations.literal: Soon the Prince of Qin became heir apparent and sent envoys to appoint Gui as Grand General of Agile Cavalry with ceremonies matching the Three Excellencies; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin was named crown prince, envoys offered Zhang Gui the post of grand general of agile cavalry with honors equal to the three dukes; he refused.

sentences.zh: 秦州刺史裴苞、東羌校尉貫與據險斷使，命宋配討之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Qinzhou Pei Bao and Colonel of the Eastern Qiang Guan Yu seized defiles and cut off envoys; he ordered Song Pei to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Bao of Qinzhou and Eastern Qiang colonel Guan Yu blocked the passes and stopped couriers, so Zhang Gui sent Song Pei against them.

sentences.zh: 西平王叔與曹祛餘黨麹儒等劫前福祿令麹恪為主，執太守趙彝，東應裴苞。

translations.literal: Wang Shu of Xiping, together with Cao Qu’s remnant follower Qu Ru and others, seized former Magistrate of Fulu Qu Que as their leader, arrested Grand Administrator Zhao Yi, and linked with Pei Bao to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu of Xiping joined Qu Ru’s faction, made Qu Que their chief, took Zhao Yi hostage, and coordinated with Pei Bao eastward.

sentences.zh: 寔回師討之，斬儒等，左督護陰預與苞戰陝西，大敗之，苞奔桑凶塢。

translations.literal: Shi turned his army back to punish them, beheaded Ru and the others; Left Army Supervisor Yin Yu fought Pei Bao west of the pass and routed him; Bao fled to the Sangxiong stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi wheeled about, executed Qu Ru’s party, and Yin Yu smashed Pei Bao in Shaanxi, driving him to the Sangxiong redoubt.

sentences.zh: 是歲，北宮純降劉聰。

translations.literal: That year Bei Gong Chun surrendered to Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: In the same year Bei Gong Chun went over to Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 皇太子遣使重申前授，固辭。

translations.literal: The crown prince sent envoys to repeat the earlier appointment; again he declined.
translations.idiomatic: The heir’s messengers renewed the offer; Zhang Gui again declined.

sentences.zh: 左司馬竇濤言於軌曰：「曲阜周旦弗辭，營丘齊望承命，所以明國憲，厲殊勳。

translations.literal: Left Major Dou Tao said to Gui, ‘At Qufu the Duke of Zhou did not decline; at Yingqiu Jiang Taigong accepted the mandate—thereby the state’s statutes were made clear and extraordinary merit encouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tao urged him: “At Qufu the Duke of Zhou did not demur; at Yingqiu the Qi founder took his charge—thus the law honored great service.

sentences.zh: 天下崩亂，皇輿遷幸，州雖僻遠，不忘匡衛，故朝廷傾懷，嘉命屢集。

translations.literal: All under heaven is collapsing in chaos, the imperial carriage has been moved, and though this province is remote it has not forgotten to aid and guard the throne; therefore the court leans upon you with favor, and gracious commissions have come again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is shattered and the court adrift, yet distant Liangzhou still shields the throne, which is why the capital keeps heaping honors on you.

sentences.zh: 宜從朝旨，以副群心。

translations.literal: You ought to follow the court’s command to satisfy the hopes of the multitude.’
translations.idiomatic: You should accept the imperial will and answer the people’s expectation.”

sentences.zh: 」軌不從。

translations.literal: Gui did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui would not agree.

sentences.zh: 初，寔平麹懦，徙元惡六百餘家。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Shi had pacified Qu Nuo, he moved more than six hundred households of the chief evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Shi crushed Qu Nuo, he resettled over six hundred families of the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 治中令狐瀏曰：「夫除惡人，猶農夫之去草，令絕其本，勿使能滋。

translations.literal: Headquarters aide Linghu Liu said, ‘In removing evil men it is like the farmer rooting out weeds: one must cut off the root so they cannot grow again.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Liu argued: “Rooting out villains is like weeding—you must kill the root so nothing sprouts.

sentences.zh: 今宜悉徙，以絕後患。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to move them all and thereby cut off later trouble.’
translations.idiomatic: Move every one of them now and leave no future threat.”

sentences.zh: 」寔不納。

translations.literal: Shi did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi did not follow the advice.

sentences.zh: 儒黨果叛，寔進平之。

translations.literal: The Qu faction indeed rebelled; Shi advanced and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Qu’s clique rose anyway, and Zhang Shi marched again to crush them.

sentences.zh: 湣帝即位，進位司空，固讓。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, Gui’s rank was advanced to Minister of Works; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min promoted him to minister of works, which he refused.

sentences.zh: 太府參軍索輔言於軌曰：「古以金貝皮幣為貨，息穀帛量度之秏。

translations.literal: Adjutant of the grand treasury Suo Fu said to Gui, ‘In antiquity shell, cowrie, hide, and cloth served as currency, sparing the waste of measuring grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Fu of the grand treasury told him: “Antiquity used metal, shell, and cloth as money to avoid the waste of weighing grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 二漢制五銖錢，通易不滯。

translations.literal: The two Han dynasties minted the five-zhu coin, so exchange flowed without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s five-zhu cash kept trade moving smoothly.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，河西荒廢，遂不用錢。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era the west of the river was desolate and coins fell out of use.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi the Hexi region was so ruined that money disappeared.

sentences.zh: 裂匹以為段數。

translations.literal: They tore bolts of silk into counted segments.
translations.idiomatic: Silk was torn into arbitrary lengths for barter.

sentences.zh: 縑布既壞，市易又難，徒壞女工，不任衣用，弊之甚也。

translations.literal: Once fine cloth was ruined, market trade became difficult, vainly harming women’s weaving yet unfit for clothing—harm indeed was extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Damaged silk ruined commerce, wasted women’s labor, and still could not clothe anyone—a thorough evil.

sentences.zh: 今中州雖亂，此方主安全，宜復五銖以濟通變之會。

translations.literal: Now the central plain is in turmoil, but this region is secure; it is fitting to restore the five-zhu coin to meet the needs of circulation.’
translations.idiomatic: The heartland is at war, yet we are safe; restoring the five-zhu will ease exchange.”

sentences.zh: 」軌納之，立制准布用錢，錢遂大行，人賴其利。

translations.literal: Gui accepted this, established regulations pegging cloth to coin, and coinage then circulated widely; people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui agreed, set a cloth-to-coin standard, and currency flourished to the people’s gain.

sentences.zh: 是時劉曜寇北地，軌又遣參軍麹陶領三千人衛長安。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yao raided Beidi; Gui again sent adjutant Qu Tao with three thousand men to defend Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao struck Beidi, he sent Qu Tao with three thousand to reinforce Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 帝遣大鴻臚辛攀拜軌侍中、太尉、涼州牧、西平公，軌又固辭。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Grand Herald Xin Pan to appoint Gui as palace attendant, grand commandant, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping; again Gui firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Xin Pan to name him attendant-in-chief, grand commandant, Liangzhou governor, and duke of Xiping—all declined again.

sentences.zh: 在州十三年，寢疾，遺令曰：「吾無德於人，今疾病彌留，殆將命也。

translations.literal: Thirteen years in the province, lying ill, he left instructions saying, ‘I have lacked virtue toward others; now my illness lingers and death is near.
translations.idiomatic: After thirteen years in office, mortally ill, he dictated: “I have done little good for anyone; my sickness lingers and the end is near.

sentences.zh: 文武將佐咸當弘盡忠規，務安百姓，上思報國，下以寧家。

translations.literal: All civil and military assistants ought to enlarge loyal counsel, work to secure the common people, think above of repaying the state, and below of quieting their households.
translations.idiomatic: Let every officer strive for loyal counsel, comfort the people, serve the throne above, and settle their homes below.

sentences.zh: 素棺薄葬，無藏金玉。

translations.literal: Use plain coffins and spare burial; do not bury gold or jade.
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in a plain coffin without gold or jade.

sentences.zh: 善相安遜，以聽朝旨。

translations.literal: Mutually yield in peace and humility, and await the court’s command.’
translations.idiomatic: Yield to one another in humility and wait for the capital’s orders.”

sentences.zh: 」表立子寔為世子。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that his son Shi be established as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to make his son Zhang Shi heir.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Duke Wu.

sentences.zh: 子孫

translations.literal: Descendants
translations.idiomatic: Section: descendants

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
translations.idiomatic: The printed edition marks a break with a lone “=” symbol.

sentences.zh: 子寔

translations.literal: Zhang Shi (寔)
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi

sentences.zh: =寔字安遜，學尚明察，敬賢愛士，以秀才為郎中。

translations.literal: = Zhang Shi, courtesy name Anxun, was studious, clear-sighted in judgment, respected the worthy and cherished gentlemen, and became a gentleman consultant on the strength of his xiucai degree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi, courtesy name Anxun, valued clear inquiry, honored talent, and entered office as a gentleman consultant after earning the xiucai certificate.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，固辭驍騎將軍，請還涼州，許之，改授議郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongjia era he firmly declined the post of General of Vehement Cavalry and asked to return to Liangzhou; permission was granted, and he was reassigned as gentleman consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongjia he refused the vehement-cavalry generalship and was allowed to go back west as a consultant.

sentences.zh: 及至姑臧，以討曹祛功，封建武亭侯。

translations.literal: When he reached Guzang, for merit in punishing Cao Qu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Martial Mettle Village.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Guzang he was made marquis of Martial Mettle village for his part in defeating Cao Qu.

sentences.zh: 尋遷西中郎將，進爵福祿縣侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the West and advanced in rank to Marquis of Fulu county.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to general of the household on the west and promoted to count of Fulu.

sentences.zh: 建興初，除西中郎將，領護羌校尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianxing era he was appointed General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the West and concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Jianxing years he took the western household generalship with the Qiang-colonel title.

sentences.zh: 軌卒，州人推寔攝父位。

translations.literal: When Gui died, the people of the province urged Shi to act in his father’s place.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Gui’s death the province asked Zhang Shi to hold his father’s post.

sentences.zh: 湣帝因下策書曰：「維乃父武公，著勳西夏。

translations.literal: Emperor Min therefore issued a patent saying, ‘Your late father Duke Wu achieved merit in the western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min’s edict read: “Your father Duke Wu won glory defending the west.

sentences.zh: 頃胡賊狡猾。

translations.literal: Recently the Hu bandits have been cunning.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the barbarians have grown bold.

sentences.zh: 侵逼近甸，義兵銳卒，萬里相尋，方貢遠珍，府無虛歲。

translations.literal: They press close to the inner districts; righteous troops and crack soldiers have sought one another across ten thousand li, and rare tribute from afar fills the treasury every year.
translations.idiomatic: They harry the capital region while loyal hosts march from afar and tribute streams in without pause.

sentences.zh: 方委專征，蕩清九域，昊天不吊，凋餘籓後，朕用悼厥心。

translations.literal: I had entrusted him with sole command to sweep clean the nine regions, but High Heaven showed no pity, cutting down a pillar at the frontier; my heart grieves for him.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to give him independent command to pacify the realm, yet Heaven cut him down at the border; I mourn his fall.

sentences.zh: 維爾雋劭英毅，宜世表西海。

translations.literal: You are outstanding, heroic, and resolute, fit to stand as model beyond the western sea.
translations.idiomatic: You are talented, resolute, and fit to lead the far west.

sentences.zh: 今授持節、都督涼州諸軍事、西中郎將、涼州刺史、領護羌校尉、西平公。

translations.literal: Now I confer staff of authority, commander of all Liangzhou military affairs, General of the Gentlemen of the Household on the West, Inspector of Liangzhou, concurrent Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore grant you the staff, command of Liangzhou armies, the western household generalship, the governorship with Qiang colonel, and the ducal title of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go and reverently accept!
translations.idiomatic: Go—receive this with reverence.

sentences.zh: 其闡弘先緒，俾屏王室。」

translations.literal: Expand your father’s work and be a screen for the house of Jin.’
translations.idiomatic: Carry forward his legacy and shield the Jin throne.”

sentences.zh: 蘭池長趙奭上軍士張冰得璽，文曰「皇帝璽。

translations.literal: Commandant of Orchid Pool Zhao Yi reported that the soldier Zhang Bing had found a seal whose inscription read “Imperial Seal.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi of Lanchi reported that trooper Zhang Bing had unearthed a jade reading “Imperial Seal.”

sentences.zh: 」群僚上慶稱德，寔曰：「孤常忿袁本初擬肘，諸君何忽有此言！

translations.literal: The officials offered congratulations and praised his virtue; Shi said, ‘I have always resented how Yuan Shao coveted the elbow; why do you gentlemen suddenly speak thus!
translations.idiomatic: His staff began to flatter him as heaven’s choice; Zhang Shi snapped, “I despised Yuan Shao’s grasping after the throne—why echo such talk now?”

sentences.zh: 」因送于京師。

translations.literal: He therefore sent it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He forwarded the seal to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 下令國中曰：「忝紹前蹤，庶幾刑政不為百姓之患，而比年饑旱，殆由庶事有缺，竊慕箴誦之言，以補不逮。

translations.literal: He issued an order to the state saying, ‘I shamefully follow in former footsteps, hoping that punishments and government may not become a plague on the people; yet in recent years famine and drought have come—perhaps because my myriad affairs fall short; I privately admire words of admonition to remedy what I lack.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed: “I follow my predecessors in hoping law and policy do not harm the people, yet drought and dearth suggest my rule is flawed; I welcome counsel to mend my faults.

sentences.zh: 自今有面刺孤罪者，酬以束帛；

translations.literal: From today whoever faces me and points out my faults shall be rewarded with a bundle of silk;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone who rebukes me to my face wins a bolt of silk;

sentences.zh: 翰墨陳孤過者，答以筐篚；

translations.literal: who sets down my faults in writing shall receive a basket of goods;
translations.idiomatic: written criticism earns a hamper of goods;

sentences.zh: 謗言於市者，報以羊米。

translations.literal: who spreads reproach in the market shall be repaid with sheep and grain.’
translations.idiomatic: rumor in the marketplace wins sheep and grain.”

sentences.zh: 」賊曹佐高昌隗瑾進言曰：「聖王將舉大事，必崇三訊之法，朝置諫官以匡大理，疑承輔弼以補闕拾遺。

translations.literal: Adjutant of the bandits bureau Wei Jin of Gaochang advanced counsel saying, ‘When a sage king is about to undertake a great matter he always honors the threefold inquiry; the court sets remonstrance officers to correct great principles, and advisers and assistants to patch omissions.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jin urged: “Great kings consult widely; remonstrators and aides exist to catch every slip.

sentences.zh: 今事無巨細，盡決聖慮，興軍布令，朝中不知，若有謬闕，則下無分謗。

translations.literal: Now affairs great and small are all decided by the sage’s private thought; when armies are raised and orders issued, the court knows nothing—if there is error, blame cannot be shared below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet today every decision rests in your hands alone; the capital hears nothing of campaigns, so if you err no one else shares the fault.

sentences.zh: 竊謂宜偃聰塞智，開納群言，政刑大小，與眾共之。

translations.literal: I humbly think you should quiet your private judgments and open your ears to the multitude, sharing government and punishments great and small with the many.
translations.idiomatic: Lower your guard, listen broadly, and let the many share governance.

sentences.zh: 若恆內斷聖心，則群僚畏威而面從矣。

translations.literal: If you always decide inwardly by the sage mind, then the host of officials will fear your majesty and only assent to your face.
translations.idiomatic: If you keep everything inside, your officers will only nod from fear.

sentences.zh: 善惡專歸於上，雖賞千金，終無言也。

translations.literal: Good and evil will all be credited to the heights above; though you offered a thousand in gold, still no one would speak.’
translations.idiomatic: Credit and blame would pile on you alone, and not even gold would buy honest words.”

sentences.zh: 」寔納之，增位三等，賜帛四十匹。

translations.literal: Shi accepted this, raised him three grades in rank, and bestowed forty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi agreed, promoted Wei Jin three ranks, and gave him forty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遣督護王該送諸郡貢計，獻名馬方珍、經史圖籍于京師。

translations.literal: He sent Army Supervisor Wang Gai to escort the commanderies’ tribute accounts and present famous horses, rare treasures, Classics, histories, and maps to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Wang Gai with provincial tribute, fine horses, curios, and books to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 會劉曜逼長安，寔遣將軍王該率眾以援京城。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao pressed Chang’an, Shi sent General Wang Gai with a host to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Yao closed on Chang’an, he sent General Wang Gai with an army to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，拜都督陝西諸軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and appointed him area commander of all military affairs west of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and named him commander of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 及帝將降于劉曜，下詔於寔曰：「天步厄運，禍降晉室，京師傾陷，先帝晏駕賊庭。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to surrender to Liu Yao, he issued an edict to Shi saying, ‘Heaven’s course meets ill fortune; calamity has fallen on the house of Jin; the capital is lost and the late emperor passed away in the rebels’ camp.
translations.idiomatic: Facing surrender to Liu Yao, the emperor wrote Zhang Shi: “Heaven has turned against us; Luoyang is gone and my predecessor died among the bandits.

sentences.zh: 朕流漂宛許，爰暨舊京。

translations.literal: I drifted to Wan and Xu and reached the old capital.
translations.idiomatic: I wandered to Wan and Xu until I regained the old capital.

sentences.zh: 群臣以宗廟無主，歸之於朕，遂以沖眇之身托于王公之上。

translations.literal: The ministers, seeing the ancestral temples without a lord, turned to me, and I have entrusted this frail person upon the high seat of the kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, finding no master for the temples, raised me, a frail child, to the throne.

sentences.zh: 自踐寶位，四載於茲，不能翦除巨寇以救危難，元元兆庶仍遭塗炭，皆朕不明所致。

translations.literal: Since I mounted the precious throne four years have passed, yet I could not extirpate the great bandits and save the crisis; the myriad common folk still suffer slaughter and scorching—all because I lack enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: Four years on the throne and I have failed to crush the foe or save the people; their agony is my fault alone.

sentences.zh: 羯賊劉載僭稱大號，禍加先帝，肆殺籓王，深惟仇恥，枕戈待旦。

translations.literal: The Jie bandit Liu Zai arrogated the great title, brought disaster on the late emperor, wantonly slew princes of the blood—I ponder this shame and bitterness and sleep on my spear awaiting the dawn.
translations.idiomatic: The Jie usurper Liu Cong claimed the throne, struck down my father, and slaughtered princes; I nurse that shame and sleep on my arms.

sentences.zh: 劉曜自去年九月率其蟻眾，乘虛深寇，劫質羌胡，攻沒北地。

translations.literal: Since last September Liu Yao has led his antlike hosts, exploited emptiness to raid deep, seized Qiang and Hu as hostages, and overrun Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn Liu Yao has driven deep with a horde of ants, taken barbarian hostages, and taken Beidi.

sentences.zh: 麹允總戎在外，六軍敗績，侵逼京城，矢流宮闕。

translations.literal: Qu Yun commanded troops outside, the six armies were routed, the enemy pressed the capital, and arrows flew within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun’s field armies collapsed, the foe ringed Luoyang, and shafts rattled in the palace.

sentences.zh: 胡崧等雖赴國難，殿而無效，圍塹十重，外救不至，糧盡人窮，遂為降虜。

translations.literal: Although Hu Song and others rushed to the national crisis, they halted without effect; ten rings of siege, no relief from outside, provisions exhausted and men desperate—thus they became captives who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song’s relief failed; ten lines of trenches, no succor, starvation—so they yielded.

sentences.zh: 仰慚乾靈，俯痛宗廟。

translations.literal: I am ashamed before Heaven on high and grieve for the ancestral temples below.
translations.idiomatic: I hang my head before Heaven and weep for the altars.

sentences.zh: 君世篤忠亮，勳隆西夏，四海具瞻，朕所憑賴。

translations.literal: You, sir, for generations have been steeped in loyalty and brightness; your merit towers in the western Xia; all within the four seas look to you, and I rely upon you.
translations.idiomatic: Your house has long been loyal; the west hangs on you, and all the realm watches.

sentences.zh: 今進君大都督、涼州牧、侍中、司空，承制行事。

translations.literal: Now I advance you to grand governor, governor of Liangzhou, palace attendant, and minister of works, with authority to act on imperial rescript.
translations.idiomatic: I promote you to grand governor of Liangzhou, attendant-in-chief, minister of works, with mandate to act by edict.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王宗室親賢，遠在江表。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye is a kinsman of the house, worthy and virtuous, far away on the south bank of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Rui of Langye, royal and worthy, waits beyond the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷播越，社稷倒懸，朕以詔王，時攝大位。

translations.literal: Now the court is driven about and the altars hang upside down; I therefore command the prince to hold the great position for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: With the court uprooted I call on him to assume the regency.

sentences.zh: 君其挾贊琅邪，共濟難運。

translations.literal: You, sir, should support and assist the Prince of Langye and together ford this hard fate.
translations.idiomatic: Stand by Prince Langye and carry us through this ordeal.

sentences.zh: 若不忘主，宗廟有賴。

translations.literal: If you do not forget the sovereign, the ancestral temples will have something to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: If you remain true, the temples still have hope.

sentences.zh: 明便出降，故夜見公卿，屬以後事，密遣黃門郎史淑、侍御史王沖齎詔假授。

translations.literal: Tomorrow I shall go out to surrender; therefore tonight I have seen the dukes and ministers, entrusted them with later affairs, and secretly sent Palace Attendant Shi Shu and attendant censor Wang Chong bearing patents of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: I surrender at dawn; tonight I charged my ministers and sent Shi Shu and Wang Chong with sealed commissions.

sentences.zh: 臨出寄命，公其勉之！

translations.literal: As I go out I leave my charge—do your utmost!’
translations.idiomatic: This is my parting charge—spare no strength!”

sentences.zh: 」寔以天子蒙塵，沖讓不拜。

translations.literal: Shi, because the Son of Heaven was in dust and disgrace, modestly declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi, seeing the emperor humiliated, modestly refused the titles.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍、西海太守張肅，寔叔父也，以京師危逼，請為先鋒擊劉曜。

translations.literal: General Who Establishes Might and Grand Administrator of the Western Sea Zhang Su, Shi’s uncle by birth, because the capital was in imminent peril, asked to serve as vanguard against Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhang Su, general who establishes might and lord of the Western Sea, begged to lead the van against Liu Yao as Luoyang tottered.

sentences.zh: 寔以肅年老，弗許。

translations.literal: Shi, because Su was old, did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi refused, citing his uncle’s age.

sentences.zh: 肅曰：「狐死首丘，心不忘本；

translations.literal: Su said, ‘When the fox dies its head points toward its mound—its heart does not forget its root;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Su replied: “The dying fox turns its head toward its burrow—never forgetting home;

sentences.zh: 鐘儀在晉，楚弁南音。

translations.literal: Zhong Yi, though held in Jin, still wore the Chu cap and sang the southern airs.
translations.idiomatic: Like Zhong Yi, a captive in Jin who kept Chu’s cap and southern songs, I remember who I am.

sentences.zh: 肅受晉龍，剖符列位。

translations.literal: Su received Jin’s dragon favor and bore the split tallies of office.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken Jin’s dragon commission and carried its halved tallies.

sentences.zh: 羯逆滔天，朝廷傾覆，肅宴安方裔，難至不奮，何以為人臣！

translations.literal: The Jie rebels overflow heaven; the court is overturned; yet Su sits at ease on the frontier—when crisis comes I do not rouse myself; how may I be called a minister!’
translations.idiomatic: The Jie flood the skies and the throne is gone—yet I sit safe in the west without stirring; what kind of servant am I?”

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「門戶受重恩，自當闔宗效死，忠衛社稷，以申先公之志。

translations.literal: Shi said, ‘Our house has received heavy favor from the state; naturally the whole clan ought to give their lives in loyalty, guarding the altars of soil and grain, so as to extend the ambition of my late father.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi answered: “Our clan owes Jin everything; every cousin should die if need be to shield the altars and fulfill my father’s will.

sentences.zh: 但叔父春秋已高，氣力衰竭，軍旅之事非耆耄所堪。

translations.literal: But my uncle’s years are already high, his strength is failing, and military affairs are not what the very aged can bear.’
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are old and frail—campaigning is no work for a graybeard.”

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the request.

sentences.zh: 既而聞京師陷沒，肅悲憤而卒。

translations.literal: Before long, hearing that the capital had fallen, Su died of grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: When news came that Luoyang had fallen, Zhang Su died of grief and wrath.

sentences.zh: 寔知劉曜逼遷天子，大臨三日。

translations.literal: When Shi learned that Liu Yao was forcing the Son of Heaven to move his residence, he observed grand mourning for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Liu Yao was marching the emperor away, Zhang Shi mourned three days.

sentences.zh: 遣太府司馬韓璞、滅寇將軍田齊、撫戎將軍張閬、前鋒督護陰預步騎一萬，東赴國難。

translations.literal: He sent Grand Treasury Major Han Pu, General Who Exterminates Bandits Tian Qi, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians Zhang Lang, and Forward Army Supervisor Yin Yu with ten thousand foot and horse eastward to answer the national crisis.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Han Pu, Tian Qi, Zhang Lang, and Yin Yu with ten thousand men east to relieve the throne.

sentences.zh: 命討虜將軍陳安、故太守賈騫、隴西太守吳紹各統郡兵為璞等前驅。

translations.literal: He ordered General Who Punishes the Caitiffs Chen An, former Grand Administrator Jia Qian, and Grand Administrator of Longxi Wu Shao each to command their commandery troops as vanguards for Han Pu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An, Jia Qian, and Wu Shao were told to lead local levies as the van for Han Pu’s column.

sentences.zh: 戒璞曰：「前遣諸將多違機信，所執不同，致有乖阻。

translations.literal: He warned Han Pu, saying, ‘The generals I sent earlier often broke faith with the opportune moment; what they held to differed, and therefore there was obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: He cautioned Han Pu: “Past columns lost coordination and missed their timing.

sentences.zh: 且內不和親，焉能服物！

translations.literal: Moreover, if there is no harmony within, how can one win submission from without!
translations.idiomatic: Without unity within, you cannot command respect abroad.”

sentences.zh: 今遣禦督五將兵事，當如一體，不得令乖異之問達孤耳也。

translations.literal: Now I send you to supervise the military affairs of five generals as one body; you must not let word of discord reach this solitary one’s ears.’
translations.idiomatic: You now oversee five generals as a single body—let no rumor of division reach me.”

sentences.zh: 」復遺南陽王保書曰：「王室有事，不忘投軀。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao saying, ‘When the royal house is in trouble I do not forget to offer my body.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote again to Prince Sima Bao of Nanyang: “When the dynasty is in peril I do not withhold my life.

sentences.zh: 孤州遠域，首尾多難，是以前遣賈騫，瞻望公舉。

translations.literal: This isolated province lies far at the frontier, beset head and tail with hardship; therefore I earlier sent Jia Qian to look to your public support.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou stands remote, hard pressed on every side, which is why I earlier sent Jia Qian to await your lead.

sentences.zh: 中被符命，敕騫還軍。

translations.literal: Midway I received a sealed order commanding Qian to turn the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Then an imperial rescript arrived ordering Jia Qian to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 忽聞北地陷沒，寇逼長安，胡崧不進，麹允持金五百請救於崧，是以決遣騫等進軍度嶺。

translations.literal: Suddenly I heard that Beidi had fallen and raiders pressed Chang’an; Hu Song did not advance, and Qu Yun took five hundred in gold to beg rescue from Song—therefore I resolved to send Qian and the others forward across the range.
translations.idiomatic: When Beidi collapsed and Hu Song stalled, Qu Yun had to buy relief with gold; I therefore pushed Jia Qian’s host over the pass.

sentences.zh: 會聞朝廷傾覆，為忠不達於主，遣兵不及於難，痛慨之深，死有餘責。

translations.literal: Just then I learned the court had been overturned; my loyalty could not reach the sovereign, and my troops could not arrive in time for the crisis—my grief and shame are boundless; even death leaves me with blame.
translations.idiomatic: Then came word that Luoyang was lost—loyalty never reached the throne, and my army arrived too late; I bear guilt beyond death.

sentences.zh: 今更遣韓璞等，唯公命是從。

translations.literal: Now I again send Han Pu and the others; they will follow whatever command you give.’
translations.idiomatic: I send Han Pu again; he awaits your orders.”

sentences.zh: 」及璞次南安，諸羌斷軍路，相持百餘日，糧竭矢盡。

translations.literal: When Han Pu halted at Nan’an, the various Qiang cut the army’s road; they stood opposed more than a hundred days until grain was exhausted and arrows were spent.
translations.idiomatic: At Nan’an the Qiang blocked the road for over a hundred days until supplies failed.

sentences.zh: 璞殺駕牛饗軍，泣謂眾曰：「汝曹念父母乎？

translations.literal: Pu slaughtered draft oxen to feast the army and wept, saying to the host, ‘Do you think of your fathers and mothers?
translations.idiomatic: Han Pu killed the baggage oxen for a feast and wept: “Do you long for your parents?”

translations.literal: They said, ‘We do.’
translations.idiomatic: They answered yes.

sentences.zh: 」「念妻子乎？

translations.literal: ‘Do you think of wives and children?’
translations.idiomatic: “Do you miss your wives and children?”

sentences.zh: 曰：「念。

translations.literal: They said, ‘We do.’
translations.idiomatic: Again they said yes.

sentences.zh: 」「欲生還乎？

translations.literal: ‘Do you wish to return alive?’
translations.idiomatic: “Do you want to see home again?”

translations.literal: They said, ‘We wish it.’
translations.idiomatic: They shouted that they did.

sentences.zh: 」「從我令乎？

translations.literal: ‘Will you obey my commands?’
translations.idiomatic: “Will you obey my orders?”

translations.literal: They said, ‘We will.’
translations.idiomatic: They swore they would.

sentences.zh: 」乃鼓噪進戰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beat drums and shouted and advanced to battle.
translations.idiomatic: He then beat the drums and charged.

sentences.zh: 會張閬率金城軍繼至，夾擊，大敗之，斬級數千。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Lang arrived leading the Jincheng army; they struck from both sides, inflicting a great defeat and beheading several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lang’s Jincheng troops came up; the combined attack routed the Qiang and took thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 時焦崧、陳安寇隴石，東與劉曜相持，雍秦之人死者十八九。

translations.literal: At that time Jiao Song and Chen An raided Longyou, facing Liu Yao to the east; of the people of Yong and Qin eight or nine in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Jiao Song and Chen An ravaged Longyou, locked with Liu Yao, and nine-tenths of Yong and Qin perished.

sentences.zh: 初，永嘉中，長安謠曰：「秦川中，血沒腕，惟有涼州倚柱觀。

translations.literal: In the beginning, in the Yongjia era, a ditty in Chang’an said, ‘In the land within Qin the blood reaches the wrist; only in Liangzhou may one lean on a pillar and watch.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia a Chang’an rhyme ran: “In Qin heartland blood wades to the wrist; only Liangzhou lets you lean on a pillar and watch.

sentences.zh: 」至是，謠言驗矣。

translations.literal: By now the ditty had proved true.
translations.idiomatic: The prophecy had come true.

sentences.zh: 焦崧、陳安逼上邽，南陽王保遣使告急。

translations.literal: Jiao Song and Chen An pressed Shanggui; Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao sent envoys with urgent pleas.
translations.idiomatic: When Song and Chen besieged Shanggui, Prince Sima Bao called for help.

sentences.zh: 以金城太守竇濤為輕車將軍。

translations.literal: He appointed Grand Administrator of Jincheng Dou Tao as General of Agile Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tao of Jincheng was named general of agile chariots.

sentences.zh: 率威遠將軍宋毅及和苞、張閬、宋輯、辛韜、張選、董廣步騎二萬赴之。

translations.literal: He led General Who Deters the Distance Song Yi together with He Bao, Zhang Lang, Song Ji, Xin Tao, Zhang Xuan, and Dong Guang with twenty thousand foot and horse to go to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yi, He Bao, Zhang Lang, and the rest marched twenty thousand to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 軍次新陽，會湣帝崩問至，素服舉哀，大臨三日。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xinyang; just then news arrived that Emperor Min had died; they put on white garments and observed mourning, holding grand lament for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Camped at Xinyang, they learned of Emperor Min’s death, donned mourning, and wailed three days.

sentences.zh: 時南陽王保謀稱尊號，破羌都尉張詵言於寔曰：「南陽王忘莫大之恥，而欲自尊，天不受其圖籙，德不足以應運，終非濟時救難者也。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao plotted to assume the imperial style; Colonel Who Breaks the Qiang Zhang Shen said to Shi, ‘The Prince of Nanyang forgets the greatest shame yet wishes to exalt himself; Heaven will not accept his talisman charts, and his virtue is not enough to answer the season—he is not one who can save the age from disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao planned to declare himself emperor; Zhang Shen warned Zhang Shi that Bao forgot national humiliation and lacked Heaven’s mandate.

sentences.zh: 晉王明德昵籓，先帝憑屬，宜表稱聖德，勸即尊號，傳檄諸籓，副言相府，則欲競之心息，未合之徒散矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin is illustrious in virtue and intimate with the feudatories; the late emperor relied on him—you ought to memorialize his sagely virtue, urge him to take the supreme title, circulate a manifesto to the princes, and send duplicate word to the minister’s headquarters; then hearts that would compete will rest and factions not yet united will scatter.’
translations.idiomatic: The Jin prince’s virtue wins the regional houses and the late emperor trusted him—memorialize him, urge the throne, circulate orders to the princes and the chief minister, and rivalry will die down.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: Shi followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是馳檄天下，推崇晉王為天子，遣牙門蔡忠奉表江南，勸即尊位。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sped a manifesto through the realm, exalting the Prince of Jin as Son of Heaven, sent gate guard Cai Zhong with a memorial south of the Yangzi, and urged him to mount the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He broadcast a call to crown Sima Rui as emperor and sent Cai Zhong to the south with a memorial urging accession.

sentences.zh: 是歲，元帝即位於建鄴，改年太興，寔猶稱建興六年，不從中興之所改也。

translations.literal: That year Yuan Di mounted the throne at Jianye and changed the era name to Taixing; Shi still used the sixth year of Jianxing and did not follow the change made for the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yuan Di took the throne at Jianye as Taixing; Zhang Shi still dated documents Jianxing year six, refusing the new era.

sentences.zh: 保聞湣帝崩，自稱晉王，建元，署置百官，遣使拜寔征西大將軍、儀同三司，增邑三千戶。

translations.literal: When Bao heard that Emperor Min had died, he styled himself Prince of Jin, established an era title, appointed the full set of officials, and sent envoys to appoint Shi as Grand General Who Conquers the West with ceremonies matching the Three Excellencies, increasing his fief by three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao then styled himself prince of Jin, set up a court calendar, and offered Zhang Shi the western-conquest generalship with three thousand extra households.

sentences.zh: 俄而保為陳安所叛，氐羌皆應之。

translations.literal: Soon Bao was betrayed by Chen An, and the Di and Qiang all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An soon rebelled against him, joined by Di and Qiang.

sentences.zh: 保窘迫，遂去上邽，遷祁山，寔遣將韓璞步騎五千赴難。

translations.literal: Bao was hard pressed, thereupon left Shanggui, and moved to Qishan; Shi sent General Han Pu with five thousand foot and horse to answer the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Bao fled to Qishan; Zhang Shi sent Han Pu with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 陳安退保綿諸，保歸上邽。

translations.literal: Chen An withdrew to defend Mianzhu; Bao returned to Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen An fell back to Mianzhu while Bao reoccupied Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 未幾，保復為安所敗，使詣寔乞師。

translations.literal: Before long Bao was again defeated by An and sent to Shi begging for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bao lost again to Chen An and begged Zhang Shi for an army.

sentences.zh: 寔遣宋毅赴之，而安退。

translations.literal: Shi sent Song Yi to go to him, and An withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi dispatched Song Yi, and Chen An retreated.

sentences.zh: 會保為劉曜所逼，遷于桑城，將謀奔寔。

translations.literal: Just then Bao was hard pressed by Liu Yao, moved to Sangcheng, and planned to flee to Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Then Liu Yao drove Bao to Sangcheng, and he meant to run to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 寔以其宗室之望，若至河右，必動物情，遣其將陰監逆保，聲言翼衛，實禦之也。

translations.literal: Shi, because Bao enjoyed prestige as a member of the imperial clan, feared that if he reached the west of the river he would stir popular feeling; he sent his general Yin Jian to intercept Bao, declaring publicly that he meant to shield him but in truth blocking him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi feared a royal prince on his soil would sway the people, so he sent Yin Jian to “escort” him while actually blocking his flight.

sentences.zh: 會保薨，其眾散奔涼州者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Just then Bao died; more than ten thousand of his host scattered and fled into Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bao died; over ten thousand of his followers drifted into Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 寔自恃險遠，頗自驕恣。

translations.literal: Shi, relying on the danger and distance of his position, became rather arrogant and self-indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: Secure in his remoteness, Zhang Shi grew proud and lax.

sentences.zh: 初，寔寢室梁間有人像，無頭，久而乃滅，寔甚惡之。

translations.literal: In the beginning, in Shi’s bedchamber a headless human form appeared between the beams; after a long while it vanished; Shi greatly hated it.
translations.idiomatic: A headless figure had appeared between the rafters of his bedroom and faded away—an omen he loathed.

sentences.zh: 京兆人劉弘者，挾左道，客居天梯第五山，然燈懸鏡於山穴中為光明，以惑百姓，受道者千餘人，寔左右皆事之。

translations.literal: There was a man of Jingzhao, Liu Hong, who practiced heterodox arts, lodged as a guest on the fifth terrace of Mount Tian ladder, hung lamps and mirrors in a mountain cave to make light, and deluded the common people; more than a thousand received his teaching, and Shi’s attendants on left and right all served him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong of Jingzhao peddled sorcery on Mount Tian, dazzled villagers with lamps and mirrors, and drew even Zhang Shi’s household into his sect.

sentences.zh: 帳下閻沙、牙門趙仰皆弘鄉人，弘謂之曰：「天與我神璽，應王涼州。

translations.literal: Camp guard Yan Sha and gate guard Zhao Yang were fellow townsmen of Hong; Hong said to them, ‘Heaven has given me a divine seal—I ought to rule Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong told Yan Sha and Zhao Yang that Heaven had given him a sacred seal to rule the west.

sentences.zh: 」沙、仰信之，密與寔左右十餘人謀殺寔，奉弘為主。

translations.literal: Sha and Yang believed him and secretly plotted with more than ten of Shi’s attendants to kill Shi and set up Hong as lord.
translations.idiomatic: They conspired with Zhang Shi’s guards to murder him and enthrone Liu Hong.

sentences.zh: 寔潛知其謀，收弘殺之。

translations.literal: Shi secretly learned of the plot, seized Hong, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi uncovered the plot, arrested Hong, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 沙等不之知，以其夜害寔。

translations.literal: Sha and the others did not know this; that night they murdered Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Sha’s party, unaware, struck that night and killed Zhang Shi.

sentences.zh: 在位六年。

translations.literal: He had occupied the position six years.
translations.idiomatic: He had held power six years.

sentences.zh: 私諡曰昭公，元帝賜諡曰元。

translations.literal: Privately he was posthumously titled Duke Zhao; Yuan Di granted the posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he was called Duke Zhao; Emperor Yuan gave him the posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 子駿，年幼，弟茂攝事。

translations.literal: His son Jun was young; younger brother Mao took charge of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Jun was a child, so his brother Zhang Mao took the reins.

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
