translations.idiomatic: The edition marks a break with a lone equals sign.

sentences.zh: 寔弟茂

translations.literal: Younger brother of Shi: Mao
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao, Zhang Shi’s younger brother

sentences.zh: =茂字成遜，虛靖好學，不以世利嬰心。

translations.literal: = Mao, courtesy name Chengxun, was empty and still, fond of learning, and did not let worldly profit entangle his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao, courtesy name Chengxun, lived plainly, loved books, and shunned gain.

sentences.zh: 建興初，南陽王保辟從事中郎，又薦為散騎侍郎、中壘將軍，皆不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianxing era Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao summoned him as an aide-de-camp; he also recommended him as cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general of the central rampart, but in neither case did he take office.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao summoned him as staff officer and recommended court posts; he declined all.

sentences.zh: 二年，徵為侍中，以父老固辭。

translations.literal: In the second year he was summoned as palace attendant but firmly declined on account of his father’s age.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he was called to be palace attendant but cited his father’s age and refused.

sentences.zh: 尋拜平西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named general who pacifies the west and inspector of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 太興三年，寔既遇害，州人推茂為大都督、太尉、涼州牧，茂不從，但受使持節、平西將軍、涼州牧。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taixing, after Shi had met murder, the people of the province urged Mao as grand governor, grand commandant, and governor of Liangzhou; Mao did not accept but took only the credentials, the title General Who Pacifies the West, and governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Shi’s murder the province offered Mao the grand governorship; he took only the staff and western pacification title.

sentences.zh: 乃誅閻沙及黨與數百人，赦其境內。

translations.literal: Thereupon he executed Yan Sha and several hundred of their faction and declared an amnesty within his borders.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Yan Sha’s clique by the hundreds and proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 復以兄子駿為撫軍將軍、武威太守、西平公。

translations.literal: He again appointed his elder brother’s son Jun as General Who Soothes the Army, grand administrator of Wuwei, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: He named his nephew Zhang Jun general who soothes the army, Wuwei governor, and duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，茂築靈鈞台，周輪八十餘堵，基高九仞。

translations.literal: After more than a year Mao built the Lingjun Terrace, more than eighty bays around its circuit, with a base nine ren high.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he began Lingjun Terrace—eighty bays around, nine ren high.

sentences.zh: 武陵人閻曾夜叩門呼曰：「武公遣我來，曰：何故勞百姓而築台乎？

translations.literal: A man of Wuling, Yan Zeng, knocked on the gate by night and shouted, ‘Duke Wu has sent me to say: why do you toil the people to build a terrace?
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zeng of Wuling beat the gate at night, claiming Duke Wu’s ghost asked why Mao burdened the people with a tower.

sentences.zh: 」姑臧令辛岩以曾妖妄，請殺之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Guzang, Xin Yan, because Zeng was a sorcerer, asked permission to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Xin Yan wanted Zeng executed as a fraud.

sentences.zh: 茂曰：「吾信勞人。

translations.literal: Mao said, ‘I truly have been toiling the people.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao admitted he had overworked the people.

sentences.zh: 曾稱先君之令，何謂妖乎！

translations.literal: Zeng invokes a command from my late father—what do you call sorcery in that!
translations.idiomatic: The voice cited my late brother—hardly mere witchcraft.”

sentences.zh: 」太府主簿馬魴諫曰：「今世駿未夷，唯當弘尚道素，不宜勞役崇飾台榭。

translations.literal: The chief clerk of the grand treasury Ma Fang remonstrated, saying, ‘In this age the fine horses of the enemy are not yet pacified; you ought to promote plain simplicity in the Way and ought not to labor corvée and exalt terrace and pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Fang urged him to forgo finery while enemies remained.

sentences.zh: 且比年以來，轉覺眾務日奢於往，每所經營，輕違雅度，實非士女所望於明公。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years one has gradually felt that public business grows more extravagant than before; each undertaking lightly departs from proper measure—this is truly not what gentlemen and ladies expect from you, sir.
translations.idiomatic: Lately every project grows more lavish and drifts from restraint—hardly what the people expect of you.

sentences.zh: 」茂曰：「吾過也，吾過也！

translations.literal: Mao said, ‘I have erred, I have erred!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao cried, “I was wrong—twice wrong!”

sentences.zh: 」命止作役。

translations.literal: He ordered the corvée work stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He halted construction.

sentences.zh: 明年，劉曜遣其將劉咸攻韓璞于冀城，呼延寔攻寧羌護軍陰鑒於桑壁。

translations.literal: The next year Liu Yao sent his general Liu Xian to attack Han Pu at Jicheng, and Hu Yan Shi to attack Colonel Who Pacifies the Qiang Yin Jian at Sangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Liu Yao’s Liu Xian besieged Han Pu at Jicheng while Hu Yan Shi struck Yin Jian at Sangbi.

sentences.zh: 臨洮人翟楷、石琮等逐令長，以縣應曜，河西大震。

translations.literal: The men of Lintao, Zhai Kai, Shi Cong, and others drove out the magistrates and opened their counties to Yao, and great panic shook the Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Kai and Shi Cong of Lintao expelled officials and surrendered counties to Liu Yao, terrifying the west.

sentences.zh: 參軍馬岌勸茂親征，長史氾禕怒曰：「亡國之人復欲幹亂大事，宜斬岌及安百姓。

translations.literal: Adjutant Ma Ji urged Mao to take the field in person; Chief Clerk Fan Yi angrily said, ‘Men of a lost state still wish to meddle in great affairs—they ought to behead Ma Ji to settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji urged a personal campaign; Fan Yi snarled that a ruined man’s counsel deserved death.

sentences.zh: 」岌曰：「氾公書生糟粕，刺舉近才，不惟國家大計。

translations.literal: Ma Ji said, ‘Lord Fan is dregs of the bookish sort, fit only for petty recommendation, never pondering the state’s great plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji retorted that Fan Yi was bookish pedantry, good for trivia, blind to strategy.

sentences.zh: 且朝廷旰食有年矣，今大賊自至，不煩遠師，遐爾之情，實系此州，事勢不可以不出。

translations.literal: Moreover the court has skipped meals for years; now the great bandit has come of himself—there is no need for a distant army—near and far, all hearts hang on this province; the situation cannot allow staying behind.
translations.idiomatic: The court has starved for years; the foe is at the gate—hope rests on Liangzhou, so the prince must ride out.

sentences.zh: 且宜立信勇之驗，以副秦隴之望。

translations.literal: Moreover you ought to establish proof of trust and courage to answer the hopes of Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Only a bold show of resolve can satisfy Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 」茂曰：「馬生之言得之矣。

translations.literal: Mao said, ‘What Ma Sheng says hits the mark.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao said Ma Ji was right.

sentences.zh: 」乃出次石頭。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out and encamped at Stone Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He marched and camped at Stone Ford.

sentences.zh: 茂謂參軍陳珍曰：「劉曜以乘勝之聲握三秦之銳，繕兵積年，士卒習戰，若以精騎奄克南安，席捲河外，長驅而至者，計將何出？

translations.literal: Mao said to Adjutant Chen Zhen, ‘Liu Yao, with the reputation of victory in hand, grasps the keen edge of the three Qin, has drilled troops and stored supplies for years, and his soldiers are practiced in war—if with picked cavalry he suddenly took Nan’an in a rush, rolled up everything beyond the Yellow River, and drove straight here, what plan would answer?
translations.idiomatic: He asked Chen Zhen how to meet Liu Yao if he swept from Nan’an.

sentences.zh: 」珍曰：「曜雖乘威怙眾，恩德未結於下，又其關東離貳，內患未除，精卒寡少，多是氐羌烏合之眾，終不能近舍關東之難，增隴上之戍，曠日持久與我爭衡也。

translations.literal: Chen Zhen said, ‘Though Yao rides on might and trusts to numbers, his grace has not yet bound those below; moreover east of the pass his followers are divided and inner troubles are not removed; crack troops are few and most are Di and Qiang thrown together—they cannot in the end neglect the troubles east of the pass to increase garrisons on Long, waste days and months, and vie with us for long.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen argued that Liu Yao’s host was divided, ill-supplied, and mostly tribal levies, unable to sustain a long duel on Long.

sentences.zh: 若二旬不退者，珍請為明公率弊卒數千以擒之。

translations.literal: If in twenty days he does not withdraw, Zhen begs to lead for you, sir, several thousand worn troops to capture him.
translations.idiomatic: If he lingers twenty days, Chen Zhen will take a few thousand tired men and seize him.

sentences.zh: 」茂大悅，以珍為平虜護軍，率卒騎一千八百救韓璞。

translations.literal: Mao was greatly pleased and appointed Zhen as Colonel Who Pacifies the Caitiffs, leading eighteen hundred foot and horse to relieve Han Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao made him colonel who pacifies the Caitiffs with eighteen hundred to relieve Han Pu.

sentences.zh: 曜陰欲引歸，聲言要先取隴西，然後回滅桑壁。

translations.literal: Yao secretly wished to withdraw but declared he would first take Longxi, then return to destroy Sangbi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao feigned a plan to take Longxi before crushing Sangbi.

sentences.zh: 珍募發氐羌之眾，擊曜走之，克復南安。

translations.literal: Zhen conscripted the hosts of Di and Qiang, attacked Yao, drove him off, and recovered Nan’an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen raised Di and Qiang auxiliaries, routed Liu Yao, and retook Nan’an.

sentences.zh: 茂深嘉之，拜折沖將軍。

translations.literal: Mao deeply praised him and appointed him General Who Breaks the Charge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao praised him and named him general who breaks the charge.

sentences.zh: 未幾，茂復大城姑臧，修靈鈞台，別駕吳紹諫曰：「伏惟修城築台，蓋是懲既往之事。

translations.literal: Before long Mao again greatly enlarged Guzang and repaired Lingjun Terrace; Chief Clerk Wu Shao remonstrated, saying, ‘I humbly reflect that repairing walls and building a terrace are meant to punish what happened before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Mao expanded Guzang and rebuilt the terrace; Wu Shao warned that fortifying recalled past trauma.

sentences.zh: 愚以為恩德未洽於近侍，雖處層樓，適所以疑諸下，徒見不安之意而失士民系托之本心，示怯弱之形，乖匡霸之勢。

translations.literal: In my foolish opinion your grace has not yet spread evenly among those close at hand; though you dwell in layered towers it only serves to make subordinates suspicious, shows them nothing but unease, loses the basic heart by which gentlemen and commoners entrust themselves to you, displays a look of timidity and weakness, and runs counter to the posture of one who would aid and hegemonize.
translations.idiomatic: Tower-building without kindness nearby only breeds mistrust, looks like fear, and undercuts true leadership.

sentences.zh: 遐方異境窺我之齷齱也，必有乘人之規。

translations.literal: Distant regions and strange lands spy on our petty faults and are sure to have designs to exploit others’ troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Distant enemies watch for weakness and will exploit any slip.

sentences.zh: 嘗願止役省勞，與下休息。

translations.literal: I have always wished to halt labor and ease toil so that those below may rest.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to spare the people and rest the realm.

sentences.zh: 而更興功動眾，百姓豈所望於明君哉！

translations.literal: Yet you again raise works and move the multitude—is this what the people expect of an enlightened lord!
translations.idiomatic: More corvée is not what people want from a wise ruler.”

sentences.zh: 」茂曰：「亡兄怛然失身於物。

translations.literal: Mao said, ‘My late elder brother perished suddenly among men.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao answered: “My brother died to treachery.

sentences.zh: 王公設險，武夫重閉，亦達人之至戒也。

translations.literal: The kingly founder sets defenses, and martial men double the gates—this too is the utmost warning of the enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: Sages built walls and warriors barred gates—that is prudence.

sentences.zh: 且忠臣義士豈不欲盡節義于亡兄哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, do loyal ministers and righteous knights not wish to exhaust their integrity toward my late elder brother?
translations.idiomatic: Would loyal men not die for my brother?

sentences.zh: 直以危機密發，雖有賁育之勇，無所復施。

translations.literal: Only because the crisis broke in secrecy, though they had the courage of Ben and Yu, there was nowhere to apply it.
translations.idiomatic: The blow came in secret; even heroes could not strike.

sentences.zh: 今事未靖，不可以拘系常言，以太平之理責人於迍邅之世。

translations.literal: Now affairs are not yet quiet; one cannot be bound by conventional sayings or demand of men, in a time of stumbling, the principles proper to an age of great peace.’
translations.idiomatic: While chaos lasts you cannot judge by peacetime rules.”

sentences.zh: 」紹無以對。

translations.literal: Shao had nothing with which to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shao fell silent.

sentences.zh: 茂雅有志節，能斷大事。

translations.literal: Mao was by nature high-minded and principled, able to decide great matters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao was resolute and decisive by nature.

sentences.zh: 涼州大姓賈摹，寔之妻弟也，勢傾西土。

translations.literal: Jia Mo of Liangzhou, a great clan and Shi’s brother-in-law by marriage, had influence that tilted the whole west.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo, Zhang Shi’s brother-in-law, dominated the great families of the west.

sentences.zh: 先是，謠曰：「手莫頭，圖涼州。

translations.literal: Earlier a ditty had said, ‘Do not lay your hand on your head—plotting Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A rhyme had warned: “Hands off your head if you mean to seize Liangzhou.”

sentences.zh: 」茂以為信，誘而殺之，於是豪右屏跡，威行涼域。

translations.literal: Mao believed it trustworthy, lured Mo in, and killed him; thereupon the powerful houses held their breath and his awe spread through the Liang domain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao took the omen literally, lured Jia Mo in, and executed him; the magnates fell silent and his terror ruled the west.

sentences.zh: 永昌初，茂使將軍韓璞率眾取隴西南安之地，以置秦州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongchang era Mao sent General Han Pu with a host to seize Nan’an in the southwest of Long and there establish Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongchang, Zhang Mao sent Han Pu to take Nan’an in Longxi and set up Qinzhou there.

sentences.zh: 卒，臨終，執駿手泣曰：「昔吾先人以孝友見稱。

translations.literal: When he died, at the end he grasped Jun’s hand and wept, saying, ‘In former times my ancestors were praised for filial piety and fraternal harmony.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he took Zhang Jun’s hand and wept: “Our forebears were famed for filial love and brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 自漢初以來，世執忠順。

translations.literal: Since the beginning of the Han they have generation after generation held to loyalty and obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Since early Han every generation has been loyal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今雖華夏大亂，皇輿播遷，汝當謹守人臣之節，無或失墜。

translations.literal: Now although the central states are in great chaos and the imperial carriage has been driven about, you must strictly keep the deportment of a minister of state and let nothing slip.
translations.idiomatic: Though China reels and the court wanders, you must hold fast to every duty of a subject.

sentences.zh: 吾遭擾攘之運，承先人餘德，假攝此州，以全性命，上欲不負晉室，下欲保完百姓。

translations.literal: I have met a time of turmoil, inherited the remaining virtue of my ancestors, and on borrowed authority governed this province to preserve lives—above wishing not to betray the house of Jin, below wishing to keep the common people whole.
translations.idiomatic: I seized this post in chaos to save lives—loyal to Jin above, protective of the people below.

sentences.zh: 然官非王命，位由私議，苟以集事，豈榮之哉！

translations.literal: Yet my office was not by royal command, and my position arose from private counsel; I took it only to get things done—how could that be glory!
translations.idiomatic: My titles were never properly sealed from Luoyang—convenience, not honor.

sentences.zh: 氣絕之日，白帢入棺，無以朝服，以彰吾志焉。

translations.literal: On the day my breath fails, wrap me in a white kerchief for the coffin; do not use court dress—thus to make plain my intent.’
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in a white headcloth, not court robes—that states my mind.”

sentences.zh: 」年四十八。

translations.literal: He was forty-eight years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 在位五年。

translations.literal: He had occupied the position five years.
translations.idiomatic: He held power five years.

sentences.zh: 私諡曰成。

translations.literal: Privately he was posthumously titled Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he was styled “Accomplished.”

sentences.zh: 茂無子，駿嗣位。

translations.literal: Mao had no sons; Jun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao left no son, so Zhang Jun inherited.

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
translations.idiomatic: The edition inserts a lone equals sign as a section marker.

sentences.zh: 茂兄子駿

translations.literal: Elder brother’s son of Mao: Jun
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, nephew of Zhang Mao

sentences.zh: =駿字公庭，幼而奇偉。

translations.literal: = Jun, courtesy name Gongting, was extraordinary and grand in youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, courtesy name Gongting, was a striking boy.

sentences.zh: ，封霸城侯。

translations.literal: (The line continues) he was enfeoffed Marquis of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as marquis of Baling.

sentences.zh: 十歲能屬文，卓越不羈，而淫縱過度，常夜微行於邑裏，國中化之，及統任，年十八。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose essays; he was outstanding and unrestrained, yet dissolute and excessive, often going out by night incognito in the towns, and the whole state imitated him; when he took overall command he was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote verse at ten, was brilliant and wild, caroused by night, set a fashion for the realm, and took full power at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 先是，湣帝使人黃門侍郎史淑在姑臧，左長史泛禕、右長史馬謨等諷淑，令拜駿使持節、大都督、大將軍、涼州牧、領護羌校尉西平公。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Min had sent Palace Attendant Shi Shu to Guzang; left chief clerk Fan Yi, right chief clerk Ma Mo, and others persuaded Shu to invest Jun with the credentials, as grand governor, grand general, governor of Liangzhou, concurrent Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min’s envoy Shi Shu was maneuvered by Fan Yi and Ma Mo into formally appointing Zhang Jun with the staff, grand governorship, generalship, Liangzhou governorship, Qiang colonelcy, and ducal title.

sentences.zh: 赦其境內，置左右前後四率官，繕南宮。

translations.literal: He declared an amnesty within his borders, established the four commands of left, right, front, and rear guards, and repaired the Southern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied the province, set up four guard commands, and rebuilt the southern palace.

sentences.zh: 劉曜又使人拜駿涼州牧、涼王。

translations.literal: Liu Yao again sent someone to appoint Jun as governor of Liangzhou and King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao’s envoys also named him Liangzhou governor and king of Liang.

sentences.zh: 時辛晏兵於枹罕，駿宴群僚於閑豫堂。

translations.literal: At that time Xin Yan had raised troops at Fuhan; Jun feasted his host of officials in the Hall of Leisure and Ease.
translations.idiomatic: While Xin Yan held Fuhan, Zhang Jun feasted his staff in the Hall of Leisure.

sentences.zh: 命竇濤等進討辛晏。

translations.literal: He ordered Dou Tao and others to advance and punish Xin Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Dou Tao against Xin Yan.

sentences.zh: 從事劉慶諫曰：「霸王不以喜怒興師，不以幹沒取勝，必須天時人事，然後起也。

translations.literal: Aide Liu Qing remonstrated, saying, ‘Overlords do not raise armies from pleasure or anger, nor do they seek victory from greed; they must wait for heaven’s season and human affairs, then act.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing urged: “True hegemons never march on whim or greed; they wait for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 辛晏父子安忍凶狂，其亡可待，奈何以饑年大舉，猛寒攻城！

translations.literal: The father and son Xin Yan endure cruelty and are frenzied with violence; their destruction can be awaited—why in a year of famine launch a great campaign and in bitter cold assault walled cities!
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yan and his son are vicious; they will ruin themselves—why waste a famine winter on storming walls.

sentences.zh: 昔周武回戈以須亡殷之期，曹公緩袁氏使自斃，何獨殿下以旋兵為恥乎！

translations.literal: Of old King Wu of Zhou turned back his spears to await the date when Yin would perish; Duke Cao slowed the Yuans and let them destroy themselves—why must you, sir, alone be ashamed to wheel your army back!’
translations.idiomatic: King Wu waited for Shang to rot; Cao Cao let the Yuans collapse—withdrawal is no disgrace.”

sentences.zh: 」駿納之。

translations.literal: Jun accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun took the advice.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍王騭聘于劉曜，曜謂之曰：「貴州必欲追蹤竇融，款誠和好，卿能保之乎？

translations.literal: He sent adjutant Wang Zhi on a mission to Liu Yao; Yao said to him, ‘Your province surely wishes to follow Dou Rong’s track, treat in good faith, and be friendly—can you guarantee it?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun sent Wang Zhi to Liu Yao, who asked whether Liangzhou could truly match Dou Rong’s loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」騭曰：「不能。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi said, ‘I cannot.’
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi answered no.

sentences.zh: 」曜侍中徐邈曰：「君來和同，而雲不能，何也？

translations.literal: Yao’s palace attendant Xu Miao said, ‘You have come to harmonize yet say you cannot—why?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao asked why an envoy of peace refused a guarantee.

sentences.zh: 」騭曰：「齊桓貫澤之盟，憂心兢兢，諸侯不召自至。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi said, ‘At Duke Huan of Qi’s covenant at Guanze he was anxious and fearful, and the feudal lords came without being summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi cited Duke Huan’s humble covenant at Guanze, when lords gathered unbidden.

sentences.zh: 葵丘之會，驕而矜誕，叛者九國。

translations.literal: At the meeting at Kuiqiu he was arrogant and boastful, and nine states rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At Kuiqiu his pride lost him nine allies.

sentences.zh: 趙國之化，常如今日可也，若政教陵遲，尚未能察邇者之變，況鄙州乎！

translations.literal: If Zhao’s transforming influence always stays as today, it can be so; if government and instruction decline, he will not yet be able to observe even changes close at hand—how much less your distant province!’
translations.idiomatic: If your rule stays this strong, peace holds; if it slips, neighbors will turn—let alone distant Liangzhou.”

sentences.zh: 」曜顧謂左右曰：「此涼州高士，使乎得人。

translations.literal: Yao looked at those to his left and right and said, ‘This is a lofty gentleman of Liangzhou—the mission has found the right man.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao told his court they had met a true spokesman from the west.

sentences.zh: 」禮而遣之。

translations.literal: He treated him with courtesy and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He honored Wang Zhi and let him depart.

sentences.zh: ，駿猶稱建興十二年，駿親耕藉田。

translations.literal: (The line continues) Jun still used the twelfth year of Jianxing; Jun personally plowed the field of the imperial plowing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun still dated documents Jianxing twelve and performed the sacred plowing rite.

sentences.zh: 尋承元帝崩問，駿大臨三日。

translations.literal: Soon he received news that Yuan Di had died; Jun observed grand mourning for three days.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Emperor Yuan had died, he mourned three days.

sentences.zh: 會有黃龍見於胥次之嘉泉，右長史氾禕言於駿曰：「案建興之年，是少帝始起之號。

translations.literal: A yellow dragon appeared at the auspicious spring beside Xuci; right chief clerk Fan Yi said to Jun, ‘According to reckoning, the Jianxing era name was the style that the young emperor first raised.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow dragon at Jiaquan prompted Fan Yi to argue that “Jianxing” belonged to the murdered boy emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝以凶終，理應改易。

translations.literal: The emperor met a violent end; by principle the name ought to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: That reign ended in murder, so the era name should change.

sentences.zh: 朝廷越在江南，音問隔絕，宜因龍改號，以章休征。

translations.literal: The court is far beyond the Yangzi and news is cut off; you ought to follow the dragon’s omen and change the era title to display auspicious response.’
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from the south, we should adopt a new era to match the omen.”

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 初，駿之立也，姑臧謠曰：「鴻從南來雀不驚，誰謂孤雛尾翅生，高舉六翮鳳皇鳴。

translations.literal: In the beginning, when Jun was first established, a ditty in Guzang said, ‘The wild goose comes from the south yet the sparrow is not startled; who says the lone chick’s tail has grown feathers—rising on six pinions, the phoenix cries.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun came to power a Guzang song spoke of a chick becoming a phoenix.

sentences.zh: 」至是而復收河南之地。

translations.literal: By then he again recovered the territory south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The rhyme foretold his recovery of Henan.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，駿遣武威太守竇濤、金城太守張閬、武興太守辛岩、揚烈將軍宋輯等率眾東會韓璞，攻討秦州諸郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianhe era Jun sent Grand Administrator of Wuwei Dou Tao, Grand Administrator of Jincheng Zhang Lang, Grand Administrator of Wuxing Xin Yan, General Who Displays Ferocity Song Ji, and others leading hosts east to join Han Pu in attacking and punishing the commanderies of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe he sent Dou Tao, Zhang Lang, Xin Yan, and Song Ji east to Han Pu to strike Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 曜遣其將劉胤來距，屯于狄道城。

translations.literal: Yao sent his general Liu Yin to oppose them; Yin encamped at Didao city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao sent Liu Yin to Didao.

sentences.zh: 韓璞進度沃幹嶺。

translations.literal: Han Pu advanced and crossed the Wogan Range.
translations.idiomatic: Han Pu crossed the Wogan ridge.

sentences.zh: 辛岩曰：「我握眾數萬，藉氐羌之銳，宜速戰以滅之，不可以久，久則變生。

translations.literal: Xin Yan said, ‘I hold several tens of thousands and rely on the keen edge of Di and Qiang; we ought to fight swiftly to destroy them and cannot prolong matters—if prolonged, change will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yan demanded a quick battle with Di and Qiang auxiliaries.

sentences.zh: 」璞曰：「自夏末以來，太白犯月，辰星逆行，白虹貫日，皆變之大者，不可以輕動。

translations.literal: Pu said, ‘Since late summer Venus has encroached on the moon, the morning star has moved retrograde, and a white rainbow pierced the sun—all are great portents and one must not move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Han Pu cited ill omens in sky: Venus, retrograde Mercury, white rainbow—ill to march.

sentences.zh: 輕動而不捷，為禍更深。

translations.literal: If one moves lightly and does not win, the disaster will be deeper.
translations.idiomatic: A rash defeat would cost even more.

sentences.zh: 吾將久而斃之。

translations.literal: I intend to wear them down over time and let them perish.
translations.idiomatic: He chose a long war of attrition.

sentences.zh: 且曜與石勒相攻，胤亦不能久也。

translations.literal: Moreover Yao and Shi Le are attacking each other; Yin likewise cannot hold out long.’
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao and Shi Le were at each other’s throats; Liu Yin could not last.

sentences.zh: 」積七十餘日，軍糧竭，遣辛岩督運于金城。

translations.literal: They stood opposed more than seventy days until army grain was exhausted; he sent Xin Yan to supervise transport from Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: After seventy days Han Pu sent Xin Yan for supplies.

sentences.zh: 胤聞之，大悅，謂其將士曰：「韓璞之眾十倍於吾，羌胡皆叛，不為之用。

translations.literal: When Yin heard this he was greatly pleased and said to his generals and soldiers, ‘Han Pu’s host is ten times ours, yet the Qiang and Hu have all rebelled and will not work for him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin thought Han Pu’s huge army was hollow because tribes had deserted.

sentences.zh: 吾糧廩將懸，難以持久。

translations.literal: Our granaries are nearly empty and it is hard to endure long.
translations.idiomatic: Yin’s own stores were low.

sentences.zh: 今虜分兵運糧，可謂天授吾也。

translations.literal: Now the enemy has divided troops to transport grain—Heaven grants this to us.
translations.idiomatic: Han Pu’s supply column was a heaven-sent chance.

sentences.zh: 若敗辛岩，璞等自潰。

translations.literal: If we defeat Xin Yan, Pu and the others will collapse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Break Xin Yan and Han Pu flees.

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，宜以死戰。

translations.literal: They are many and we few; we ought to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had fewer men and needed desperation.

sentences.zh: 戰而不捷，當無匹馬得還，宜厲爾戈矛，竭汝智力。

translations.literal: If we fight and do not win, not a single horse should return—sharpen your spears and exhaust your wits.’
translations.idiomatic: He ordered total commitment or annihilation.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸奮。

translations.literal: The host all swelled with zeal.
translations.idiomatic: The troops roared assent.

sentences.zh: 於是率騎三千，襲岩於沃幹嶺，敗之，璞軍遂潰，死者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led three thousand cavalry, raided Xin Yan at the Wogan Range, defeated him, and Pu’s army thereupon collapsed; more than twenty thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin ambushed Xin Yan, shattered Han Pu, and left twenty thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 面縛歸罪，駿曰：「孤之罪也，將軍何辱！

translations.literal: They came with bound hands to confess guilt; Jun said, ‘It is this solitary one’s fault—why should the generals suffer shame!
translations.idiomatic: Survivors bound themselves to surrender; Zhang Jun blamed himself, not his generals.

sentences.zh: 」皆赦之。

translations.literal: He pardoned them all.
translations.idiomatic: He forgave every officer.

sentences.zh: 胤乘勝追奔，濟河，攻陷令居，入據振武，河西大震。

translations.literal: Yin pursued the rout, crossed the Yellow River, captured Lingju, entered and occupied Zhenwu, and great panic shook the Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin crossed the river, took Lingju and Zhenwu, and terrified the west.

sentences.zh: 駿遣皇甫該禦之，赦其境內。

translations.literal: Jun sent Huangfu Gai to oppose him and declared an amnesty within the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun sent Huangfu Gai and proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 會劉曜東討石生，長安空虛。

translations.literal: Just then Liu Yao marched east to punish Shi Sheng, and Chang’an was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao left for Shi Sheng, leaving Chang’an weak.

sentences.zh: 大蒐講武，將襲秦雍，理曹郎中索詢諫曰：「曜雖東征，胤猶守本。

translations.literal: He held a great hunt and drilled arms, planning to raid Qin and Yong; bureau gentleman Suo Xun remonstrated, saying, ‘Though Yao has gone east, Yin still guards the root.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun staged a great hunt to strike Qin-Yong; Suo Xun warned that Liu Yin still held the rear.

sentences.zh: 險阻路遙，為主人甚易，胤若輕騎憑氐羌以距我省，則奔突難測；

translations.literal: The defiles are long and the road far; for a defender it is very easy; if Yin with light cavalry relies on Di and Qiang to screen us in the narrows, sudden charges will be hard to predict;
translations.idiomatic: Mountain passes favor the defender; Liu Yin could screen the narrows with tribal horse;

sentences.zh: 輟彼東合而逆戰者，則寇我未已。

translations.literal: if he breaks off his eastern union and turns to fight us, then the raiding against us will not cease.
translations.idiomatic: if he broke eastward pacts to face us, raids would never end.

sentences.zh: 頃年頻出，戎馬生郊，外有饑羸，內資虛耗，豈是殿下子物之謂邪！

translations.literal: In recent years you have repeatedly gone out; war horses foal in the suburbs; outside there is hunger and weakness, inside resources are drained—how is this what is called a lord cherishing his people!’
translations.idiomatic: Repeated campaigns had beggared horse and man—hardly humane rule.”

sentences.zh: 」駿曰：「每患忠言不獻，面從背違，吾政教缺然而莫我匡者。

translations.literal: Jun said, ‘I always worry that loyal words are not offered, that men assent to my face yet oppose behind my back, that my government and instruction are flawed yet none corrects me.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun welcomed blunt speech.

sentences.zh: 卿盡辭規諫，深副孤之望也。

translations.literal: You have exhausted remonstrance in speech; this deeply matches what this solitary one hoped.’
translations.idiomatic: Suo Xun’s candor matched his hopes.

sentences.zh: 」以羊酒禮之。

translations.literal: He treated him with courtesy of sheep and wine.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with sheep and wine.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國獻汗血馬、火浣布、犎牛、孔雀、巨象及諸珍異二百餘品。

translations.literal: The various states of the Western Regions presented sweat-blood horses, fire-washed cloth, humped cattle, peacocks, great elephants, and more than two hundred kinds of rare treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Western Regions kingdoms sent blood-sweat horses, asbestos cloth, zebu, peacocks, elephants, and over two hundred tribute curios.

sentences.zh: 四域長史李柏請擊叛將趙貞，為貞所敗。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Four Regions Li Bo asked permission to strike the rebel general Zhao Zhen and was defeated by Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bo of the frontier directorate attacked Zhao Zhen and lost.

sentences.zh: 議者以柏造謀致敗，請誅之。

translations.literal: Counselors held that Bo had devised the plan that led to defeat and asked to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: The court wanted Li Bo’s head for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 駿曰：「吾每以漢世宗之殺王恢，不如秦穆之赦孟明。

translations.literal: Jun said, ‘I always think that Shizong of Han’s killing Wang Hui was not as good as Duke Mu of Qin’s pardoning Meng Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun preferred Duke Mu’s pardon of Meng Ming to Han’s execution of Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 」竟以減死論，群心咸悅。

translations.literal: In the end he was sentenced to commute death; the hearts of the host were all pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bo’s death sentence was commuted and the army rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 駿觀兵新鄉，狩於北野，因討軻沒虜，破之。

translations.literal: Jun reviewed troops at Xinxing, hunted in the northern wilds, and thereupon attacked the Kemo barbarians, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled at Xinxing, hunted north, and crushed the Kemo tribes.

sentences.zh: 下令境中曰：「或鯀殛而禹興，芮誅而缺進，唐帝所以殄洪災，晉侯所以成五霸。

translations.literal: He issued an order within the borders saying, ‘Some when Gun was executed Yu arose; when Rui was put to death Que advanced—thereby the Tang emperor ended the great flood, and the marquis of Jin became one of the Five Overlords.
translations.idiomatic: He cited how punishing one man raised another—Yao and Jin hegemons did the same.

sentences.zh: 法律犯死罪，期親不得在朝。

translations.literal: By law those whose close kin commit capital crimes may not serve at court.
translations.idiomatic: Law barred kin of capital criminals from court.

sentences.zh: 今盡聽之，唯不宜內參宿衛耳。

translations.literal: Now all such are permitted, only they may not serve in the inner palace guard.’
translations.idiomatic: He waived that bar except for inner-palace duty.

sentences.zh: 」於是刑清國富，群僚勸駿稱涼王，領秦、涼二州牧，置公卿百官，如魏武、晉文故事。

translations.literal: Thereupon punishments were clear and the state grew rich; the host of officials urged Jun to style himself King of Liang, concurrently governor of Qin and Liang, to set up dukes and ministers and the hundred offices on the precedent of Cao Cao and Sima Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Peace and plenty led his staff to urge a Liang kingship with full bureaucracy like Cao Cao or Sima Zhao.

sentences.zh: 駿曰：「此非人臣所宜言也。

translations.literal: Jun said, ‘That is not what a minister of state ought to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun called that treasonous talk.

sentences.zh: 敢有言此者，罪在不赦。

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak thus shall be guilty without pardon.’
translations.idiomatic: Anyone proposing it would die.

sentences.zh: 」然境內皆稱之為王。

translations.literal: Yet within the borders all called him king.
translations.idiomatic: Still, everyone called him king.

sentences.zh: 群僚又請駿立世子，駿不從。

translations.literal: The host of officials again asked Jun to establish an heir apparent; Jun did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: They begged him to name an heir; he refused.

sentences.zh: 中堅將軍宋輯言於駿曰：「禮急儲君者，蓋重宗廟之故。

translations.literal: General of the Central Rampart Song Ji said to Jun, ‘The rites stress an heir apparent because the ancestral temples are weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Song Ji cited ritual: the heir secures the temples.

sentences.zh: 周成、漢昭立於繦褓，誠以國嗣不可曠，儲宮當素定也。

translations.literal: King Cheng and Emperor Zhao were established in swaddling clothes—truly because the state’s succession may not be left vacant and the heir’s palace ought to be fixed early.
translations.idiomatic: Infant emperors Cheng and Zhao showed that the line must never gape.

sentences.zh: 昔武王始有國，元王作儲君。

translations.literal: In former times when King Wu first had the state, the heir apparent was appointed at the outset.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu founded Zhou he named an heir the moment the state stood.

sentences.zh: 建興之初，先王在位，殿下正名統，況今社稷彌崇，聖躬介立，大業遂殷，繼貳闕然哉！

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianxing the late king held the position; you, sir, set straight the name and succession—how much more now that the altars of soil and grain are loftier, your sacred person stands alone, the great enterprise is abundant—yet the successor is still vacant!
translations.idiomatic: At Jianxing your father fixed the line—now the realm is greater and you stand alone, yet still no heir!

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為國有累卵之危，而殿下以為安逾泰山，非所謂也。

translations.literal: I humbly think the state has the danger of piled eggs, yet you, sir, think it safer than Mount Tai—this is not what I would call right.’
translations.idiomatic: The state teeters like stacked eggs; to call it safe as Tai is wrong.”

sentences.zh: 」駿納之，遂立子重華為世子。

translations.literal: Jun accepted this and thereupon established his son Chonghua as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun agreed and named Zhang Chonghua heir.

sentences.zh: 先是，駿遣傅穎假道於蜀，通表京師。

translations.literal: Earlier Jun had sent Fu Ying to borrow a road through Shu to deliver a memorial to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He had sent Fu Ying through Shu to reach Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 李雄弗許。

translations.literal: Li Xiong would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong refused passage.

sentences.zh: 駿又遣治中從事張淳稱籓於蜀，托以假道焉。

translations.literal: Jun again sent headquarters aide Zhang Chun to declare himself a vassal of Shu, using that as a pretext to borrow the road.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Chun to submit to Cheng Han as cover for transit.

sentences.zh: 雄大悅。

translations.literal: Xiong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 雄又有憾于南氐楊初，淳因說曰：「南氐無狀，屢為邊害，宜先討百頃，次平上珪。

translations.literal: Xiong also harbored resentment toward Yang Chu of the southern Di; Chun thereupon urged, saying, ‘The southern Di behave intolerably and repeatedly harm the border; you ought first to punish Baiqing, then pacify Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun played on Li Xiong’s grudge against Yang Chu, urging a strike on Baiqing then Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 二國並勢，席捲三秦，東清許洛，掃氛燕趙，拯二帝梓宮於平陽，反皇輿於洛邑，此英霸之舉，千載一時。

translations.literal: With the two states’ combined power you can roll up the three Qin, clear Xu and Luo to the east, sweep miasma from Yan and Zhao, recover the two emperors’ coffins from Pingyang, and return the imperial carriage to Luoyang—this is a heroic hegemon’s deed, a chance in a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: United, Liang and Shu could sweep Guanzhong, free the east, recover the emperors’ coffins, and restore Luoyang—a once-in-an-age feat.

sentences.zh: 寡君所以遣下臣冒險通誠，不遠萬里者，以陛下義聲遠播，必能湣寡君勤王之志。

translations.literal: The reason my lord has sent his low servant to brave danger and communicate sincerity, not shrinking from ten thousand li, is that your majesty’s righteous fame spreads far and you are sure to pity my lord’s zeal in serving the king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun said his master crossed perils because Li Xiong’s virtue would honor Jin’s loyalists.

sentences.zh: 天下之善一也，惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: The good of all under heaven is one—may your majesty ponder it.’
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness is one under heaven—consider it.”

sentences.zh: 」雄怒，偽許之，將覆淳於東峽。

translations.literal: Xiong was angry, falsely granted it, and planned to destroy Chun in the eastern gorges.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong feigned consent and meant to kill Zhang Chun in the eastern defiles.

sentences.zh: 蜀人橋贊密以告淳。

translations.literal: A man of Shu, Qiao Zan, secretly informed Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zan of Shu secretly warned Zhang Chun.

sentences.zh: 淳言於雄曰：「寡君使小臣行無跡之地、通百蠻之域、萬里表誠者，誠以陛下義矜戮力之臣，能成人之美節故也。

translations.literal: Chun said to Xiong, "My lord sent your servant to walk trackless ground and pass through the realm of the hundred barbarians, to declare sincerity across ten thousand li—truly because Your Majesty in righteousness pities ministers who exhaust their strength and can complete the fine integrity of others."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun told Li Xiong that his master had sent him through deadly wilds solely because Li Xiong was known to honor steadfast servants.

sentences.zh: 若欲殺臣者，當顯於都市，宣示眾目，雲涼州不忘舊義，通使琅邪，為表忠誠，假途於我，主聖臣明，發覺殺之。

translations.literal: If you wish to kill your servant, you ought to do it openly in the capital market, display it before the multitude’s eyes, declare that Liangzhou does not forget old duty, that envoys were sent to Langye to show loyalty, that they borrowed a road through us, that lord is sage and ministers enlightened, and that on discovery he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: If Li Xiong meant to kill him, he should do it publicly so all would see Liangzhou’s loyalty to Jin and Li Xiong’s justice—or the deed would win no glory.

sentences.zh: 當令義聲遠著，天下畏威。

translations.literal: Then righteous fame will spread far and all under heaven will fear your majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Open execution would spread righteous awe across the realm.

sentences.zh: 今盜殺江中，威刑不顯，何足以揚休烈，示天下也！

translations.literal: Now to murder him secretly on the river—your awesome punishment is not displayed; how could that suffice to raise glorious merit and show all under heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: A secret killing on the river would prove nothing to the world.

sentences.zh: 」雄大驚曰：「安有此邪！

translations.literal: Xiong was greatly startled and said, "How could there be such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong feigned shock and swore he would never do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 當相放還河右耳。

translations.literal: I shall certainly send him back across the river to the right bank."
translations.idiomatic: He promised safe conduct back to Hexi.

sentences.zh: 」雄司隸校尉景騫言於雄曰：「張淳壯士，宜留任之。

translations.literal: Xiong’s metropolitan commandant Jing Qian said to Xiong, "Zhang Chun is a stalwart; you ought to retain and employ him."
translations.idiomatic: His officer Jing Qian urged him to keep the talented envoy; Li Xiong refused.

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「壯士豈為人留，且可以卿意觀之。

translations.literal: Xiong said, "A stalwart is not kept by other men; moreover you may observe him as you think fit."
translations.idiomatic: He said a true stalwart could not be bought and told Jing Qian to test Zhang Chun instead.

sentences.zh: 」騫謂淳曰：「卿體大，暑熱，可且遣下吏，少住須涼。

translations.literal: Qian said to Chun, "Your frame is large and the heat is fierce; you may for the moment send down a subordinate clerk and stay a little until it is cool."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Qing invited Zhang Chun to rest and send a subordinate in the heat.

sentences.zh: 」淳曰：「寡君以皇輿幽辱，梓宮未反，天下之恥未雪，蒼生之命倒懸，故遣淳來，表誠大國。

translations.literal: Chun said, "Because the imperial carriage is in shame and disgrace, the coffins of the late emperors have not returned, the shame of all under heaven is not washed away, and the lives of the black-haired folk hang upside down, my lord therefore sent Chun to declare sincerity to a great state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun replied that Jin’s humiliation and unburied emperors drove his mission—weighty business no clerk could carry.

sentences.zh: 所論事重，非下吏能傳。

translations.literal: The matters discussed weighty; they are not what a subordinate clerk can transmit.
translations.idiomatic: If a clerk sufficed, he would not have come; he would cross fire or flood, let alone summer heat.

sentences.zh: 若下吏所了者，則淳本亦不來，雖有火山湯海，無所辭難，豈寒暑之足避哉！

translations.literal: If what subordinate clerks could settle, then Chun would originally not have come; though there were volcanoes and seas of boiling water, I would not decline the hardship—how could mere heat and cold be worth avoiding!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong conceded Zhang Chun was incorruptible and unusable against Jin.

sentences.zh: 」雄曰：「此人矯矯，不可得用也。

translations.literal: Xiong said, "This man stands tall and straight; he cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Chun home with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 」厚禮遣之。

translations.literal: He treated him generously and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong asked why Zhang Jun did not declare himself emperor in his stronghold.

sentences.zh: 謂淳曰：「貴主英名蓋世，土險兵盛，何不稱帝，自娛一方？

translations.literal: He said to Chun, "Your noble lord’s heroic name covers the age; his land is perilous and his soldiers strong—why does he not style himself emperor and amuse himself in one quarter?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun answered that Zhang Jun served Jin from grandfather to father, ate bitterness for the throne, and backed Sima Rui like Duke Huan, not for private amusement.

sentences.zh: 」淳曰：「寡君以乃祖乃父世濟忠良，未能雪天人之大恥，解眾庶之倒懸，日昃忘食，枕戈待旦。

translations.literal: Chun said, "My lord because from grandfather to father for generations they have aided loyal good men, yet have been unable to wash away the great shame of heaven and man, to release the multitude who hang upside down, forgets food at sunset and sleeps on his spear awaiting dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong flushed and admitted his own ancestors had been Jin subjects who fled west; if Sima Rui restored the north, he would help.

sentences.zh: 以琅邪中興江東，故萬里翼戴，將成桓文之事，何言自娛邪！

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Langye has raised the house east of the Yangzi, therefore across ten thousand li he wings and supports him, intending to accomplish the deeds of Huan and Wen—what talk of amusing oneself!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun returned, raised troops, and got messages through to Jiankang; the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 」雄有慚色，曰：「我乃祖乃父亦是晉臣，往與六郡避難此都，為同盟所推，遂有今日。

translations.literal: Xiong had a shamefaced look and said, "My grandfather and father were also ministers of Jin; in former times together with the six commanderies they fled disaster to this capital, were pushed by the covenant of allies, and thus came to today.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun debated harsh laws; his staff approved.

sentences.zh: 琅邪若能中興大晉於中州者，亦當率眾輔之。

translations.literal: If the Prince of Langye can restore great Jin in the central plain, I too ought to lead the host and assist him."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Bin alone objected.

sentences.zh: 」淳還至龍鶴，募兵通表，後皆達京師，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: When Chun returned to Longhe, he recruited soldiers and sent memorials; afterward all reached the capital; the court praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun asked why.

sentences.zh: 駿議欲嚴刑峻制，眾咸以為宜。

translations.literal: Jun deliberated wishing to impose harsh laws and stern punishments; the multitude all thought it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Bin explained that law must bind high and low alike or it collapses.

sentences.zh: 參軍黃斌進曰：「臣未見其可。

translations.literal: Adjutant Huang Bin advanced and said, "Your servant has not yet seen that this can work."
translations.idiomatic: If nobles break rules, decrees mean nothing.

sentences.zh: 」駿問其故。

translations.literal: Jun asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun took the rebuke to heart and thanked him.

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「夫法制所以經綸邦國，篤俗齊物，既立民行，不可窪隆也。

translations.literal: Bin said, "Laws and regulations are what arrange the state, deepen custom, and level things; once the people’s conduct is set, it cannot be made high in one place and low in another.
translations.idiomatic: Without Huang Bin he would have missed his error.

sentences.zh: 若尊者犯令，則法不行矣。

translations.literal: If the honored violate the order, then the law cannot be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: He called Huang Bin the soul of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」駿屏機改容曰：「夫法唯上行，制無高下。

translations.literal: Jun pushed aside his armrest and changed countenance, saying, "The law applies only from above; regulation knows no high or low.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Huang Bin to Dunhuang governor on the spot.

sentences.zh: 且微黃君，吾不聞過矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, were it not for Lord Huang, I would not have heard my fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun reformed, worked tirelessly, and earned the nickname “the gatherer of worthies.”

sentences.zh: 黃君可謂忠之至也。

translations.literal: Lord Huang may be called loyal in the extreme."
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Gui’s day Liangzhou had known endless war.

sentences.zh: 」于坐擢為敦煌太守。

translations.literal: At the sitting he promoted him to be grand administrator of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Jun the province finally knew peace.

sentences.zh: 駿有計略，於是厲操改節，勤修庶政，總禦文武，咸得其用，遠近嘉詠，號曰積賢君。

translations.literal: Jun had stratagems; thereupon he sharpened his conduct and changed his style, diligently cultivated myriad government affairs, and commanded civil and military men so all found their use; far and near praised and sang of him, calling him the lord who piled up worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yang Xuan across the sands; Qiuci and Shanshan submitted, bringing the Tarim basin to heel.

sentences.zh: 自軌據涼州，屬天下之亂，所在征伐，軍無寧歲。

translations.literal: From the time Gui held Liangzhou, because all under heaven was in chaos, wherever there was campaigning the army knew no year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanshan king sent a “Beauty”; Zhang Jun built a pavilion for her.

sentences.zh: 至駿，境內漸平。

translations.literal: Down to Jun, within the borders gradually became calm.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqi and Khotan sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 又使其將楊宣率眾越流沙，伐龜茲、鄯善，於是西域並降。

translations.literal: He also sent his general Yang Xuan leading a host across the drifting sands to attack Qiuci and Shanshan; thereupon the entire Western Regions submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A river jade seal bore a prophecy of universal rule.

sentences.zh: 鄯善王元孟獻女，號曰美人，立賓遐觀以處之。

translations.literal: The king of Shanshan, Yuan Meng, presented a daughter styled the Beauty; he built the Guest-from-Afar View to house her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun controlled Longxi and fielded a strong army while still nominally serving Jin without adopting the southern calendar.

sentences.zh: 焉耆前部、于闐王並遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: The forward division of Yanqi and the king of Khotan both sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: He used royal ritual—six rows of dancers, leopard-tail banners, and a bureaucracy aping the throne under slightly altered titles.

sentences.zh: 得玉璽于河，其文曰「執萬國，建無極。」

translations.literal: He obtained a jade seal in the Yellow River whose inscription read, "He holds the myriad states and establishes boundlessness."
translations.idiomatic: He carved out Shazhou in the west and Hezhou in the east.

sentences.zh: 時駿盡有隴西之地，士馬強盛，雖稱臣于晉，而不行中興正朔。

translations.literal: At that time Jun held all the territory of Longxi; soldiers and horses were strong; although he called himself a subject of Jin, he did not use the restored court’s standard calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Both administrations styled themselves ministers to him.

sentences.zh: 舞六佾，建豹尾，所置官僚府寺擬于王者，而微異其名。

translations.literal: He danced the six rows of dancers, set up leopard-tail banners, and the officials and offices he established modeled the king’s, only slightly differing in their names.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the Qian Guang Palace complex south of Guzang, gilded and painted in five colors.

sentences.zh: 又分州西界三郡置沙州，東界六郡置河州。

translations.literal: He also split off three commanderies on the west of the province to establish Shazhou, and six commanderies on the east to establish Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Four seasonal halls—green east, red south, white west, black north—matched robes and gear to each season.

sentences.zh: 二府官僚莫不稱臣。

translations.literal: The officials of the two administrations all styled themselves ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He spent spring in the green hall, summer in the red, autumn in the white, winter in the black.

sentences.zh: 又于姑臧城南築城，起謙光殿，畫以五色，飾以金玉，窮盡珍巧。

translations.literal: He also south of Guzang built a wall and raised the Palace of Humble Radiance, painted in the five colors, ornamented with gold and jade, exhausting every rare and cunning art.
translations.idiomatic: Each hall had offices dyed to match its season.

sentences.zh: 殿之四面各起一殿，東曰宜陽青殿，以春三月居之，章服器物皆依方色；

translations.literal: On each of the four sides of the hall he raised a hall: east was called Xuanyang, the Green Hall, where he dwelt in the third month of spring, and robes and utensils all matched the quarter’s color;
translations.idiomatic: In old age he ignored the seasonal rotation and lived where he pleased.

sentences.zh: 南曰硃陽赤殿，夏三月居之；

translations.literal: south was called Zhuyang, the Red Hall, where he dwelt the third month of summer;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe he moved Nan’an families to Guzang for safety and reopened ties with Cheng Han.

sentences.zh: 西曰政刑白殿，秋三月居之；

translations.literal: west was called Zhengxing, the White Hall, where he dwelt the third month of autumn;
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao stormed Fuhan, Han Pu and Xin Yan were crushed at Lintao; Liu Yin chased them past the river and Zhang Jun lost Henan again.

sentences.zh: 北曰玄武黑殿，冬三月居之。

translations.literal: north was called Xuanwu, the Black Hall, where he dwelt the third month of winter.
translations.idiomatic: He later conquered Zhao Zhen and annexed his territory as Gaochang commandery.

sentences.zh: 其傍皆有直省內官寺署，一同方色。

translations.literal: Beside each were straight offices and inner bureaus, all matching the quarter’s color.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Le killed Liu Yao, Zhang Jun exploited Chang’an’s chaos to retake Henan to Didao and set five border garrisons against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 及末年，任所遊處，不復依四時而居。

translations.literal: In his last years, wherever he roamed and dwelt, he no longer followed the four seasons in choosing halls.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le’s investiture envoys were detained until Zhang Jun briefly submitted out of fear.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，懼為劉曜所逼，使將軍宋輯、魏纂將徙隴西南安人二千餘家于姑臧，使聘于李雄，修鄰好。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianhe, fearing pressure from Liu Yao, he sent generals Song Ji and Wei Zuan to move more than two thousand households of Nan’an in Longxi to Guzang, sent envoys to Li Xiong, and repaired neighborly friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, market director Tan Xiang wanted to lend granary grain at triple repayment after harvest.

sentences.zh: 及曜工攻枹罕，護軍辛晏告急，駿使韓璞、辛岩率步騎二萬擊之，戰於臨洮，大為曜軍所敗，璞等退走，追至令居，駿遂失河南之地。

translations.literal: When Yao attacked Fuhan in force, Protector Xin Yan reported urgent distress; Jun sent Han Pu and Xin Yan with twenty thousand foot and horse to strike him; they fought at Lintao and were greatly defeated by Yao’s army; Pu and the others retreated in flight, were pursued to Lingju, and Jun thereupon lost the territory south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ju cited classical examples against profiteering from hunger.

sentences.zh: 初，戊己校尉趙貞不附於駿，至是，駿擊擒之，以其地為高昌郡。

translations.literal: In the beginning Colonel of the Garrison of Wu and Ji Zhao Zhen had not submitted to Jun; at this point Jun attacked, captured him, and made his territory Gaochang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ximen Bao and Xie Bian illustrated wise granary policy.

sentences.zh: 及石勒殺劉曜，駿因長安亂，復收河南地，至於狄道，置武衛、石門、候和、漒川、甘松五屯護軍，與勒分境。

translations.literal: When Shi Le killed Liu Yao, Jun because Chang’an was in chaos again recovered Henan territory as far as Didao, established the five garrison protectors of Wuwei, Shimen, Houhe, Qiangchuan, and Gansong, and divided the border with Le.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Wen judged merit and fault fairly.

sentences.zh: 勒遣使拜駿官爵，駿不受，留其使。

translations.literal: Le sent envoys to invest Jun with office and rank; Jun did not accept and detained his envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Xiang’s scheme would strip the people like flipping a fur inside out.

sentences.zh: 後懼勒強，遣使稱臣於勒，兼貢方物，遣其使歸。

translations.literal: Later fearing Le’s strength, he sent envoys declaring himself Le’s subject while also presenting local products, and sent Le’s envoys back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun accepted Yin Ju’s advice.

sentences.zh: 駿境內嘗大饑，穀價踴貴，市長譚詳請出倉谷與百姓，秋收三倍征之。

translations.literal: Within Jun’s borders there was once a great famine; grain prices leaped; market director Tan Xiang asked to release granary grain to the common people and after autumn harvest levy three times the amount in return.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Geng Fang had long urged the court to notify Liangzhou of Jin’s restoration.

sentences.zh: 從事陰據諫曰：「昔西門豹宰鄴，積之於人；

translations.literal: Aide Yin Ju remonstrated, saying, "In olden times Ximen Bao governed Ye and stored grain in the people;
translations.idiomatic: Civil war delayed the mission.

sentences.zh: 解扁蒞東封之邑，計三倍。

translations.literal: Xie Bian took charge of the eastern border town and reckoned a threefold return.
translations.idiomatic: The court finally commissioned Geng Fang with twelve aides to carry the edict west.

sentences.zh: 文侯以豹有罪而可賞，扁有功而可罰。

translations.literal: Marquis Wen of Wei thought Bao guilty yet praiseworthy, and Bian meritorious yet punishable.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years in Liangzhou passed before the road cleared enough to recall him.

sentences.zh: 今詳欲因人之饑，以要三倍，反裘傷皮，未足喻之。

translations.literal: Now Xiang wishes to exploit people’s hunger to demand threefold return—reversing the fur injures the skin is not enough to compare."
translations.idiomatic: He passed the edict to Jia Ling disguised as a merchant.

sentences.zh: 」駿納之。

translations.literal: Jun accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Ling crept west by stages.

sentences.zh: 初，建興中，敦煌計吏耿訪到長安，既而遇賊，不得反，奔漢中，因東渡江，乙太興二年至京都，屢上書，以本州未知中興，宜遣大使，乞為鄉導。

translations.literal: In the beginning, in the Jianxing era, Dunhuang clerk Geng Fang reached Chang’an, then met bandits and could not return; he fled to Hanzhong, crossed the Yangzi eastward, and in the second year of Taixing reached the capital; he repeatedly submitted memorials that his home province did not know of the restoration and ought to dispatch a great envoy, begging to serve as guide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun received the imperial patent, sent Wang Feng to thank the throne, returned Jia Ling, acknowledged Jin as suzerain, yet still dated documents Jianxing twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 時連有內難，許而未行。

translations.literal: At that time troubles followed one another within the court; they granted it but did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted again by memorial through Geng Fang.

sentences.zh: 至是，始以訪守治書御史，拜駿鎮西大將軍，校尉、刺史、公如故，選西方人隴西賈陵等十二人配之。

translations.literal: At this point they first appointed Fang acting imperial secretary and invested Jun as Grand General Who Garrisons the West; colonel, inspector, and duke as before, and chose twelve western men including Jia Ling of Longxi to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions thereafter ran yearly.

sentences.zh: 訪停梁州七年，以驛道不通，召還。

translations.literal: Fang stayed in Liangzhou seven years; because the post road was not open, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Hu’s memorial began by lamenting how long Liangzhou had been cut off from the south.

sentences.zh: 訪以詔書付賈陵，托為賈客。

translations.literal: Fang handed the edict to Jia Ling, entrusting him to pose as a merchant.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled his undying loyalty to the Jin court despite the distance.

sentences.zh: 到長安，不敢進，以始達涼州。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang’an he did not dare advance, and only then reached Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of the throne’s silence toward the northwest and broken alliances.

sentences.zh: 駿受詔，遣部曲督王豐等報謝，並遣陵歸，上疏稱臣，而不奉正朔，猶稱建興二十一年。

translations.literal: Jun received the edict, sent troop commander Wang Feng and others to return thanks, and also sent Ling back; he submitted a memorial declaring himself subject but did not adopt the standard calendar, still calling it the twenty-first year of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the edict naming him grand general over four provinces moved him to tears of joy and grief.

sentences.zh: 九年，復使訪隨豐等齎印板進駿大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again sent Fang with Feng and others carrying seals to advance Jun to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to repay such grace and hold the frontier for the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲使命不絕。

translations.literal: From this time envoys every year were uninterrupted.
translations.idiomatic: He praised the emperor’s talents yet mourned the ruined temples and tombs.

sentences.zh: 後駿遣參軍麹護上疏曰：

translations.literal: Later Jun sent adjutant Qu Hu to submit a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: He restated his duty as regional commander with power of life and death out to Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 東西隔塞，逾歷年載，夙承聖德，心系本朝。

translations.literal: East and west are blocked and separated, passing years on end; long I have received sagely virtue and my heart ties to the capital court.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that with Shi Le and Li Xiong gone, traitors such as Shi Hu and Li Qi should have fallen quickly, yet usurpation continued year after year.

sentences.zh: 而江吳寂蔑，餘波莫及，雖肆力修塗，同盟靡恤。

translations.literal: Yet the Jiang and Wu region is silent and remote; the lingering wave cannot reach; though I exhaust strength on the road, the covenant allies show no pity.
translations.idiomatic: He deplored how vast distances left loyalists isolated while petty rebels flourished like grain borers.

sentences.zh: 奉詔之日，悲喜交並，天恩光被，褒崇輝渥，即以臣為大將軍、都督陝西雍秦涼州諸軍事。

translations.literal: On the day I received the edict, joy and grief crossed; Heaven’s grace shines on me, glorious favor heaps high, and at once your subject was made grand general and area commander of Shaanxi, Yong, Qin, and Liang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the patent, he felt joy and grief together, awed that grace should raise him to grand general over Shaanxi, Yong, Qin, and Liang.

sentences.zh: 休寵振赫，萬里懷戴，嘉命顯至，銜感屏營。

translations.literal: The rest and favor shake brilliance; ten thousand li cherish and support; the gracious command shone forth and I bore gratitude in awe.
translations.idiomatic: The favor shone far; all within ten thousand li looked up in loyalty; the gracious order dazzled him and he trembled with gratitude.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下天挺岐嶷，堂構晉室，遭家不造，播幸吳楚，宗廟有《黍離》之哀，園陵有殄廢之痛，普天咨嗟，含氣悲傷。

translations.literal: I bow my head: Your Majesty is heaven-endowed with keen intelligence and builds the house of Jin; meeting ill fortune in the family, you wander in Wu and Chu; the ancestral temples have the sorrow of Millet’s Odes, the park tombs the pain of ruin; all under heaven sighs and every breathing creature grieves.
translations.idiomatic: He extolled the emperor’s sagely gifts yet mourned the ancestral temples’ Millet Odes sorrow and the ruined imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 臣專命一方，職在斧鉞，遐域僻陋，勢極秦隴。

translations.literal: Your subject holds sole command in one quarter; my office is the axe and halberd; the distant region is remote and crude, my strength ends at Qin and Long.
translations.idiomatic: He pledged the axe of command to hold the far west for the throne, his power reaching only to Qin and Long.

sentences.zh: 勒雄既死，人懷反正，謂季龍、李期之命曾不崇朝，而皆篡繼凶逆，鴟目有年。

translations.literal: Le and Xiong are dead and men cherish return to rectitude; I thought Ji Hu and Li Qi’s fate would not last a morning, yet both usurped succession, cruel and rebellious, owl-eyed for years.
translations.idiomatic: With Shi Le and Li Xiong gone, he had hoped Shi Hu and Li Qi would fall in a morning, yet both usurped the line and glared like owls for years.

sentences.zh: 東西遼曠，聲援不接，遂使桃蟲鼓翼，四夷喧嘩，向義之徒更思背誕，鉛刀有幹將之志，螢燭希日月之光。

translations.literal: East and west stretch boundlessly and voice and aid do not connect, so the peach-borer beats its wings and the four barbarians clamor; those who faced righteousness now think of turning back; lead knives aspire to the keenness of Ganjiang, fireflies hope for sun and moon light.
translations.idiomatic: East and west lay too far apart for aid, so grain borers beat their wings, barbarians clamored, wavering loyalists thought of rebellion, and lead knives dreamed of being Ganjiang.

sentences.zh: 是以臣前章懇切，欲齊力時討。

translations.literal: Therefore your servant’s earlier memorial was earnest, wishing to join strength and strike in season.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore his earlier memorial had pleaded earnestly for a joint, timely strike.

sentences.zh: 而陛下雍容江表，坐觀禍敗，懷目前之安，替四祖之業，馳檄佈告，徒設空文，臣所以宵吟荒漠，痛心長路者也。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty at ease south of the Yangzi sits watching calamity and defeat, cherishing peace before your eyes and casting aside the work of the four ancestors; proclamations and notices are only empty writing—this is why your servant chants at night in the desert and grieves along the long road.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne dallied south of the Yangzi, watched disaster, clung to present peace, cast away the four ancestors’ work, and issued empty edicts—why he wailed nights on desert roads.

sentences.zh: 且兆庶離主，漸冉經世，先老消落，後生靡識，忠良受梟懸之罰，群凶貪縱橫之利，懷君戀故，日月告流。

translations.literal: Moreover the myriad common folk have left their lord; gradually a generation passes; the old die off and the young know nothing; the loyal and good suffer owl-display punishment while villainous clans grasp profit in wanton license; longing for the lord and old home flows like sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The people had long lost their lord; elders died and youths knew no Jin; good men were executed while villains profited; memory of the old house ebbed like sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 雖時有尚義之士，畏逼首領，哀歎窮廬。

translations.literal: Though from time to time there are men who honor duty, they fear for their heads and wail in poor huts.
translations.idiomatic: Even men of honor, fearing for their heads, could only weep in hovels.

sentences.zh: 臣聞少康中興，由於一旅，光武嗣漢，眾不盈百，祀夏配天，不失舊物，況以荊揚栗悍，臣州突騎，吞噬遺羯，在於掌握哉！

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Shaokang’s restoration rose from one brigade, Guangwu continued Han with fewer than a hundred men, sacrificed to Xia and matched Heaven without losing the old inheritance—how much more with Jing and Yang fierce and your subject’s province’s shock cavalry, swallowing the remnant Jie, lies in the hollow of the hand!
translations.idiomatic: He cited Shaokang’s single brigade and Guangwu’s hundred men to show a tiny host can restore a dynasty—surely fierce Jing and Yang plus Liangzhou’s shock horse could devour the remnant Jie.

sentences.zh: 願陛下敷弘臣慮，永念先績，敕司空鑒、征西亮等泛舟江沔，使首尾俱至也。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to spread wide your servant’s thought, ever remember former merit, and order Minister of Works Jian and Grand General Who Conquers the West Liang to float boats on the Jiang and Mian so head and tail may both arrive."
translations.idiomatic: He begged the emperor to widen his plan, remember past merit, and order Yu Liang’s hosts onto the Jiang and Mian so both ends of the realm could strike together.

sentences.zh: 自後駿遣使多為季龍所獲，不達。

translations.literal: Afterward Jun’s envoys were mostly taken by Ji Hu and did not get through.
translations.idiomatic: After that, Zhang Jun’s envoys were often captured by Shi Hu and never arrived.

sentences.zh: 後駿又遣護羌參軍陳宇、從事徐虓、華馭等至京師，征西大將軍亮上疏言陳宇等冒險遠至，宜蒙銓敘，詔除寓西平相，虓等為縣令。

translations.literal: Later Jun again sent Colonel aide Chen Yu, aides Xu Xiao and Hua Yu and others to the capital; Grand General Who Conquers the West Liang submitted a memorial saying Chen Yu and the others braved danger to come from afar and ought to receive appointments; an edict appointed Yu west-ping minister and Xiao and the others county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Jun sent Chen Yu, Xu Xiao, and Hua Yu to the capital; Yu Liang memorialized their perilous journey and won them appointments as west-ping minister and county magistrates.

sentences.zh: ，以世子重華為五官中郎將、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: (The line continues) he appointed heir apparent Chonghua as General of the Gentlemen of the Household for All Purposes and inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He named crown prince Zhang Chonghua general of the gentlemen of the household for all purposes and inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 酒泉太守馬岌上言：「酒泉南山，即昆侖之體也。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Jiuquan Ma Ji submitted a memorial saying, "The southern mountain of Jiuquan is the body of Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji began a memorial claiming Jiuquan’s southern mountain was the body of Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 周穆王見西王母，樂而忘歸，即謂此山。

translations.literal: King Mu of Zhou saw the Queen Mother of the West, rejoiced and forgot to return—he meant this mountain.
translations.idiomatic: King Mu of Zhou met the Queen Mother of the West there and lingered, forgetting to return—that was this peak.

sentences.zh: 此山有石室玉堂，珠璣鏤飾，煥若神宮。

translations.literal: This mountain has stone chambers and jade halls, pearls and carvings dazzling like a spirit palace.
translations.idiomatic: He described jeweled caverns on the mountain.

sentences.zh: 宜立西王母祠，以裨朝廷無疆之福。

translations.literal: It is fitting to establish a shrine to the Queen Mother of the West to add boundless blessing to the court."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to build a shrine for boundless blessing.

sentences.zh: 」駿從之。

translations.literal: Jun followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun approved and built the shrine.

sentences.zh: 駿在位二十二年卒，時年四十，私諡曰文公，穆帝追諡曰忠成公。

translations.literal: Jun died in the twenty-second year of his reign at the age of forty; privately he was titled Duke Wen; Emperor Mu posthumously titled him Duke Zhongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun died at forty after twenty-two years in power; private posthumous title Wen; Emperor Mu later styled him Zhongcheng.

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
translations.idiomatic: The edition inserts a lone equals sign as a section marker.

sentences.zh: 駿子重華

translations.literal: Son of Jun: Chonghua
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua, Zhang Jun’s heir

sentences.zh: =重華字泰臨，駿之第二子也。

translations.literal: = Chonghua, courtesy name Tailin, was Jun’s second son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua, courtesy name Tailin, was the second son.

sentences.zh: 寬和懿重，沈毅少言。

translations.literal: He was generous, mild, stately, and weighty, deep and resolute and seldom speaking.
translations.idiomatic: He was gentle, grave, and taciturn.

sentences.zh: 父卒，時年十六。

translations.literal: When his father died he was sixteen years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixteen when his father died.

sentences.zh: 以自稱持節、大都督、太尉、護羌校尉、涼州牧、西平公、假涼王，赦其境內。

translations.literal: He thereupon styled himself bearer of credentials, grand governor, grand commandant, Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, governor of Liangzhou, Duke of Xiping, and acting King of Liang, and declared an amnesty within his borders.
translations.idiomatic: He assumed the staff, grand governorship, grand commandant, Qiang colonelcy, Liangzhou shepherd, ducal title, and acting kingship of Liang, then amnestied the province.

sentences.zh: 尊其母嚴氏為太王太后，居永訓宮；

translations.literal: He honored his mother Lady Yan as grand king dowager, dwelling in the Yongxun Palace;
translations.idiomatic: He elevated Lady Yan to grand queen dowager in Yongxun Palace.

sentences.zh: 所生母馬氏為王太后，居永壽宮。

translations.literal: His birth mother Lady Ma was made queen dowager, dwelling in the Yongshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He elevated his mother Lady Ma to queen dowager in Yongshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 輕賦斂，除關稅，省園囿，以恤貧窮。

translations.literal: He lightened taxes and levies, abolished transit duties, reduced park and garden expenses, and thereby gave relief to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua cut taxes, lifted tolls, shrank court parks, and steered relief to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 遣使奉章于石季龍。

translations.literal: He sent envoys presenting a memorial to Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched a memorial to Shi Hu, styled Jilong.

sentences.zh: 季龍使王擢、麻秋、孫伏都等侵寇不輟。

translations.literal: Jilong sent Wang Zhuo, Ma Qiu, Sun Fudu, and others to raid and invade without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu answered with Wang Zhuo, Ma Qiu, and Sun Fudu in relentless border raids.

sentences.zh: 金城太守張沖降於秋。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Jincheng Zhang Chong surrendered to Ma Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng’s Zhang Chong went over to Ma Qiu.

sentences.zh: 於是涼州振動。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liangzhou was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept the province.

sentences.zh: 重華掃境內，使其征南將軍裴恆禦之。

translations.literal: Chonghua swept the territory within his borders and sent his General Who Conquers the South Pei Heng to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua mobilized the province and sent Pei Heng, general who conquers the south, to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 恆壁于廣武，欲以持久弊之。

translations.literal: Heng walled at Guangwu, intending by long delay to wear the enemy down.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Heng fortified Guangwu, planning to exhaust the foe by stalemate.

sentences.zh: 牧府相司馬張耽言于重華曰：「臣聞國以兵為強，以將為主。

translations.literal: Marshal of the shepherd’s headquarters Zhang Dan said to Chonghua, ‘Your servant has heard that the state is strong through arms and rests on its generals.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Zhang Dan told him: “A state’s strength is its army; its heart is its generals.

sentences.zh: 主將者，存亡之機，吉凶所系。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief is the pivot of survival or loss, to which good and ill attach.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commander decides whether the realm stands or falls.

sentences.zh: 故燕任樂毅，克平全齊，及任騎劫，喪七十城之地。

translations.literal: Therefore Yan employed Yue Yi and was able to pacify all Qi; when it employed Qi Jia, it lost seventy cities.
translations.idiomatic: Yan used Yue Yi and conquered Qi; with Qi Jia it lost seventy towns.

sentences.zh: 是以古之明君靡不慎於將相也。

translations.literal: Thus enlightened kings of old were never careless in choosing generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wise kings always picked commanders with care.

sentences.zh: 今之所要，在於軍師。

translations.literal: What matters now is the army’s strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Today the crucial post is chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 然議者舉將多推宿舊，未必妙盡精才也。

translations.literal: Yet those who debate raising generals mostly push aged veterans, not necessarily men who exhaust the finest talent.
translations.idiomatic: Counselors keep naming old faces who may not be the best talents.

sentences.zh: 且韓信之舉，非舊名也；

translations.literal: Moreover Han Xin’s elevation was not an old reputation;
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin had no prior fame when taken up;

sentences.zh: 穰宜之信，非舊將也；

translations.literal: Rang Ju’s trust was not an old general;
translations.idiomatic: Rang Ju was no longtime commander when trusted;

sentences.zh: 呂蒙之進，非舊勳也；

translations.literal: Lü Meng’s promotion was not for old merit;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng was not promoted for past laurels;

sentences.zh: 魏延之用，非舊德也。

translations.literal: Wei Yan’s use was not for old virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yan was not chosen for old kindness.

sentences.zh: 蓋明王之舉，舉無常人，才之所能，則授以大事。

translations.literal: In general the enlightened king’s choice has no fixed person—wherever talent reaches, there he entrusts the great task.
translations.idiomatic: Great kings assign great tasks purely on talent.

sentences.zh: 今強寇在郊，諸將不進，人情騷動，危機稍逼。

translations.literal: Now a strong foe presses the border; the generals do not advance; popular feeling is restless and crisis draws near.
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy at the gate and armies idle, the people panicked.

sentences.zh: 主簿謝艾，兼資文武，明識兵略，若授以斧鉞，委以專征，必能折沖禦侮，殲殄凶類。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Xie Ai combines civil and martial gifts, understands strategy—if you give him the axe and halberd and entrust him with sole command, he is sure to break charges, repel insult, and wipe out the villains.’
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Xie Ai, both scholar and soldier, could shatter the invasion if given independent command.”

sentences.zh: 」重華召艾，問以討寇方略。

translations.literal: Chonghua summoned Ai and asked him for plans to punish the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua called Xie Ai in for a war plan.

sentences.zh: 艾曰：「昔耿弇不欲以賊遺君父，黃權願以萬人當寇。

translations.literal: Ai said, ‘In olden times Geng Yan did not wish to leave bandits for his lord and father; Huang Quan was willing with ten thousand men to face the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai cited Geng Yan and Huang Quan’s zeal against rebels.

sentences.zh: 乞假臣兵七千，為殿下吞王擢、麻秋等。

translations.literal: I beg to borrow seven thousand troops for your highness to swallow Wang Zhuo, Ma Qiu, and the rest.’
translations.idiomatic: He asked for seven thousand men to destroy Wang Zhuo and Ma Qiu.”

sentences.zh: 」重華大悅，以艾為中堅將軍，配步騎五千擊秋。

translations.literal: Chonghua was greatly pleased, appointed Ai as General of the Central Rampart, and assigned him five thousand foot and horse to strike Ma Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua made him central-rampart general with five thousand to hit Ma Qiu.

sentences.zh: 引師出振武，夜有二梟鳴於牙中，艾曰：「梟，邀也，六博得梟者勝。

translations.literal: He led the army out from Zhenwu; at night two owls cried in the headquarters; Ai said, ‘The owl is “invite”; in the six sticks game he who throws the owl wins.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Zhenwu, two owls hooted in camp; Xie Ai called it a lucky omen like the owl token in liubo.

sentences.zh: 今梟鳴牙中，克敵之兆。

translations.literal: Now the owl cries in the headquarters—an omen of crushing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The owl at headquarters foretold victory.

sentences.zh: 」於是進戰，大破之，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced to battle, inflicted a great defeat, and beheaded five thousand ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked and routed them, taking five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 重華封艾為福祿伯，善待之。

translations.literal: Chonghua enfeoffed Ai as Earl of Fulu and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua ennobled him as count of Fulu and favored him.

sentences.zh: 諸寵貴惡其賢，共毀譖之，乃出為酒泉太守。

translations.literal: The various favorites hated his worth and together slandered him; he was therefore sent out as grand administrator of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Court favorites envied him and had him posted away to Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 季龍又令麻秋進陷大夏，大夏護軍梁式執太守宋晏，以城應秋。

translations.literal: Jilong again ordered Ma Qiu to advance and capture Daxia; Protector of Daxia Liang Shi seized Grand Administrator Song Yan and opened the city to Ma Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sent Ma Qiu to take Daxia; its protector seized the governor and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 秋遣晏以書誘宛戍都尉宋矩。

translations.literal: Qiu sent Yan with a letter to entice Garrison Commandant of Wanshu Song Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu used Song Yan to lure Wanshu’s commandant Song Ju.

sentences.zh: 宋矩謂秋曰：「辭父事君，當立功義；

translations.literal: Song Ju said to Ma Qiu, ‘Leaving father to serve a lord, one ought to establish merit and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Song Ju told Ma Qiu that serving a lord meant earning honor or dying with honor;
