sentences.zh: 功義不立，當守名節。

translations.literal: if merit and righteousness are not established, one ought to guard name and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: without achievement, a man still keeps his good name.

sentences.zh: 矩終不肯主偷生於世。

translations.literal: Ju will in the end not consent to live basely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He would not live in shame.

sentences.zh: 」於是先殺妻子，自刎而死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first killed wife and children, then cut his own throat and died.
translations.idiomatic: He slew his family and cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 是月，有司議遣司兵趙長迎秋西郊。

translations.literal: That month the offices debated sending Army Officer Zhao Chang to welcome Ma Qiu west of the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Officials proposed welcoming Ma Qiu outside the west gate.

sentences.zh: 謝艾以《春秋》之義，國有大喪，省蒐狩之禮，宜待逾年。

translations.literal: Xie Ai, citing the Spring and Autumn Annals’ meaning that when the state has great mourning hunting rites are reduced, said they ought to wait more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai cited the Annals: great mourning cancels hunts—wait a year.

sentences.zh: 別駕從事索遐議曰：「禮，天子崩，諸侯薨，末殯，五祀不行，既殯而行之。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Suo Xia argued, ‘By the rites, when the Son of Heaven dies the feudal lords wail—before the end of the fifth sacrifice, the five household sacrifices are not performed; after the end of wailing they are performed.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Xia argued ritual allowed the ceremony after burial.

sentences.zh: 魯宣三年，天王崩，不廢郊祀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duke Xuan of Lu the king of heaven died, yet suburban sacrifice was not halted.
translations.idiomatic: Lu kept suburban sacrifice when the Zhou king died.

sentences.zh: 今聖上統承大位，百揆惟新，宜在璿璣玉衡以齊七政。

translations.literal: Now the sage lord has inherited the great position and the hundred affairs are anew—it is fitting to align the seven powers with the jade armillary.
translations.idiomatic: The new ruler should align heaven and earth with the seven luminaries.

sentences.zh: 立秋，萬物將成，殺氣之始，其于王事，杖麾誓眾，釁鼓禮神，所以討逆除暴，成功濟務，寧宗廟社稷，致天下之福，不可廢也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of autumn the myriad things are about to mature; killing qi begins; for kingly affairs, leaning on the staff, swearing the host, smearing the drums and sacrificing to the spirits are how one punishes rebels, removes violence, completes merit, aids the task, quiets the altars of soil and grain, and brings blessing to all under heaven—it cannot be abandoned.’
translations.idiomatic: Autumn rites for war against rebels must proceed.”

sentences.zh: 」重華從之。

translations.literal: Chonghua followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua agreed.

sentences.zh: 俄而麻秋進攻枹罕，時晉陽太守郎坦以城大難守，宜棄外城。

translations.literal: Before long Ma Qiu advanced to attack Fuhan; at that time grand administrator of Jinyang Lang Tan thought the city too large to defend and that the outer wall ought to be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu besieged Fuhan; Lang Tan of Jinyang wanted to abandon the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 武城太守張悛曰：「棄外城則大事去矣，不可以動眾心。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Wucheng Zhang Quan said, ‘If we abandon the outer wall the great task is lost—it cannot be done without shaking the host’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan of Wucheng warned that yielding the outer wall would break morale.

sentences.zh: 」甯戎校尉張璩從之，固守大城。

translations.literal: Colonel Who Pacifies the Rong Zhang Qu followed this and firmly defended the great city.
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Zhang Qu agreed and held the main citadel.

sentences.zh: 秋率眾八萬，圍塹數重，雲梯雹車，地突百道，皆通於內。

translations.literal: Qiu led eighty thousand men, rings of trenches layer on layer, cloud ladders and hailstone carts, a hundred underground saps—all connected within.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu brought eighty thousand, trenches, ladders, siege towers, and saps.

sentences.zh: 城中亦應之，殺傷秋眾已數萬。

translations.literal: The city answered in kind and had already killed or wounded tens of thousands of Qiu’s men.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders killed tens of thousands of his troops.

sentences.zh: 季龍復遣其將劉渾等率步騎二萬會之。

translations.literal: Jilong again sent his general Liu Hun and others with twenty thousand foot and horse to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu reinforced him with Liu Hun and twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 郎坦恨言之不從，教軍士李嘉潛與秋通，引賊千餘人上城西北隅。

translations.literal: Lang Tan resented that his words were not followed and instructed the soldier Li Jia secretly to communicate with Ma Qiu, leading more than a thousand bandits onto the northwest corner of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tan betrayed the city, smuggling Ma Qiu’s men onto the wall.

sentences.zh: 璩使宋修、張弘、辛挹、郭普距之，短兵接戰，斬二百餘人，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Qu sent Song Xiu, Zhang Hong, Xin Yi, and Guo Pu to oppose them; fighting at close quarters they beheaded more than two hundred and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qu’s officers drove the breach force back, killing two hundred.

sentences.zh: 璩戮李嘉以徇，燒其攻具。

translations.literal: Qu executed Li Jia as a warning and burned the assault engines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qu executed Li Jia and torched the siege gear.

sentences.zh: 秋退保大夏，謂諸將曰：「我用兵於五都之間，攻城掠地，往無不捷。

translations.literal: Qiu withdrew to hold Daxia and said to his generals, ‘I have used troops among the five capitals, stormed cities and seized land—wherever I went there was no failure.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu boasted of past invincibility across the heartland.

sentences.zh: 及登秦隴，謂有征無戰。

translations.literal: When I mounted Qin and Long I thought there would be expeditions without battles.
translations.idiomatic: He had expected the northwest to fall easily.

sentences.zh: 豈悟南襲仇池，破軍殺將；

translations.literal: Who would have thought that striking south at Chouchi I would break armies and lose generals;
translations.idiomatic: Southward at Chouchi he had lost generals;

sentences.zh: 築城長最，匹馬不歸；

translations.literal: that building the wall at Changzui not a single horse returned;
translations.idiomatic: at Changzui not one horse came home;

sentences.zh: 及攻此城，傷兵挫銳。

translations.literal: and that attacking this city would wound soldiers and blunt keen edges.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhan had bloodied his veterans.

sentences.zh: 殆天所贊，非人力也。

translations.literal: This is almost Heaven’s aid, not human power.’
translations.idiomatic: He blamed Heaven, not his skill.

sentences.zh: 」季龍聞而歎曰：「吾以偏師定九州，今以九州之力困於枹罕，真所謂彼有人焉，未可圖也。」

translations.literal: When Jilong heard this he sighed and said, ‘I with a partial army settled the nine provinces; now with the strength of nine provinces I am exhausted at Fuhan—this is truly what they call “they have men there—it cannot be plotted against.”’
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu sighed that one good defender had stymied his whole empire.

sentences.zh: 重華以謝艾為使持節、軍師將軍，率步騎三萬，進軍臨河。

translations.literal: Chonghua appointed Xie Ai as bearer of credentials and Army Supervisor General, leading thirty thousand foot and horse to advance to the river.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua gave Xie Ai the staff as army supervisor with thirty thousand men to the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 秋以三萬眾距之。

translations.literal: Qiu opposed him with thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu met him with thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 艾乘軺車，冠白帢，鳴鼓而行。

translations.literal: Ai rode in a light cart, wore a white kerchief, and advanced beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai rode a light wagon in a white cap, drums rolling.

sentences.zh: 秋望而怒曰：「艾年少書生，冠服如此，輕我也。

translations.literal: Qiu saw from afar and angrily said, ‘Ai is a young student; such cap and dress—he despises me.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu raged that a young clerk in white was mocking him.

sentences.zh: 」命黑槊龍驤三千人馳擊之。

translations.literal: He ordered three thousand black-lance dragon chargers to gallop and strike them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent three thousand elite lancers to charge.

sentences.zh: 艾左右大擾。

translations.literal: Ai’s attendants were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai’s staff panicked.

sentences.zh: 左戰帥李偉勸艾乘馬，艾不從，乃下車踞胡床，指麾處分。

translations.literal: Left battle commander Li Wei urged Ai to mount a horse; Ai did not follow, but got down from the cart, sat cross-legged on a folding stool, and directed disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei begged him to mount; Xie Ai sat on a camp stool and commanded seated.

sentences.zh: 賊以為伏兵發也，懼不敢進。

translations.literal: The bandits thought ambush troops had sprung and feared to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The foe thought an ambush had fired and hesitated.

sentences.zh: 張瑁從左南緣河而截其後，秋軍乃退。

translations.literal: Zhang Mao from the left south followed the river and cut off their rear; Qiu’s army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mao swung from the left along the river and severed Ma Qiu’s retreat; Ma Qiu pulled back.

sentences.zh: 艾乘勝奔擊，遂大敗之，斬秋將杜勳、汲魚，俘斬一萬三級，秋匹馬奔大夏。

translations.literal: Ai pursued with victory and inflicted a great rout, beheading Qiu’s generals Du Xun and Ji Yu, capturing or beheading thirteen thousand ranks, and Qiu fled on a single horse to Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai routed him, slew Du Xun and Ji Yu, took thirteen thousand heads, and drove Ma Qiu alone to Daxia.

sentences.zh: 重華論功，以謝艾為太府左長史，進封福祿縣伯，邑五千戶，帛八千匹。

translations.literal: Chonghua assessed merit and appointed Xie Ai as left chief clerk of the grand treasury, advanced his fief to County Earl of Fulu with five thousand households and eight thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua raised him to left chief clerk of the grand treasury, count of Fulu with five thousand households and eight thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 麻秋又據枹罕，有眾十二萬，進屯河內，遣王擢略地晉興、廣武，越洪池嶺，至於曲柳，姑臧大震。

translations.literal: Ma Qiu again held Fuhan with a host of one hundred twenty thousand, advanced and encamped south of the river, sent Wang Zhuo to raid Jinxing and Guangwu, crossed Hongchi Ridge as far as Quwillow, and Guzang was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qiu massed one hundred twenty thousand, crossed toward Guzang, and raided deep toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 重華議欲親出距之，謝艾固諫以為不可。

translations.literal: Chonghua debated wishing to go out in person to oppose him; Xie Ai firmly remonstrated that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua meant to lead in person; Xie Ai forbade it.

sentences.zh: 別駕從事索遐進曰：「賊眾甚盛，漸逼京畿。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Suo Xia advanced and said, ‘The bandits are very numerous and gradually press the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Xia said the enemy was too strong for the prince to ride out.

sentences.zh: 君者，國之鎮也，不可以親動。

translations.literal: The lord is the state’s anchor—he cannot move in person.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler must not risk the field.

sentences.zh: 左長史謝艾，文武兼資，國之方邵，宜委以推轂之任。

translations.literal: Left chief clerk Xie Ai combines civil and martial gifts and is the state’s Fang and Shao—it is fitting to entrust him with the mission of pushing the chariot-shaft.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ai was the realm’s Fang and Shao—give him the army.

sentences.zh: 殿下居中作鎮，授以算略，小賊不足平也。

translations.literal: If your highness stays in the center as anchor and hands him stratagems, a small bandit is not enough to be worth pacifying.’
translations.idiomatic: Hold Guzang and let Xie Ai win the campaign.”

sentences.zh: 」重華納之，於是以艾為使持節、都督征討諸軍事、行衛將軍，遐為軍正將軍，率步騎二萬距之。

translations.literal: Chonghua accepted this; thereupon he appointed Ai as bearer of credentials, area commander of all military affairs on the punitive expedition, acting General Who Guards the Camp, Xia as General Who Corrects the Army, and led twenty thousand foot and horse to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua named Xie Ai expedition commander with twenty thousand men and Suo Xia as army corrector.

sentences.zh: 艾建牙旗，盟將士，有西北風吹旌旗東南指。

translations.literal: Ai raised the signal flag and swore the host; a northwest wind blew the banners so their points faced southeast.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Ai swore his host, a northwest wind snapped the flags southeast.

sentences.zh: 遐曰：「風為號令，今能令旗指之，天所贊也，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Xia said, ‘Wind is the signal; now it can make the banners point—Heaven approves; breaking them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Xia read the wind as Heaven’s omen of victory.

sentences.zh: 」軍次神鳥，王擢與前鋒戰，敗，遁還河南。

translations.literal: The army halted at Shenniao; Wang Zhuo fought the vanguard and was defeated, then fled back south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: At Shenniao, Wang Zhuo lost the van and fled to Henan.

sentences.zh: 還討叛虜斯骨真萬餘落，破之，斬首千餘級，俘擒二千八百，獲牛羊十餘萬頭。

translations.literal: Returning, he attacked the rebel barbarians Siguzhen’s more than ten thousand camps, defeated them, beheaded more than a thousand ranks, captured twenty-eight hundred, and took more than a hundred thousand head of cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He then crushed Siguzhen’s tribal camps, taking livestock and captives.

sentences.zh: 重華自以連破勍敵，頗怠政事，希接賓客。

translations.literal: Chonghua, because he had repeatedly broken mighty foes, slackened in government affairs and seldom received guests.
translations.idiomatic: Flush with victories, Zhang Chonghua neglected administration.

sentences.zh: 司直索遐諫曰：「殿下承四聖之基，當升平之會，荷當今之任，憂率土之塗炭。

translations.literal: Rectifier Suo Xia remonstrated, saying, ‘Your highness inherits the foundation of four sages, meets a time of rising peace, bears the duty of the age, and ought to worry for the black-haired folk smeared with ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Xia the rectifier urged him to shoulder the people’s woes.

sentences.zh: 宜躬親萬機，開延英乂，夙夜乾乾，勉於庶政。

translations.literal: You ought personally to attend the myriad threads, open the way to heroes, toil early and late, and strive in myriad government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He should rule dawn to dusk and court wise men.

sentences.zh: 自頃內外囂然，皆云去賊投誠者應即撫慰，而彌日不接。

translations.literal: Lately within and without there is uproar—all say that those who leave the bandits and come in good faith ought at once to be comforted, yet whole days pass without audience.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors waited days for an audience he never granted.

sentences.zh: 國老朝賢，當虛己引納，詢訪政事，比多經旬積朔，不留意接之。

translations.literal: The state’s elders and court worthies ought to be drawn in with empty seats and consulted on government affairs; lately many pass a month or more without your attending to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Elders languished unheard for months.

sentences.zh: 文奏入內，曆月不省，廢替見務，注情於棋弈之間，繾綣左右小臣之娛，不存將相遠大之謀。

translations.literal: Memorials enter the inner palace and go a month without review; business that should be seen to is cast aside while you fix your heart on chess and go and linger with petty attendants for amusement, not storing up the far-reaching plans of generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials piled unread while he played weiqi with favorites.

sentences.zh: 至使親臣不言，朝吏杜口，愚臣所以回惶忘寢與食也。

translations.literal: Down to making close ministers not speak and court clerks shut their mouths—this is why your foolish servant turns in anxiety and forgets sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Silence had fallen on honest officials—that was Suo Xia’s fear.

sentences.zh: 今王室如毀，百姓倒懸，正是殿下銜膽茹辛厲心之日。

translations.literal: Now the royal house is as if smashed and the common people hang upside down—this is truly the day when your highness ought to hold gall in the mouth and harden the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jin’s house was shattered; the moment called for bitter resolve.

sentences.zh: 深願垂心朝政，延納直言，周爰五美，以成六德，捐彼近習，弭塞外聲，修政聽朝，使下觀而化。

translations.literal: I deeply hope you will bend your heart to court government, extend acceptance to straight words, seek the five beauties everywhere, and complete the six virtues; cast aside those near favorites, stopper outside rumor, cultivate government and listen at court, so those below may look and be transformed.’
translations.idiomatic: He begged for open courts, straight speech, and an end to petty distractions.”

sentences.zh: 」重華覽之大悅，優文答謝，然不之改也。

translations.literal: Chonghua read it and was greatly pleased, answered with gracious text thanking him, yet did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua praised Suo Xia’s memorial but changed nothing.

sentences.zh: 詔遣侍御史俞歸拜重華護羌校尉、涼州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: An edict sent Attending Secretary Yu Gui to appoint Chonghua as Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, inspector of Liangzhou, and bearer of credentials.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Yu Gui to confirm his Qiang colonelcy, Liangzhou inspectorship, and staff.

sentences.zh: 是時石季龍西中郎將王擢屯結隴上，為苻雄所破，奔重華。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Jilong’s general of the gentlemen of the household on the west Wang Zhuo had entrenched on Long and was broken by Fu Xiong; he fled to Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo, beaten by Fu Xiong on Long, fled to Zhang Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 重華厚寵之，以為征虜將軍、秦州刺史、假節，使張弘、宗悠率步騎萬五千配擢，伐苻健。

translations.literal: Chonghua treated him generously, appointed him General Who Punishes the Caitiffs, inspector of Qinzhou, bearer of credentials, and had Zhang Hong and Zong You lead fifteen thousand foot and horse to reinforce Zhuo and attack Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua ennobled Wang Zhuo and sent Zhang Hong and Zong You with fifteen thousand to strike Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 健遣苻碩禦之，戰于龍黎。

translations.literal: Jian sent Fu Shuo to oppose them; they fought at Longli.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Fu Shuo to meet them at Longli.

sentences.zh: 擢等大敗，單騎而還，弘、悠皆沒。

translations.literal: Zhuo and the others were greatly defeated, returned on single horses, and Hong and You both perished.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo fled alone; Zhang Hong and Zong You died.

sentences.zh: 重華痛之，素服為戰亡吏士舉哀號慟，各遣吊問其家。

translations.literal: Chonghua grieved for them, put on white garments, and for the clerks and soldiers dead in battle raised lament and wailing, sending condolences separately to their families.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua wore white and mourned every fallen soldier, sending aid to their kin.

sentences.zh: 復授擢兵，使攻秦州，克之。

translations.literal: He again gave Zhuo troops and had him attack Qinzhou; he captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He rearmed Wang Zhuo, who then took Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣使上疏曰：「季龍自斃，遺燼遊魂，取亂侮亡，睹機則發。

translations.literal: He sent envoys submitting a memorial saying, ‘Jilong has destroyed himself; his remaining embers wander as ghosts—“take chaos and insult the doomed,” strike when the moment appears.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial declared Shi Hu dead and the remnant Zhao state ripe for attack.

sentences.zh: 臣今遣前都鋒督裴恆步騎七萬，遙出隴上，以俟聖朝赫然之威。

translations.literal: Your subject now sends former vanguard supervisor Pei Heng with seventy thousand foot and horse to emerge far on Long and await the sage court’s terrible majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He would march Pei Heng with seventy thousand onto Long to await Jin’s strike.

sentences.zh: 山東騷擾不足厝懷，長安膏腴，宜速平蕩。

translations.literal: Disturbance east of the mountains is not worth harboring in the heart; Chang’an is fat land and ought quickly to be swept clear.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed the Shandong turmoil as trivial and urged a swift strike on Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 臣守任西荒，山川悠遠，大誓六軍，不及聽受之末；

translations.literal: Your servant guards the assignment in the western wastes; mountains and rivers stretch far; the great oath of the six armies does not reach to the end of listening and receiving;
translations.idiomatic: The memorial continued: cut off on the frontier, he could not hear the court’s reply in time;

sentences.zh: 猛將鷹揚，不豫告成之次，瞻雲望日，孤憤義傷，彈劍慷慨，中情蘊結。

translations.literal: fierce generals soar like hawks and do not take part in the ranks that announce completion; gazing at clouds and sun, alone in indignant righteousness, I strike my sword in fervor and knot feeling within.
translations.idiomatic: His crack troops could not share Luoyang’s triumphs; he nursed private grief for Jin.

sentences.zh: 」於是康獻皇后詔報，遣使進重華為涼州牧。

translations.literal: Thereupon Empress Dowager Kangxian issued an edict in reply and sent envoys to advance Chonghua to governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Kangxian answered and promoted him to Liangzhou governor.

sentences.zh: 是時御史俞歸至涼州，重華方謀為涼王，不肯受詔，使親信人沈猛謂歸曰：「我家主公奕世忠於晉室，而不如鮮卑矣。

translations.literal: At that time Censor Yu Gui reached Liangzhou; Chonghua was plotting to become King of Liang and would not accept the edict; he sent his trusted man Shen Meng to say to Gui, ‘My family’s lord for generations has been loyal to the house of Jin—are we now worse than the Xianbei!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua refused the edict while plotting kingship and sent Shen Meng to bluster at Yu Gui.

sentences.zh: 台加慕容皝燕王，今甫授州主大將軍，何以加勸有功忠義之臣乎！

translations.literal: The terrace raised Murong Huang to Prince of Yan; now it has only just invested our lord as grand general—how does that encourage meritorious loyal ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Shen Meng complained that Murong Huang got a royal title while Zhang Chonghua only got general.

sentences.zh: 明台今宜移河右，共勸州主為涼王。

translations.literal: Sir, you ought now to cross to the west of the river and together urge our lord to be King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Yu Gui to cross the river and support a Liang kingship.

sentences.zh: 大夫出使，苟利社稷，專之可也。

translations.literal: When a great officer goes on mission, if it profits the altars of soil and grain, he may act on his own.’
translations.idiomatic: He cited the right of an envoy to improvise for the state’s good.”

sentences.zh: 」歸對曰：「王者之制，異姓不得稱王；

translations.literal: Gui replied, ‘By the kingly founder’s institutions, those not of the same surname may not be styled king;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gui replied that non-imperial kin could not be kings under Jin law;

sentences.zh: 九州之內，重爵不得過公。

translations.literal: within the nine provinces doubled nobility may not surpass duke.
translations.idiomatic: noble rank could not exceed duke inside the nine provinces.

sentences.zh: 漢高一時王異姓，尋皆誅滅，蓋權時之宜，非舊體也。

translations.literal: Gaozu of Han for a time enfeoffed kings of other surnames, but soon all were executed and destroyed—this was a measure for a moment, not the standing system.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu’s non-Liu kings were a temporary mistake quickly purged.

sentences.zh: 故王陵曰：'非劉氏而王，天下共伐之。

translations.literal: Therefore Wang Ling said, “Whoever is not surnamed Liu yet is king, all under heaven shall attack him.”
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Wang Ling’s oath against non-Liu kings.

sentences.zh: '至於戎狄，不從此例。

translations.literal: As for the Rong and Di, this rule does not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians were a separate case.

sentences.zh: 春秋時吳楚稱王，而諸侯不以為非者，蓋蠻夷畜之也。

translations.literal: In Spring and Autumn times Wu and Chu styled themselves kings yet the feudal lords did not think it wrong—because they were treated as barbarian stock.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Chu’s royal titles were tolerated as barbarian pretense.

sentences.zh: 假令齊魯稱王，諸侯豈不伐之！

translations.literal: Suppose Qi and Lu had styled themselves kings—would the feudal lords not have attacked them!
translations.idiomatic: Had Chinese states claimed kingship, allies would have crushed them.

sentences.zh: 故聖上以貴公忠賢，是以爵以上公，位以方伯，鮮卑北狄，豈足為比哉！

translations.literal: Therefore the sage lord, because your noble lord is loyal and worthy, therefore ennobles him as high duke and posts him as regional shepherd—the Xianbei northern Di, how can they be compared!
translations.idiomatic: Jin honored Zhang Chonghua as duke and shepherd—barbarian princes were no parallel.

sentences.zh: 子失問也。

translations.literal: You have asked wrongly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Gui dismissed the question.

sentences.zh: 且吾又聞之，有殊勳絕世者亦有不世之賞，若今便以貴公為王者，設貴公以河右之眾南平巴蜀，東掃趙魏，修復舊都，以迎天子，天子復以何爵何位可以加賞？

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that for those with extraordinary merit transcending the age there are also rewards that match no age—if now at once we made your noble lord king, suppose with the hosts west of the river he southward pacified Ba and Shu, eastward swept Zhao and Wei, repaired the old capital, and welcomed the Son of Heaven—what rank or position could the Son of Heaven add to reward that!
translations.idiomatic: He asked what higher title could Jin offer if Zhang Chonghua already took the throne and then reconquered the north.

sentences.zh: 幸三思之。

translations.literal: I hope you will think thrice.’
translations.idiomatic: He told Shen Meng to think again.”

sentences.zh: 」猛具宣歸言，重華遂止。

translations.literal: Meng reported Gui’s words in full; Chonghua thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Meng relayed Yu Gui’s logic and Zhang Chonghua dropped his claim.

sentences.zh: 重華好與群小遊戲，屢出錢帛以賜左右。

translations.literal: Chonghua loved to sport with petty followers and repeatedly issued cash and silk to reward those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua gambled and showered favorites with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 征事索振諫曰：「先王寢不安席，志平天下，故繕甲兵，積資實。

translations.literal: Retainer Suo Zhen remonstrated, saying, ‘The late king did not sleep on a secure mat, his aim was to pacify all under heaven; therefore he repaired armor and weapons and piled up supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Zhen reminded him his father had saved every coin for conquest.

sentences.zh: 大業未就，懷恨九泉。

translations.literal: The great enterprise was not completed and he cherished regret below the nine springs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun died with the north unconquered.

sentences.zh: 殿下遭巨寇於諒闇之中，賴重餌以挫勍敵。

translations.literal: Your highness met great bandits in the mourning shed and relied on heavy bait to break mighty foes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua had survived crisis with bribes and armies.

sentences.zh: 今遺燼尚廣，倉帑虛竭，金帛之費，所宜慎之。

translations.literal: Now remaining embers are still broad, the treasury is empty and exhausted—expense in gold and silk is what ought to be guarded.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury was bare; spending had to be restrained.

sentences.zh: 昔世祖即位，躬親萬機，章奉詣闕，報不終日，故能隆中興之業，定萬世之功。

translations.literal: In olden times when Shizu mounted the throne he personally attended the myriad threads; memorials that reached the palace gate were answered within the day—therefore he could raise the enterprise of restoration and settle merit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Guangwu’s instant replies to memorials.

sentences.zh: 今章奉停滯，動經時月，下情不得上達，哀窮困于囹圄，蓋非明主之事，臣竊未安。

translations.literal: Now memorials are stalled, often passing months; feeling below cannot ascend; the pitiable languish in prison—this is surely not an enlightened lord’s affair; your servant privately is uneasy.’
translations.idiomatic: Memorials now sat unread while innocents rotted in jail.”

sentences.zh: 」重華善之。

translations.literal: Chonghua praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chonghua praised Suo Zhen.

sentences.zh: 將受詔，未及而卒，時年二十七。

translations.literal: He was about to receive the edict but before it could happen he died, at the age of twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-seven before taking the new commission.

sentences.zh: 在位十一年。

translations.literal: He had occupied the position eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled eleven years.

sentences.zh: 私諡曰昭公，後改曰桓公，穆帝賜諡曰敬烈。

translations.literal: Privately he was titled Duke Zhao, later changed to Duke Huan; Emperor Mu granted the posthumous title Reverent and Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Private posthumous titles changed to Huan; Emperor Mu named him Jinglie.

sentences.zh: 子耀靈嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yaoling succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Yaoling inherited.

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
translations.idiomatic: The edition marks a section break with “=”.

sentences.zh: 重華子耀靈

translations.literal: Son of Chonghua: Yaoling
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaoling, Zhang Chonghua’s son

sentences.zh: =耀靈字元舒。

translations.literal: = Yaoling, courtesy name Yuanshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yaoling, courtesy name Yuanshu.

sentences.zh: 年十歲嗣事，稱大司馬、校尉、刺史、西平公。

translations.literal: At ten years of age he inherited the affairs, styling himself grand marshal, colonel, inspector, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: The boy ruler took titles as grand marshal and duke of Xiping at ten.

sentences.zh: 伯父長寧侯祚性傾巧，善承內外，初與重華寵臣趙長、尉緝等結異姓兄弟。

translations.literal: His uncle Marquis of Changning Zhang Zuo was by nature crafty, good at ingratiating himself within and without; in the beginning he formed sworn brotherhood with Chonghua’s favored ministers Zhao Chang and Wei Ji and others.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhang Zuo curried favor with Zhao Chang and Wei Ji.

sentences.zh: 長等矯稱重華遺令，以祚為持節、督中外諸軍、撫軍將軍，輔政。

translations.literal: Chang and others forged a claim to Chonghua’s dying order appointing Zuo as bearer of credentials, commander of all military affairs within and without, and General Who Soothes the Army, to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: They forged a will naming Zhang Zuo regent.

sentences.zh: 長待議以耀靈沖幼，時難未夷，宜立長君。

translations.literal: Chang awaited deliberation with the argument that Yaoling was young and the times’ troubles not yet pacified, and that it was fitting to establish the senior lord.
translations.idiomatic: They argued a child could not rule in wartime.

sentences.zh: 祚先烝重華母馬氏，馬氏遂從緝議，命廢耀靈為涼甯侯而立祚。

translations.literal: Zuo had first committed adultery with Chonghua’s mother Lady Ma; Lady Ma therefore followed Ji’s deliberation, ordering Yaoling deposed as Marquis of Liangning and Zuo set up instead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo had seized Lady Ma; she deposed her grandson for him.

sentences.zh: 祚尋使楊秋胡害耀靈于東苑，埋之於沙坑，私諡曰哀公。

translations.literal: Zuo soon sent Yang Qiuhu to murder Yaoling in the eastern park and buried him in a sand pit; privately he was titled Duke Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo had Zhang Yaoling murdered in the east park.

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
translations.idiomatic: Section marker in the edition.

sentences.zh: 耀靈伯父祚

translations.literal: Yaoling’s uncle by senior line: Zuo
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo, uncle of Zhang Yaoling

sentences.zh: =祚字太伯，博學雄武，有政事之才。

translations.literal: = Zuo, courtesy name Taibo, was broadly learned, heroic in arms, and had talent for government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo, courtesy name Taibo, was learned, martial, and politically capable.

sentences.zh: 既立，自稱大都督、大將軍、涼州牧、涼公。

translations.literal: Once established, he styled himself grand governor, grand general, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He took grand governor, general, Liangzhou governor, and duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 淫暴不道，又通重華妻裴氏，自閣內媵妾及駿、重華未嫁子女，無不暴亂，國人相目，咸賦《牆茨》之詩。

translations.literal: He was debauched and cruel without the Way, also debauched Chonghua’s wife Lady Pei, and from concubines within the harem down to Jun’s and Chonghua’s unmarried sons and daughters there was none he did not outrage—the people looked at one another and all composed poems on “The Tares on the Wall.”
translations.idiomatic: He raped kin including Zhang Chonghua’s widow and children, revolting the realm.

translations.literal: The source line carries only a full stop.
translations.idiomatic: The manuscript shows a stray period.

sentences.zh: 祚納尉緝、趙長等議，僭稱帝位，立宗廟，舞八佾，置百官，下書曰：「昔金行失馭，戎狄亂華，胡、羯、氐、羌咸懷竊璽。

translations.literal: Zuo accepted Wei Ji and Zhao Chang’s counsel, arrogated the imperial title, set up ancestral temples, danced the eight rows of dancers, established the hundred offices, and issued a rescript saying, ‘In olden days the metal element lost the reins and Rong and Di threw Huaxia into chaos; Hu, Jie, Di, and Qiang all coveted the stolen seal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo declared himself emperor with a long usurpation edict.

sentences.zh: 我武公以神武撥亂，保甯西夏，貢款勤王，旬朔不絕。

translations.literal: Our martial duke with divine arms put down chaos and guarded and pacified the western Xia, paying tribute and serving the king without ceasing for ten-day periods.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Zhang Gui’s loyal service to Jin.

sentences.zh: 四祖承光，忠誠彌著。

translations.literal: The four ancestors received his light and loyalty shone ever brighter.
translations.idiomatic: He listed Zhang successors’ loyalty.

sentences.zh: 往受晉禪，天下所知，謙沖遜讓，四十年於茲矣。

translations.literal: In former times he received abdication from Jin—all under heaven knows it—yet modestly yielded, and forty years have passed since.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed the Zhangs had once taken Jin’s abdication yet stayed humble.

sentences.zh: 今中原喪亂，華裔無主，群後僉以九州之望無所依歸，神祇嶽瀆罔所憑系，逼孤攝行大統，以一四海之心。

translations.literal: Now the central plain is lost in chaos and Huaxia lacks a lord; the host of lords unanimously deem the hope of the nine provinces to have nowhere to turn, gods and spirits of peaks and rivers to have nothing to rely on, and they press this solitary one to hold the great line in order to unify the hearts of all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned popular demand to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 辭不獲已，勉從群議。

translations.literal: I declined but could not obtain permission and have strained to follow the host of lords’ counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed reluctant acceptance.

sentences.zh: 待掃穢二京，蕩清周魏，然後迎帝舊都，謝罪天闕，思與兆庶，同茲更始。

translations.literal: When I have swept filth from the two capitals and cleansed Zhou and Wei, then I shall welcome the emperor to the old capital, confess guilt at Heaven’s gate, and wish together with the myriad common folk to renew ourselves on this day.’
translations.idiomatic: He promised to restore Jin after conquering the north.

sentences.zh: 」改建興四十二年為和平元年，赦殊死，賜鰥寡帛，加文武爵各一級，追崇曾祖軌為武王，祖寔為昭王，從祖茂為成王，父駿為文王，弟重華為明王。

translations.literal: He changed the forty-second year of Jianxing to the first year of Heping, granted amnesty short of capital crimes, bestowed silk on widowers and widows, raised civil and military rank one grade, posthumously honored great-grandfather Gui as King Wu, grandfather Shi as King Zhao, uncle Mao as King Cheng, father Jun as King Wen, and younger brother Chonghua as King Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the era Heping and piled royal posthumous titles on the Zhang line.

sentences.zh: 立妻辛氏為皇后，弟天錫為長寧王，子泰和為太子，庭堅為建康王，耀靈弟玄靚為涼武侯。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Xin as empress, younger brother Tianxi as Prince of Changning, son Taihe as heir apparent, Tingjian as Prince of Jiankang, and Yaoling’s younger brother Xuanjing as Marquis of Liangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He crowned his wife, ennobled kin, and named an heir.

sentences.zh: 其夜，天有光如車蓋，聲若雷霆，震動城邑。

translations.literal: That night heaven had light like a carriage canopy and a sound like thunder, shaking the city.
translations.idiomatic: Omens: a canopy of light and thunder over the city.

sentences.zh: 明日，大風拔木。

translations.literal: The next day a great wind uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: A gale tore up trees.

sentences.zh: 災異屢見，而祚凶虐愈甚。

translations.literal: Prodigies appeared again and again, yet Zuo’s ferocity grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Portents multiplied while Zhang Zuo grew crueller.

sentences.zh: 其尚書馬岌以切諫免官。

translations.literal: His Minister Ma Ji because of blunt remonstrance was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ma Ji lost office for speaking plainly.

sentences.zh: 郎中丁琪又諫曰：「先公累執忠節，遠宗吳會，持盈守謙，五十作載，蒼生所以鵠企西望，四海所以注心大涼，皇天垂贊，士庶效死者，正以先公道高彭昆，忠逾西伯，萬里通虔，任節不貳故也。

translations.literal: Gentleman consultant Ding Qi again remonstrated, saying, ‘The former lords repeatedly held loyal integrity, looked far to Wu and Yue, kept fullness and guarded modesty for nearly fifty years—why the black-haired folk crane-necks to gaze west and the four seas fix their hearts on great Liang, why High Heaven hangs blessing and gentry and commoners die in service, is solely because the former lords’ way towered above Peng and Kun, loyalty surpassed the western lords, sincerity reached ten thousand li, and duty never wavered.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Qi praised the Zhang line’s loyalty and warned against usurpation.

sentences.zh: 能以一州之眾抗崩天之虜，師徒歲起，人不告疲。

translations.literal: With one province’s host they resisted heaven-toppling foes; armies rose year after year yet the people did not complain of weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou had long held off invaders.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖以大聖雄姿纂戎鴻緒，勳德未高於先公，而行革命之事，臣竊未見其可。

translations.literal: Although your majesty with great sage heroic mien has inherited vast enterprise, merit and virtue are not yet higher than the former lords’ while you carry out “revolution”—your servant privately does not yet see that this can work.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo had not earned the right to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 華夷所以歸系大涼、義兵所以千里響赴者，以陛下為本朝之故。

translations.literal: The reason Huaxia ties itself to great Liang and righteous troops echo for a thousand li is that they take your majesty as still tied to this court.
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty had rested on nominal Jin service.

sentences.zh: 今既自尊，人斯高競，一隅之地何以當中國之師！

translations.literal: Now that you have exalted yourself, men will vie for height—how can one corner of land withstand the armies of the central state!
translations.idiomatic: Usurpation would invite Jin’s crushing response.

sentences.zh: 城峻沖生，負乘致寇，惟陛下圖之。

translations.literal: High walls breed collision; bearing treasure draws bandits—may your majesty ponder it.’
translations.idiomatic: He warned that pride invites attack.”

sentences.zh: 」祚大怒，斬之于闕下。

translations.literal: Zuo was greatly angry and beheaded him below the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo executed Ding Qi at the gate.

sentences.zh: 遣其將和昊率眾伐麗靬戎于南山，大敗而還。

translations.literal: He sent his general He Hao leading a host to attack the Ligian Rong in the southern mountains and returned after a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He Hao’s campaign against southern tribes failed.

sentences.zh: 太尉桓溫入關，王擢時鎮隴西，馳使於祚，言溫善用兵，勢在難測。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Huan Wen entered the passes; Wang Zhuo then garrisoned Longxi and sent a galloping messenger to Zuo, saying Wen was skilled in arms and his power hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo warned that Huan Wen was marching into Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 祚既震懼，又慮擢反噬，即召馬岌復位而與之謀。

translations.literal: Zuo was both shaken and fearful and also worried that Zhuo might turn and bite; he at once summoned Ma Ji back to office and plotted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo recalled Ma Ji, fearing Wang Zhuo might defect.

sentences.zh: 密遣親人刺擢，事覺，不克。

translations.literal: He secretly sent kin to assassinate Zhuo; the affair was discovered and did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The plot to murder Wang Zhuo failed.

sentences.zh: 祚益懼，大聚眾，聲言東征，實欲西保敦煌。

translations.literal: Zuo grew more fearful, greatly gathered hosts, declared an eastern expedition in words but in truth meant to flee west to secure Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned an eastward march to run for Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 會溫還而止。

translations.literal: Just then Wen returned and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen withdrew, so Zhang Zuo stayed.

sentences.zh: 更遣其平東將軍秦州刺史牛霸、司兵張芳率三千人擊擢，破之。

translations.literal: He again sent his General Who Pacifies the East and inspector of Qinzhou Niu Ba and Army Officer Zhang Fang with three thousand men to strike Zhuo and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Ba and Zhang Fang beat Wang Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 擢奔於苻健。

translations.literal: Zhuo fled to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuo fled to Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 其國中五月霜降，殺苗稼果實。

translations.literal: Within his state in the fifth month frost fell and killed seedlings, grain, and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: May frost in Liangzhou ruined the crops.

sentences.zh: 祚宗人張瓘時鎮枹罕，祚惡其強，遣其將易揣、張玲率步騎萬三千以襲之。

translations.literal: Zuo’s clansman Zhang Quan then garrisoned Fuhan; Zuo hated his strength and sent his generals Yi Chuai and Zhang Ling with thirteen thousand foot and horse to raid him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo sent Yi Chuai against kinsman Zhang Quan at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 時張掖人王鸞頗知神道，言於祚曰：「軍出不復還，涼國將有不利矣。

translations.literal: At that time a man of Zhangye, Wang Luan, knew something of the spirit way and said to Zuo, ‘The army will not return; Liang state will meet ill.’
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luan prophesied defeat.

sentences.zh: 」祚大怒，以鸞妖言沮眾，斬之以徇，三軍乃發。

translations.literal: Zuo was greatly angry, held that Luan’s sorcerer’s words discouraged the host, and beheaded him as a warning; only then did the three armies set out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo executed Wang Luan for dampening morale.

sentences.zh: 鸞臨刑曰：「我死不二十日，軍必敗。

translations.literal: Facing execution Luan said, ‘No more than twenty days after my death the army will be defeated.’
translations.idiomatic: Wang Luan predicted defeat within twenty days.

sentences.zh: 」時有神降於玄武殿，自稱玄冥，與人交語。

translations.literal: At that time a spirit descended on the Xuanwu Hall, calling itself Dark Obscurity, and conversed with people.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit possessed the Xuanwu Hall claiming to be Xuanming.

sentences.zh: 祚日夜祈之，神言與之福利，祚甚信之。

translations.literal: Zuo prayed to it day and night; the spirit spoke of blessings and profit with him, and Zuo greatly trusted it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo trusted the possessing spirit.

sentences.zh: 祚又遣張掖太守索孚代瓘鎮枹罕，為瓘所殺。

translations.literal: Zuo again sent grand administrator of Zhangye Suo Fu to replace Quan at Fuhan; Fu was killed by Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Fu died trying to replace Zhang Quan.

sentences.zh: 玲等濟河未畢，又為瓘兵所破。

translations.literal: Ling and the others had not finished crossing the river when they were again broken by Quan’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ling’s column was routed mid-river.

sentences.zh: 仍舊單騎奔走，瓘軍躡之。

translations.literal: Yi Chuai fled alone on horseback and Quan’s army followed on his heels.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Chuai fled with Zhang Quan in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 祚眾震懼。

translations.literal: Zuo’s host was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo’s men panicked.

sentences.zh: 敦煌人宋混與弟澄等聚眾以應瓘。

translations.literal: Song Hun of Dunhuang and younger brother Song Cheng and others gathered a host to answer Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Song Hun rose for Zhang Quan.

sentences.zh: 趙長、張璹等懼罪，入閣呼重華母馬氏出殿，拜耀靈庶弟玄靚為主。

translations.literal: Zhao Chang, Zhang Shu, and others, fearing punishment, entered the private apartments and called out Chonghua’s mother Lady Ma to the hall, saluting Yaoling’s younger brother by a concubine, Xuanjing, as lord.
translations.idiomatic: The coup party proclaimed Zhang Xuanjing.

sentences.zh: 揣等率眾入殿伐長，殺之。

translations.literal: Chuai and the others led a host into the hall, attacked Chang, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Chuai’s faction killed Zhao Chang in the hall.

sentences.zh: 瓘弟琚及子嵩募數百市人，揚聲言：「張祚無道，我兄大軍已到城東，敢有舉手者誅三族。

translations.literal: Quan’s younger brother Ju and son Song recruited several hundred townspeople and shouted, ‘Zhang Zuo is without the Way; my elder brother’s great army has already reached the east of the city—whoever raises a hand will have three clans executed.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju spread panic that Zhang Quan’s army was at the gates.

sentences.zh: 」祚眾披散。

translations.literal: Zuo’s host scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo’s guards melted away.

sentences.zh: 琚、嵩率眾入城，祚按劍殿上，大呼，令左右死戰。

translations.literal: Ju and Song led the host into the city; Zuo grasped his sword on the hall and shouted loudly, ordering those to left and right to fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju entered; Zhang Zuo raged on the dais.

sentences.zh: 祚既失眾心，莫有鬥志，於是被殺。

translations.literal: Zuo had already lost the host’s hearts; none had fighting will; thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: No one fought for him and he was cut down.

sentences.zh: 梟其首，宣示內外，暴屍道左，國內咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: They displayed his head, proclaimed it within and without, exposed the corpse beside the road, and all within the state cried “Ten thousand years!”
translations.idiomatic: His head hung on the wall and the capital rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 祚篡立三年而亡。

translations.literal: Zuo usurped and stood three years then perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo’s three-year reign ended in blood.

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
translations.idiomatic: Section marker.

sentences.zh: 耀靈弟玄靚

translations.literal: Younger brother of Yaoling: Xuanjing
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing, younger brother of Zhang Yaoling

sentences.zh: =玄靚字元安。

translations.literal: = Xuanjing, courtesy name Yuan’an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing, courtesy name Yuan’an.

sentences.zh: 既立，自號大都督、大將軍、校尉、涼州牧、西平公，赦其國內，廢和平之號，復稱建興四十三年。

translations.literal: Once established, he styled himself grand governor, grand general, colonel, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping, declared an amnesty within his state, abolished the Heping era name, and again called it the forty-third year of Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: He restored nominal Jin dating as Jianxing forty-three and amnestied the realm.

sentences.zh: 誅祚二子，以張瓘為衛將軍，領兵萬人，行大將軍事，改易僚屬。

translations.literal: He executed Zuo’s two sons, appointed Zhang Quan as General Who Guards the Army with ten thousand troops acting in grand general’s affairs, and changed his staff.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Zhang Zuo’s sons and put Zhang Quan in command.

sentences.zh: 有隴西人李儼，誅大姓彭姚，自立於隴右，奉中興年號，百姓悅之。

translations.literal: There was a man of Longxi, Li Yan, who executed the great clan Peng Yao, set himself up on the right of Long, used the restored court’s era name, and the common people were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan of Longxi killed magnates, declared autonomy, and used Jin’s era calendar to popular acclaim.

sentences.zh: 玄靚遣牛霸率眾討之，未達，而西平人衛綝又據郡叛。

translations.literal: Xuanjing sent Niu Ba leading a host to punish him; before he arrived, a man of Xiping, Wei Shen, also seized the commandery and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing sent Niu Ba against Li Yan, but Wei Shen rebelled in Xiping first.

sentences.zh: 霸眾潰，單騎而還。

translations.literal: Ba’s host collapsed; he returned on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Ba’s army routed and he fled alone.

sentences.zh: 瓘先欲征綝、以兄珪在綝中為疑，綝亦以弟在瓘中，故彼我經年不相伐。

translations.literal: Quan had wished to campaign against Shen but hesitated because elder brother Gui was inside Shen’s camp; Shen likewise because a younger brother was inside Quan’s camp—therefore they and we for a full year did not attack each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan and Wei Shen held each other’s kin hostage and avoided battle.

sentences.zh: 西平人郭勳解天文，不應州郡之命，綝禮聘之。

translations.literal: A man of Xiping, Guo Xun, understood astronomy and would not answer the province’s summons; Shen treated him with courtesy and hired him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shen recruited the astronomer Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 勳曰：「張氏應衰，衛氏當興，豈得以一弟而滅一門，宜速伐瓘。

translations.literal: Xun said, ‘The Zhang house is due to decline and the Wei house is due to rise—how can one younger brother destroy a whole gate! You ought quickly to attack Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun urged that the Zhangs were fading and Weis rising.

sentences.zh: 」綝將從之。

translations.literal: Shen was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shen agreed.

sentences.zh: 瓘遣弟琚領大眾征綝敗之。

translations.literal: Quan sent younger brother Ju leading a great host to campaign against Shen and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan’s brother Zhang Ju crushed Wei Shen.

sentences.zh: 西平田旋要酒泉太守馬基背瓘應綝，旋謂基曰：「綝擊其東，我等絕其西，不六旬，天下可定，斯閉口捕舌也。

translations.literal: Tian Xuan of Xiping invited grand administrator of Jiuquan Ma Ji to turn against Quan and answer Shen; Xuan said to Ji, ‘Shen strikes him in the east and we cut him in the west—in less than sixty days all under heaven can be settled; it is like closing the mouth to catch the tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xuan tried to flip Ma Ji against Zhang Quan.

sentences.zh: 」基許之。

translations.literal: Ji promised it.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ji agreed.

sentences.zh: 瓘遣司馬張姚、王國將二千人伐基，敗之，斬基、旋二人之首，傳姑臧。

translations.literal: Quan sent Major Zhang Yao and Wang Guo with two thousand men to attack Ji, defeated them, and beheaded Ji and Xuan, sending the two heads to Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan executed Ma Ji and Tian Xuan and sent their heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 瓘兄弟強盛，負其勳力，有篡立之謀。

translations.literal: The Quan brothers were strong and relied on their merit and force, harboring plans to usurp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan and his brothers grew arrogant and plotted the throne.

sentences.zh: 輔國宋混與弟澄共討瓘，盡夷其屬，玄靚以混為都督中外諸軍事、車騎大將軍、假節，輔政。

translations.literal: Song Hun who Supports the State with younger brother Song Cheng together attacked Quan, exterminated his whole faction; Xuanjing appointed Hun as area commander of all military affairs within and without, chariot-and-horse general, bearer of credentials, to assist the government.
translations.idiomatic: Song Hun destroyed the Zhang Quan faction and became regent.

sentences.zh: 混卒，又以澄代之。

translations.literal: When Hun died, Cheng replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Song Cheng succeeded his brother.

sentences.zh: 玄靚右司馬張邕惡澄專擅，殺之。

translations.literal: Xuanjing’s right major Zhang Yong hated Cheng’s monopoly and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong murdered Song Cheng.

sentences.zh: 遂滅宋氏，玄靚乃以邕為中護軍，叔父天錫為中領軍，共輔政。

translations.literal: Thereupon he exterminated the Song clan; Xuanjing then made Yong central protector and uncle Tianxi central leader of the guards, together assisting the government.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong wiped out the Songs and shared power with Zhang Tianxi.

sentences.zh: 邕自以功大，驕矜淫縱，又通馬氏，樹黨專權。

translations.literal: Yong thought his own merit great, grew arrogant and wanton, also debauched Lady Ma, built factions and monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong grew tyrannical and seized the court.

sentences.zh: 國人患之。

translations.literal: The people of the state suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: The realm hated Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 天錫腹心郭增、劉肅二人，並年十八九，因寢，謂天錫曰：「天下事欲未靜。

translations.literal: Tianxi’s confidants Guo Zeng and Liu Su, both eighteen or nineteen, because of sleeping said to Tianxi, ‘Affairs under heaven are not yet quiet.’
translations.idiomatic: Two youths warned Zhang Tianxi at night.

sentences.zh: 」天錫曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: Tianxi said, ‘What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: He asked what they meant.

sentences.zh: 」二人曰：「今護軍出入，有似長寧。

translations.literal: The two said, ‘Now the protector’s comings and goings resemble Changning’s.’
translations.idiomatic: They compared Zhang Yong to the tyrant Zhang Zuo of Changning.

sentences.zh: 」天錫大驚曰：「我早疑之，未敢出口。

translations.literal: Tianxi was greatly startled and said, ‘I long suspected it but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi admitted his fear.

sentences.zh: 計當云何？

translations.literal: What plan should there be?
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a plan.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「政當速除之耳。

translations.literal: Su said, ‘The policy ought to be to remove him quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Su urged assassination.

sentences.zh: 」天錫曰：「安得其人？

translations.literal: Tianxi said, ‘How can I obtain the right man?
translations.idiomatic: He asked who could do it.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「肅即是也。

translations.literal: Su said, ‘Su is the man.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Su volunteered.

sentences.zh: 」天錫曰：「汝年少，更求可與謀者。

translations.literal: Tianxi said, ‘You are young; seek another who can plot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi hesitated at his youth.

sentences.zh: 」肅曰：「趙白駒及肅二人足以辦之矣。

translations.literal: Su said, ‘Zhao Baiju together with Su are enough to finish it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Su named Zhao Baiju as accomplice.

sentences.zh: 」於是天錫從兵四百人，與邕俱入朝，肅與白駒剔刀鞘出刃，從天錫入。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tianxi followed four hundred soldiers and entered court with Yong; Su and Baiju drew blades from scabbards and followed Tianxi in.
translations.idiomatic: They armed four hundred guards and entered the palace.

sentences.zh: 值邕于門下，肅斫之不中，白駒繼之，又不克，二人與天錫俱入禁中。

translations.literal: They met Yong at the gate; Su struck him but did not hit; Baiju followed and again did not succeed; the two entered the forbidden quarters together with Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: The first strikes on Zhang Yong missed.

sentences.zh: 邕得逸走，因率甲士三百餘人反攻禁門。

translations.literal: Yong obtained escape and fled, then led more than three hundred armored soldiers to counterattack the forbidden gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong rallied three hundred men against the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 天錫上屋大呼，謂將士曰：「張邕凶逆，所行無道，諸宋何罪，盡誅滅之？

translations.literal: Tianxi mounted the roof and shouted loudly, saying to the generals and soldiers, ‘Zhang Yong is fierce and rebellious; his conduct is without the Way—what crime had the various Songs that they were utterly exterminated!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi harangued the troops from the roof.

sentences.zh: 傾覆國家，肆亂社稷。

translations.literal: He overturned the state and wantonly threw the altars into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: He accused Zhang Yong of ruining the state.

sentences.zh: 我不惜死，實懼先人廢祀，事不獲已故耳。

translations.literal: I do not spare death; I truly fear that the ancestors’ sacrifices would be cut off—affairs would not succeed for that reason alone.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed he acted to save the Zhang ancestral cult.

sentences.zh: 我家門戶事，而將士豈可以干戈見向！

translations.literal: It is my household’s affair—how can generals and soldiers turn weapons on me!
translations.idiomatic: He begged the army not to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 今之所取，邕身而已。

translations.literal: What is sought now is only Yong’s person.
translations.idiomatic: He swore only Zhang Yong would die.

sentences.zh: 天地有靈，吾不食言。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth have spirits—I will not break my word.’
translations.idiomatic: He swore an oath to heaven.

sentences.zh: 」邕眾聞之，悉散走，邕以劍自刎而死。

translations.literal: When Yong’s host heard this, they all scattered and fled; Yong cut his own throat with a sword and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong’s men deserted; he killed himself.

sentences.zh: 於是悉誅邕黨。

translations.literal: Thereupon they executed all of Yong’s faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi purged Zhang Yong’s clique.

sentences.zh: 玄靚年既幼沖，性又仁弱，天錫既克邕，專掌朝政，改建興四十九年，奉升平之號。

translations.literal: Xuanjing was still in childhood and by nature kind and weak; after Tianxi had overcome Yong he monopolized court government, changed the forty-ninth year of Jianxing, and adopted the Taiping era title.
translations.idiomatic: The boy ruler fell under Zhang Tianxi’s thumb; the era became Jin’s Taiping.

sentences.zh: ，駿妻馬氏卒，玄靚以其庶母郭氏為太妃。

translations.literal: (The line continues) when Jun’s wife Lady Ma died, Xuanjing made his concubine mother Lady Guo grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: After Lady Ma’s death he elevated concubine Lady Guo.

sentences.zh: 郭氏以天錫專政，與大臣張欽等謀討之。

translations.literal: Because Lady Guo saw Tianxi monopolize government, she plotted with great minister Zhang Qin and others to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo and Zhang Qin plotted against Zhang Tianxi.

sentences.zh: 事泄，欽等伏法。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Qin and the others suffered the law.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed and they were executed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，天錫率眾入禁門，潛害玄靚，宣言暴薨，時年十四。

translations.literal: That year Tianxi led a host into the forbidden gate, secretly harmed Xuanjing, declared he had died suddenly of violence; he was fourteen years of age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi murdered Zhang Xuanjing at fourteen and faked a natural death.

sentences.zh: 在位九年。

translations.literal: He had occupied the position nine years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanjing had ruled nine years.

sentences.zh: 私諡曰沖公，孝武帝賜諡曰敬悼公。

translations.literal: Privately he was titled Duke Chong; Emperor Xiaowu granted the posthumous title Reverent and Mourned.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Jingdao.

translations.literal: An equals sign appears alone in the source edition.
translations.idiomatic: Section marker.

sentences.zh: 玄靚叔天錫

translations.literal: Uncle of Xuanjing: Tianxi
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi, Zhang Xuanjing’s uncle

sentences.zh: =天錫字純嘏，駿少子也，小名獨活。

translations.literal: = Tianxi, courtesy name Chungu, was Jun’s youngest son, childhood name Duhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi, youngest son of Zhang Jun, courtesy Chungu, nicknamed Duhuo.

sentences.zh: 初字公純嘏，入朝，人笑其三字，因自改焉。

translations.literal: His first courtesy was Gongchungu; when he entered court people laughed at the three characters, so he changed it himself.
translations.idiomatic: He shortened an awkward childhood courtesy name after mockery at court.

sentences.zh: 玄靚死，國人立之，自號大將軍、校尉、涼州牧、西平公。

translations.literal: When Xuanjing died, the people of the state set him up; he styled himself grand general, colonel, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Xuanjing’s death Zhang Tianxi took the same titles.

sentences.zh: 遣司馬綸騫奉章請命，並送御史俞歸還京都。

translations.literal: He sent Major Lun Qian to present a memorial requesting mandate and also sent censor Yu Gui back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Lun Qian to Jiankang with tribute and returned Yu Gui.

sentences.zh: 太和初，詔以天錫為大將軍、大都督、督隴右關中諸軍事、護羌校尉、涼州刺史、西平公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe era an edict appointed Tianxi as grand general, grand governor, commander of all military affairs on Long and within the pass, Colonel Who Protects the Qiang, inspector of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Jin confirmed him as grand general and Liangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 天錫數宴園池，政事頗廢。

translations.literal: Tianxi repeatedly feasted in parks and pools and government affairs were rather neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi neglected rule for garden parties.

sentences.zh: 蕩難將軍、校書祭酒索商上疏極諫，天錫答曰：「吾非好行，行有得也。

translations.literal: General Who Sweeps Difficulties and Libationer for Collating Documents Suo Shang submitted a blunt memorial; Tianxi answered, ‘I am not fond of going out—there is gain in going out.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Shang remonstrated; Zhang Tianxi offered a sophistical reply about nature walks.

sentences.zh: 觀朝榮，則敬才秀之士；

translations.literal: When I observe morning splendor I then respect talented gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: He claimed flowers taught him to honor talent;

sentences.zh: 玩芝蘭，則愛德行之臣；

translations.literal: when I play with irises and orchids I then love ministers of virtue;
translations.idiomatic: orchids taught love of virtue;

sentences.zh: 睹松竹，則思貞操之賢；

translations.literal: when I gaze on pines and bamboo I then think of worthies who keep chaste integrity;
translations.idiomatic: pines suggested integrity;

sentences.zh: 臨清流，則貴廉潔之行；

translations.literal: when I face clear currents I then prize conduct of integrity;
translations.idiomatic: streams suggested honesty;

sentences.zh: 覽蔓草，則賤貪穢之吏；

translations.literal: when I view tangled creepers I then despise greedy and filthy clerks;
translations.idiomatic: weeds meant corrupt officials;

sentences.zh: 逢飆風，則惡凶狡之徒。

translations.literal: when I meet whirlwinds I then hate fierce and crafty fellows.
translations.idiomatic: gales meant villains.

sentences.zh: 若引而申之，觸類而長之，庶無遺漏矣。」

translations.literal: If I draw this out and extend it by categories, perhaps nothing will be left out.’
translations.idiomatic: He claimed moral lessons from every stroll.”

sentences.zh: 羌廉岐自稱益州刺史，率略陽四千家背苻堅就李儼。

translations.literal: The Qiang Lian Qi styled himself inspector of Yizhou and led four thousand households of Lüeyang to leave Fu Jian and join Li Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Qi took four thousand households from Fu Jian to Li Yan.

sentences.zh: 天錫自往討之，以別駕楊遹為監前鋒軍事、前將軍，趣金城。

translations.literal: Tianxi went in person to punish him, making chief clerk Yang You supervisor of the vanguard army and forward general, hurrying to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi marched with Yang You toward Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 晉興相常據為使持節、征東將軍，向左南，遊擊將軍張統出白土，天錫自率三萬人次倉松，伐儼。

translations.literal: Chancellor of Jinxing Chang Ju was made bearer of credentials and general who conquers the east toward Zuo south; roaming general Zhang Tong issued from White Earth; Tianxi himself followed thirty thousand men and halted at Cangsong to attack Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He coordinated columns against Li Yan.

sentences.zh: 儼大敗，入城固守，遣子純求救於苻堅。

translations.literal: Yan was greatly defeated, entered the city and held firm fast, and sent his son Chun to beg rescue from Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan lost and begged Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅使其將王猛救之。

translations.literal: Jian sent his general Wang Meng to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 天錫敗績，死者十二三，天錫乃還。

translations.literal: Tianxi was routed; twelve or thirteen in ten of the dead; Tianxi then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi lost twelve or thirteen men in ten and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 立子大懷為世子。

translations.literal: He established his son Dahuai as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He named Zhang Dahuai heir.

sentences.zh: 自天錫之嗣事也，連年地震山崩，水泉湧出，柳化為松，火生泥中。

translations.literal: From the time Tianxi succeeded, in successive years there were earthquakes and mountain collapses, springs gushed water, willows turned into pines, and fire sprang within mud.
translations.idiomatic: Nature threw omens at Liangzhou yearly.

sentences.zh: 而天錫荒於聲色，不恤政事。

translations.literal: Yet Tianxi was dissolute in music and women and did not pity government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi ignored government for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 初，安定梁景、敦煌劉肅並以門胄，總角與天錫友昵。

translations.literal: In the beginning Liang Jing of Anding and Liu Su of Dunhuang, both by noble houses, from childhood were friendly with Tianxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jing and Liu Su had been his childhood friends.

sentences.zh: 張邕之誅，肅、景有勳，天錫深德之賜姓張氏，又改其字，以為己子。

translations.literal: At Zhang Yong’s execution Su and Jing had merit; Tianxi deeply favored them, gave them the surname Zhang, and changed their courtesy names, treating them as his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: He adopted them as Zhang clan sons for killing Zhang Yong.

sentences.zh: 天錫諸子皆以大為字，故景曰大奕，肅曰大誠。

translations.literal: Tianxi’s sons all took Da- as their courtesy prefix; therefore Jing was called Dayi and Su was called Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: They became Zhang Dayi and Zhang Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 廢大懷為高昌公，更立嬖子大豫為世子，景、肅等俱參政事。

translations.literal: He deposed Dahuai as Duke of Gaochang, changed to establish beloved son Dayu as heir apparent; Jing, Su, and others all joined in government.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced his heir with a favorite son and empowered the adoptees.

sentences.zh: 人情怨懼，從弟從事中郎憲切諫，不納。

translations.literal: Human feeling resented and feared; cousin aide-de-camp Xian remonstrated sharply and was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsmen warned him in vain.

sentences.zh: 時苻堅強盛，每攻之，兵無寧歲。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Jian was strong and repeatedly attacked; the army knew no year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin hammered the border every year.

sentences.zh: 天賜甚懼，乃立壇刑牲，率典軍將軍張甯、中堅將軍馬芮等，遙與晉三公盟誓，獻書大司馬桓溫，克六年夏誓同大舉。

translations.literal: Tianxi (text writes 天賜) was very afraid; thereupon he raised an altar and slaughtered victims, led Generals Who Manage the Army Zhang Ning and Ma Rui of the central rampart, swore alliance at a distance with the three dukes of Jin, and sent a letter to Grand Marshal Huan Wen, pledging a joint great campaign in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi allied formally with Jin and Huan Wen against Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 遣從事中郎韓博、奮節將軍康妙奉表，並送盟文。

translations.literal: He sent aide-de-camp Han Bo and General Who Displays Resolve Kang Miao to present a memorial together with the covenant text.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Han Bo to Jiankang with the alliance document.

sentences.zh: 博有口才，溫甚稱之。

translations.literal: Bo had eloquence; Wen greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen admired Han Bo’s wit.

sentences.zh: 嘗大會，溫使司馬刁彝嘲之，彝謂博曰：「君是韓盧後邪？

translations.literal: At a great gathering Wen had Major Diao Yi mock him; Yi said to Bo, ‘Are you descended from the Han hound?
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yi insulted Han Bo as a dog’s offspring.

sentences.zh: 」博曰：「卿是韓盧後。

translations.literal: Bo said, ‘You are descended from the Han hound.
translations.idiomatic: Han Bo turned the insult on Diao’s name.

sentences.zh: 」溫笑曰：「刁以君姓韓，故相問焉。

translations.literal: Wen laughed and said, ‘Diao, because your surname is Han, therefore asked;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen tried to smooth it over;

sentences.zh: 他自姓刁，那得韓盧後邪！

translations.literal: he himself is surnamed Diao—how could he be a Han hound’s descendant!
translations.idiomatic: Diao was not surnamed Han;

sentences.zh: 」博曰：「明公脫未之思，短尾者則為刁也。

translations.literal: Bo said, ‘My lord has not thought it through—short tail means Diao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Bo called Diao Yi “short tail,” a dog joke.

sentences.zh: 」一坐推歎焉。

translations.literal: The whole sitting pushed praise for him.
translations.idiomatic: The hall roared approval.

sentences.zh: 太元元年，苻堅遣其將苟萇、毛當、梁熙、姚萇來寇，渡石城津。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyuan, Fu Jian sent his generals Gou Chang, Mao Dang, Liang Xi, and Yao Chang to invade, crossing the Shicheng ford.
translations.idiomatic: In 376 Fu Jian sent Gou Chang, Mao Dang, Liang Xi, and Yao Chang across the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 天錫集議，中錄事席仂曰：「先公既有故事，徐思後變，此孫仲謀屈伸之略也。

translations.literal: Tianxi gathered counsel; chief recorder Xi Le said, ‘The former lord already had precedent—ponder later change; this is Sun Quan’s strategy of bending and stretching.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Le urged delay like Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 」眾以仂為老怯，咸曰：「龍驤將軍馬達，精兵萬人距之，必不敢進。

translations.literal: The multitude thought Le old and timid and all said, ‘General of Dragon Soaring Ma Da with ten thousand crack troops will oppose them—they will surely not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The court mocked Xi Le and trusted Ma Da.

sentences.zh: 」廣武太守辛章保城固守。

translations.literal: Grand administrator of Guangwu Xin Zhang defended the city and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Zhang held Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 章與晉興相彭知正、西平相趙疑謀曰：「馬達出於行陣，必不為用，則秦軍深入。

translations.literal: Zhang with chancellor of Jinxing Peng Zhizheng and chancellor of Xiping Zhao Yi plotted, saying, ‘Ma Da comes from the ranks and will surely not be useful—then Qin troops will penetrate deep.
translations.idiomatic: Local governors doubted Ma Da’s ability;

sentences.zh: 吾相與率三郡精卒，斷其糧運，決一朝命矣。

translations.literal: We together will lead crack troops of three commanderies, cut their grain transport, and settle fate in one morning.’
translations.idiomatic: they planned to cut Former Qin’s supply lines.

sentences.zh: 」征東常據亦欲先擊姚萇，須天錫命。

translations.literal: General who conquers the east Chang Ju also wished first to strike Yao Chang, awaiting Tianxi’s order.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ju wanted to hit Yao Chang first.

sentences.zh: 天錫率萬人頓金昌城。

translations.literal: Tianxi led ten thousand men and halted at Jinchang city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi camped at Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 馬達萬人逆萇等，因請降，兵人散走。

translations.literal: Ma Da’s ten thousand met Chang and the others, then asked to surrender; soldiers scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Da surrendered to Former Qin at once.

sentences.zh: 常據、席仂皆戰死。

translations.literal: Chang Ju and Xi Le both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Ju and Xi Le fell.

sentences.zh: 司兵趙充哲與萇苦戰，又死。

translations.literal: Army officer Zhao Chongzhe fought bitterly against Chang and again died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chongzhe died fighting Gou Chang.

sentences.zh: 中衛將軍史景亦沒於陣。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the Center Shi Jing also perished in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jing died in the rout.

sentences.zh: 天錫大懼，出城自戰，城內又反。

translations.literal: Tianxi was greatly afraid, went out of the city to fight in person, and within the city there was again revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi sallied as his capital mutinied.

sentences.zh: 天錫窘逼，降於萇等。

translations.literal: Tianxi was hard pressed and surrendered to Chang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered to Gou Chang.

sentences.zh: 初，天錫所居安昌門及平章殿無故而崩，旬日而國亡。

translations.literal: In the beginning Tianxi’s Anchang Gate and Pingzhang Hall for no reason collapsed; within ten days the state was lost.
translations.idiomatic: His gates and hall had collapsed before the fall—an omen of doom.

sentences.zh: 即位凡十三年。

translations.literal: In all he occupied the throne thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi had ruled Former Liang thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 自軌為涼州，至天錫，凡九世，七十六年矣。

translations.literal: From the time Gui became inspector of Liang down to Tianxi, in all there were nine generations and seventy-six years.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhang Gui to Zhang Tianxi the house held the west nine generations over seventy-six years.

sentences.zh: 苻堅先為天錫起宅，至，以為尚書，封歸義侯。

translations.literal: Fu Jian had first built a house for Tianxi; when he arrived he made him Minister of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian housed him in Chang’an and made him a minister and marquis of submission.

sentences.zh: 堅大敗于淮肥時，天錫為苻融征南司馬，於陣歸國。

translations.literal: When Jian was greatly defeated at the Fei River, Tianxi was southern expedition major for Fu Rong’s staff and returned to Jin amid the battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fei River disaster Zhang Tianxi slipped back to Jin from Fu Rong’s army.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔孟明不替，終顯厥功，豈以一眚而廢才用！

translations.literal: An edict said, ‘In olden times Meng Ming was not replaced and in the end displayed his merit—how can one fault dismiss talent!
translations.idiomatic: Jin cited Meng Ming: one defeat must not ruin a good man.

sentences.zh: 其以天錫為散騎常侍、左員外。

translations.literal: Let Tianxi be appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and supernumerary left gentleman consultant.’
translations.idiomatic: They named him cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「故太尉、西平公張軌著德遐域，世襲前勞。

translations.literal: Another edict said, ‘The late grand commandant, Duke of Xiping Zhang Gui, displayed virtue in a distant region and generation after generation inherited earlier toil;
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Zhang Gui’s legacy;

sentences.zh: 強兵縱害，遂至失守。

translations.literal: strong soldiers ran wild with harm, and thus led to loss of the command.
translations.idiomatic: warlords had cost them the province;

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍天錫拔跡登朝，先祀淪替，用增矜慨，可復天錫西平郡公爵。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Tianxi has pulled himself up to enter the court; earlier sacrifices have sunk and been replaced—increase pity and grief; Tianxi may be restored as duke of Xiping commandery.’
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi was restored as duke of Xiping for his suffering.

sentences.zh: 」俄拜金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed grand master with golden purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took golden-purple grand master honors.

sentences.zh: 天錫少有文才，流譽遠近。

translations.literal: Tianxi in youth had literary talent and his fame flowed far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi had been a famed young writer.

sentences.zh: 及歸朝，甚被恩遇。

translations.literal: When he returned to the court he was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Jin treated him kindly at first.

sentences.zh: 朝士以其國破身虜，多共毀之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen because his state was broken and he himself a captive mostly together slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang snobs sneered at the fallen prince.

sentences.zh: 會稽王道子嘗問其西土所出，天錫應聲曰：「桑葚甜甘，鴟鴞革響，乳酪養性，人無妒心。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi, once asked him what products the western soil produced; Tianxi answered on the spur of the moment, ‘Mulberries are sweet, owls and shrikes change their cries, dairy nourishes nature, and the people have no jealous hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi asked for a western travelogue; Zhang Tianxi answered with a whimsical rhyme.

sentences.zh: 」後形神昏喪，雖處列位，不復被齒遇。

translations.literal: Afterward his form and spirit grew dim and ruined; although he occupied a rank he no longer received tooth-count favor.
translations.idiomatic: He faded mentally and lost standing at court.

sentences.zh: 隆安中，會稽世子元顯用事，常延致之，以為戲弄。

translations.literal: In the Longan era the heir of Kuaiji, Yuanxian, held power and often summoned him to treat him as sport.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yuanxian mocked him at parties.

sentences.zh: 以其家貧，拜廬江太守，本官如故。

translations.literal: Because his household was poor, he was appointed grand administrator of Lujiang while his original posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was given Lujiang to earn a salary.

sentences.zh: 桓玄時，欲招懷四遠，乃用天錫為護羌校尉、涼州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Huan Xuan, wishing to win over the four quarters, he then employed Tianxi as Colonel Who Protects the Qiang and inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan briefly restored his old Liangzhou titles for show.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: Soon he died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 追贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Posthumous gifts made him grand master with golden purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously awarded golden-purple grand master.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians’ appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Section: historians’ appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：長河外區，流沙作紀，玉關懸險，金城負固，有苗攸竄，帝舜投而不羈；

translations.literal: The historians say: Beyond the long river lies an outer region; drifting sands mark its bounds; the Jade Pass hangs perilous; Metal City leans on strength—where the Miao fled, Emperor Shun drove them yet could not bind them;
translations.idiomatic: They paint the Hexi corridor’s harsh geography and ancient tribes;

sentences.zh: 渠搜是居，大禹即而方敘。

translations.literal: the Qu sou dwell there, and Great Yu approached and then set them in order.
translations.idiomatic: Yu the Great ordered the western wastes.

sentences.zh: 世逢多難，嬰五郡以誰何；

translations.literal: Meeting many hard generations, they girded five commanderies and defied all comers;
translations.idiomatic: Through generations of crisis they armed five commanderies and dared any challenger to intervene.

sentences.zh: 時遇兵凶，阻三邊而高視。

translations.literal: Encountering seasons of weapons and slaughter, they blocked three frontiers and gazed from on high.
translations.idiomatic: They barred three frontiers in an age of war and held a commanding gaze.

sentences.zh: 雖非久安之地，足為苟全之所乎！

translations.literal: Though it was no land of long peace, was it not enough for a place to preserve life awhile!
translations.idiomatic: Hexi was no paradise but a refuge.

sentences.zh: 周公保之而立功，士彥擁之布延世。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou guarded it and achieved merit; Shiyan upheld it and prolonged the generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou’s model and Zhang Shiyan’s grit extended the line.

sentences.zh: 摯虞觀象，記洪災之不流；

translations.literal: Zhi Yu watched the stars and recorded that the great flood’s waters did not reach;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu’s omen said Chang’an’s flood would spare Liangzhou;

sentences.zh: 侯瑾覘泉，知霸者之斯在。

translations.literal: Hou Jin peered at the spring and knew a hegemon would be there.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jin’s spring prophecy foretold Zhang power.

sentences.zh: 匪唯地勢，抑亦有天道歙！

translations.literal: Not only terrain—was there not also Heaven’s way!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven as well as earth favored the west.

sentences.zh: 茂、駿、重華資忠踵武，崎嶇僻陋，無忘本朝，故能西控諸戎，東攘巨猾，綰累葉之珪組，賦絕域之琛賨，振曜遐荒，良由杖順之效矣。

translations.literal: Mao, Jun, and Chonghua relied on loyalty and followed in martial footsteps; on cragged remote ground they did not forget the capital court; therefore they could control the various Rong to the west, brush aside great villains to the east, thread generation after generation of jade seals and silken cords, and levy treasure from the farthest lands—shaking brilliance across the wastes—truly the effect of wielding the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: The good early Zhangs held Jin’s mandate in the wilds and prospered.

sentences.zh: 祚以卑孽，陰傾塚嗣，播有茨于彤管，擬宸居於黑山，丁琪以切諫遇誅夷，王鸞以讜言嬰顯戮，境內雲據，仇其竊名，卒致梟懸，自然之理也。

translations.literal: Zuo, base-born, secretly overturned the heir, spread “tares on the wall” in the crimson tube, modeled the imperial seat on Black Mountain—Ding Qi met execution for blunt remonstrance, Wang Luan suffered clear execution for candid words—cloudlike factions within the borders hated his stolen name, until at last his head hung displayed—principle of nature.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zuo’s incest and usurpation brought a natural fall.

sentences.zh: 純嘏微弱，竟亡其眾。

translations.literal: Chungu being feeble, in the end he lost his hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi’s weakness lost the army and state.

sentences.zh: 奉身魏闕，齒跡朝流，再襲銀黃，祖德之延慶矣。

translations.literal: Offering himself to the Weique, treading in the tracks of court currents, twice donning silver and gold—extension of ancestral virtue’s blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi ended his days a Jin official, still honored as Zhang Gui’s heir.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：三象構氛，九土瓜分。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Three luminaries built miasma; the nine provinces were carved like a melon.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy opens on cosmic chaos and partition.

sentences.zh: 鼎遷江介，地絕河濆。

translations.literal: The cauldron moved to the Yangzi’s margin; land was cut off at the river’s bank.
translations.idiomatic: Jin ruled south of the river while the north split;

sentences.zh: 歸誠晉室，美矣張君。

translations.literal: turning in sincerity to the house of Jin—how fine, Lord Zhang!
translations.idiomatic: the Zhangs served Jin faithfully;

sentences.zh: 內撫遺黎，外攘逋寇。

translations.literal: within they soothed the surviving commoners, without they brushed aside fleeing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: they sheltered people and fought invaders;

sentences.zh: 世既綿遠，國亦完富。

translations.literal: generations stretched far and the state was also whole and rich.
translations.idiomatic: their realm endured and grew rich;

sentences.zh: 杖順為基，蓋天所佑。

translations.literal: taking the righteous cause as foundation—surely Heaven’s aid.
translations.idiomatic: righteousness drew Heaven’s help.
